The little word "each one" is not to be referred to all who were in the church of the Corinthians, but only to those who, being schismatics, were tearing apart the communion of the church. For the remaining multitude, which those men despised, is not touched by this rebuke. Let the reader consider how far from this apostolic reasoning are those who think the sacred Mass is more efficacious and useful for themselves in the sight of the Lord if they have procured a private one for money, than if they are only partakers of the public one, since every good is the more divine the more it is common. But the deceived common people ought to be led by this foolish opinion into priestly trade and profit. The invention of the Papist priesthood has brought into the churches corruptions of every kind, and this is one of them: the little priest sells and applies his priestly office privately to any buyer for a fixed sum of money, and persuades the wretched man that it is an incomparable good to have a Mass celebrated for himself alone; whereas by this profanation of the Lord's supper the divine majesty is provoked far more than it is appeased.

units.la: ET hic quidem esurit, inquit, ille vero ebrius est.) Poterat multo graviora objicere, quibus per dominicae coenae prophanationem in Deum peccabant, verum in praesenti contentus est exprobratione inaequalitatis, qua fiebat, ut esurientibus egenis schismatici & opulenti inebriarentur.
units.tr: "And one indeed is hungry, the other is drunk." He could have objected to much graver things by which they sinned against God through the profanation of the Lord's supper; but for the present he is content to rebuke the inequality by which it came about that the needy went hungry while the schismatics and the rich were drunk.

units.la: Hieronymus sic annotat: Quicunq; non obtulisset, non communicabat, quia omnia soli qui obtulerant, insumebant. Haec autem inaequalitas bonorum omnium iudicio vehementer est detestabilis, etiamsi in prophanis conuiuijs, nedum in ipsa coena dominica admittatur. Poterat dicere: Et hic quidem minus, ille vero plus edit & bibit, verum ut iniquitatem schismaticorum grauius exprimat, maluit pleno ore dicere. Et hic quidem esurit, ille vero ebrius est. Magna omnino peruersitas. Coena Christiano rum non ingurgitationis & inebriationis erat, sed disciplinae Christianae, non propter opulentos inebriandos, sed propter inopes refocillandos instituta. Vnde & Tertullianus de illa scribens dicit: Coena nostra de nomine rationem suam offendit. Vocatur ἀγάπη, id quod dilectio est penes Graecos. Quantiscunq; summptibus constet, lucrum est pietatis nomine facere sumptum. Siquidem inopes quosq; refrigerio isto iuuamus. Hęcille. Quod indecorum ac deforme erat in coena dominica apud Corinthios, id hodie quoq; in ecclesijs obtinet, in quibus Missa, quam vocant, inebriat sacrificulos, & interim inopes nullo refrigerio reficit, sed ut esurientes veniunt, ita & esurientes dimittit. Praeterquam enim quod in sacro oblata ad se rapiunt sacrificuli, peracto etiam sacro laute accipiuntur, & non sine graui sumptu saginatur, sicuti cernere est in exequijs funeralibus, septimis, tricesimis, & anniuersarijs, pauperum vero nulla interea habetur ratio. Quare quod in Corinthijs reprehendit Apostolus dicens: Et hic quidem esurit, ille vero ebrius est, hic quoq; locum habet. Et vtinam nihil tale de nostris posset ecclesijs dici, in quibus, etsi non in templis, extra tamen qui opulenti sunt inebriantur, & in delicijs sumptuosissime volutantur, pauperes vero esuriunt, imo Christus ipse in illis & alget, & esurit, & exulat, &c.
units.tr: Jerome comments thus: "Whoever did not offer did not partake, because all things were consumed only by those who had offered." This inequality is, by the judgment of all good people, vehemently detestable, even if it were admitted at profane banquets, let alone at the Lord's supper itself. He could have said, "This one eats and drinks less, that one more," but to express the iniquity of the schismatics more gravely, he preferred to say with full mouth: "one indeed is hungry, the other is drunk." Truly a great perversity. The supper of Christians was not for gorging and drunkenness, but was instituted as a Christian discipline, not to make the rich drunk but to refresh the needy. Whence Tertullian too, writing of it, says: "Our supper takes its reason from its name. It is called agape, which among the Greeks means love. Whatever it costs, the outlay is gain under the name of piety, since by this refreshment we help the needy." So far he. What was unseemly and deformed in the Lord's supper among the Corinthians still prevails today in churches, where the Mass, as they call it, makes the little priests drunk, and meanwhile refreshes the poor with nothing; as they come hungry, so it sends them away hungry. For besides the little priests snatching the offerings made in the sacred rite to themselves, after the rite is over they are entertained lavishly and fattened at no small cost, as can be seen at funeral rites, seventh-day and thirtieth-day commemorations, and anniversaries, while meanwhile no account is taken of the poor. Therefore what the Apostle rebukes in the Corinthians, saying "one indeed is hungry, the other is drunk," has a place here too. And would that nothing of the sort could be said of our churches, in which, if not in the temples, then outside them the rich are drunk and wallow most sumptuously in luxuries, while the poor go hungry; indeed Christ himself in them is cold, and hungry, and an exile, etc.

units.la: AN domos, inquit, non habetis ad edendum & bibendum? Quasi dicat: Si nihil aliud quaeri tis in coena dominica, quam vt edatis & bibatis, potestis hoc domi vestrae facere, priusquam in coetum sacrum ueniatis, sicut & infradicit: Si quis esurit, domi edat. Non damnat morem ecclesiae, quo vna in Synaxi sacra edebant & bibebant, communiter omnes, qua de re iam ex Tertulliano paucula citauimus, sed eos reprehendit, qui proprias coenas in coetu sacro praesumebant, & esurientibus egenis ipsi inebriabantur.
units.tr: "Have you not houses to eat and drink in?" It is as if he said: if you seek nothing else in the Lord's Supper than to eat and drink, you can do that at home before you come to the sacred assembly, as he also says below: "If anyone is hungry, let him eat at home." He does not condemn the custom of the church by which all together ate and drank in the sacred Synaxis, as we have already cited a little from Tertullian on this matter. He rebukes those who presumed to hold their own private dinners in the sacred assembly, while the needy went hungry and they themselves got drunk.

units.la: Discernit quidem inter coenas domesticas & eam quae dominica vocatur, interq; domos priuatas & conuentum ecclesiasticum, & vindicat coenae dominicae & coetui sacro suum de corum, verum iuxta non tollit morem communis mensae, qua simul edebant ac bibebant omnes. Quare quod dicit: An domos non habetis ad edendum & bibendum? non est alio rapiendum, quam contra carnales illos qui nihil aliud quaerebant in coena dominica, quam vt ventri edendo & bibendo cofuleret, quod non erat dicturus, si ad erigendam fidem suam, & alendam charitatem mutuam, inopesque reficiendos vnà comedissent ac bibissent omnes. Morem ethnicum inducebant in ecclesiam, quo perinde atq; antea in sacrificijs idolorum priuatis coenis sese ingurgitauerant, ita & in coena dominica faciebant. Eum abusum damnat & reijcit ex ecclesia.
units.tr: He does distinguish between domestic meals and the meal called the Lord's, and between private houses and the ecclesiastical gathering, and he assigns to the Lord's Supper and the sacred assembly their own proper place. Yet he does not for all that remove the custom of the common table, at which all ate and drank together. So the words "Have you not houses to eat and drink in?" must not be taken in any other sense than as directed against those carnal people who sought nothing in the Lord's Supper but to indulge the belly by eating and drinking. He would not have said this if they had all eaten and drunk together, to raise up their faith, to nourish mutual love and to refresh the poor. They were bringing a heathen custom into the church: just as before, in the sacrifices to idols, they had gorged themselves at private banquets, so they did in the Lord's Supper too. He condemns that abuse and casts it out of the church.

units.la: Aut ecclesiam Dei contemnitis, inquit, & pudefacitis eos qui non habent? Ecclesiam vocat conuentum fidelium. Ad hunc pertinent non modo diuites, sed & pauperes. Quoniam pudefaciebant eos qui nihil habebant quod adferrent in ecclesiam, dicit eos ecclesiam dei contemnere, in quam pauperum contemptus redundabat. Sic vtitur interpretatione satis in loco, dum contemptum egenorum interpretatur contemptum ecclesiae. Nec ociosum est, quod non simpliciter dicit: Ecclesiam Dei contemnitis, & pudefacitis eos qui non habent, sed per contadio & instando: An ecclesiam Dei contemnitis? & pudefacitis eos qui non habent? Quasi dicat: Estisne adeo carnales & irreligiosi, vt ne ecclesiae quidem Dei reuerētia cohibeamini? Estisne adeo inhumani, vt fratres egenos à cibo ac potu exclusos pudefaceres possitis? Sic exaggerat irreligiosam illorum superbiam & impudentem ingluuiem.
units.tr: "Or do you despise the church of God, and shame those who have nothing?" By "the church" he means the assembly of the faithful. To this belong not only the rich but also the poor. Because they shamed those who had nothing to bring into the church, he says that they despise the church of God, into which the contempt of the poor flowed back. In this way he uses an interpretation that suits the place well, explaining the contempt of the needy as contempt of the church. Nor is it idle that he does not simply say, "You despise the church of God and shame those who have nothing," but puts it as a question with emphasis: "Do you despise the church of God? And do you shame those who have nothing?" It is as if he said: Are you so carnal and irreligious that not even reverence for the church of God restrains you? Are you so inhuman that you can shame needy brothers, shut out from food and drink? In this way he magnifies their irreligious pride and shameless gluttony.

units.la: An ecclesiam Dei contemnitis, inquit? Sanè quod non expectabant alios, sed proprias coenas praecipiebant, certam habebat contemptus ecclesiae notam. Neq; enim hoc fecissent, nisi multitudinem tenuiorum in ecclesia contemnisfent. Vnde colligitur reprehendi hic non inferiores,sed eos qui quod potiores esse videbantur cæteros præ se tastidiebant. Est ergo malum hoc antiquum, quod à potioribus ecclesia contemnitur in inferioribus, à doctis in idiotis & indoctis,à diuitibus in pauperib à valentioribus in infirmis,hoc est, in illis ipsis quorum rationem potissimam habet domin9. Atq; ita fit,vt tubera in corpore ecclesiæ vera illius membra contemnant.
units.tr: "Do you despise the church of God?" Clearly, because they did not wait for others but made their own dinners in advance, their conduct bore the clear mark of contempt for the church. They would not have done this unless they despised the lesser folk in the church. From this it is gathered that the ones rebuked here are not the inferior people, but those who, because they seemed to be the more important, looked down on the rest. This is therefore an ancient evil: the church is despised by the more important in the less important, by the learned in the simple and unlearned, by the rich in the poor, by the strong in the weak, that is, in those very people whose cause the Lord especially takes up. And so it happens that the swellings in the body of the church despise its true members.

units.la: ET pudefacitiseos,inquit,qui nó habent.) Obserua.Nó dicit,Et esurire sinitis, sed:Et pu defacitis eos qui non habent.Plus est pudesie ri,quàm esuriem pati.Speraba pauper, ingref surum se conuentum fratrum , in quo nihil sit discriminis inter diuitem & pauperem, inter adferentem cibaria,& non adferentem,sed fra terna omnium communicatio. Verùm vbi vi debat excludi se à communicatione mense,ac contemni,propterea quod nihil attulisset,pu dore suffundebatur.An non hodie quoq; inec clesia pudefiunt pauperes, dum se contemni, diuites verò in precio haberi cernunt?
units.tr: "And you shame those who have nothing," he says. Observe that he does not say, "You allow them to go hungry," but, "You shame those who have nothing." Being shamed is worse than suffering hunger. The poor man hoped to enter an assembly of brothers in which there was no distinction between rich and poor, between the one who brought food and the one who did not, but a common fellowship of all. But when he saw himself shut out from the communion of the table and despised, because he had brought nothing, he was overwhelmed with shame. Do not the poor today also feel shame in the church, when they see themselves despised while the rich are held in esteem?

units.la: Notus est locus Iacob.cap.2.Si introierit, in quit,in conuentum vestrum , vir aureum ha bens anulum,& vestem candidam, introierit autem & pauper in sordido vestitu, & intenda tis in eũ,qui indutus est veste præclara,&dixe ritis ei,Tu sede hic bene,pauperi autem dica tis, tu sta illic,aut sede sub scabello pedum me orum,&c.paulo post:Nónne Deus elegit pau peres in mundo,diuites in fide,& hæredes re gni:vos verò dehonestastis pauperem.
units.tr: The passage of James 2 is well known: "If a man with a gold ring and fine clothing comes into your assembly, and a poor man also comes in shabby clothing, and you look upon him who wears the fine clothing and say to him, 'Sit here in a good place,' but to the poor man you say, 'Stand there,' or 'Sit under the footstool of my feet,' etc." A little later: "Has not God chosen the poor of this world, rich in faith and heirs of the kingdom? But you have dishonoured the poor man."

units.la: Et hoc quoq; obserua,quod non dicit : Et pudefacitis eos qui nihil adferunt, sed, Et pu- defacitis eos qui non habent . Aliud est nihil adferre in refrigerium egenorumcum habeas, & aliud nó habere quod adferas . Prius dignũ est pudore,postèrius verò non pudore, sed mi sericordia.At Romæ pudor est grandis habe- re nihil.
units.tr: Observe also that he does not say, "You shame those who bring nothing to relieve the needy," but, "You shame those who have nothing." It is one thing to bring nothing to refresh the needy, when you have something, and another thing not to have anything you could bring. The first deserves shame; the second deserves not shame but pity. Yet at Rome it is a great disgrace to have nothing.

units.la: QVID vobis dicâ?inquit.Laudabo uos?In hoc non laudo.)Postquamabusus illorum re prehendit,subiungitdicens:Quid uobis dicâ? Quasi dicat:Iam uosipsi iudicate, quid adhæc mihi sit dicédum.Sùntne hæc in uobis laudâ da?Licet,laudem uos in eo quod statuta mea tenetis,in hoc tamê non laudo,quod ecclesiâ Dei scinditis & contemnitis, proprias cœnas præsumitis,ac pauperes qui sunt inter uos pu defacitis.Obserua discretionem Apostolo di- gnam,quam utinam seruarêt hodie, qui mox in uniuersum damnât,si uno tantum apiculo ab ipsis dissentias.Non laudat Apost.q nô lau danda sunt,sed reprehendenda.Rursus nô dâ nat in uniuersum omnia eorû, qui in nonnullis delinquebant,sed quæ bona in illis deprehê debat,candidè laudat.Sic non dicit hic simpli citer,non laudo uos,sedcum specificatione,in hoc,inquit,non laudo.Candidi ac iusti homi nis est,laudare laudanda,& reprehendere re prehendenda. Nimis morbidi sunt, qui tan-
units.tr: "What shall I say to you?" he says. Shall I praise you? In this I do not praise you. After he has rebuked their abuse, he adds, saying, "What shall I say to you?" As if he said: "Now judge for yourselves what I ought to say to you in response. Are these things worthy of praise among you? You may be praised for keeping my ordinances, but in this I do not praise you, because you divide and despise the Church of God, presume to hold your own private suppers, and shame the poor who are among you." Observe the discernment worthy of the Apostle, which would that those today would keep, who at once condemn everything in a whole body if they differ from them even by a hair's breadth. The Apostle does not praise what is not to be praised but rebukes it. Again, he does not condemn wholesale everything done by those who were erring in some matters, but frankly praises whatever good he found in them. So here he does not say simply, "I do not praise you," but with a qualification: "In this," he says, "I do not praise you." It belongs to a sincere and just man to praise what is praiseworthy and to rebuke what is blameworthy. Those are far too diseased who so indulge their own feelings that, if you agree with them in the opinion for which they fight, they are blind to all the rest, but if you disagree, they condemn everything at once, even those things they cannot rightly find fault with. And this disease must reign wherever zeal for factions and schisms prevails in the Church.

units.la: tum permittunt affectibus suis, vt si in opinio ne pro qua pugnant consentias,ad omnia reli qua sunt cæci, contrà, si dissentias , omnia si mul damnant,etiá ea, quæ reprehendere non possunt.Et hunc morbum regnare necesse est, vbi obtinent in ecclesia studia & schismata.
units.tr: so that you agree with them on whatever opinion they fight for, they are blind to everything else; on the other hand, if you dissent, they condemn everything at once, even those things they cannot find fault with. And this disease must necessarily reign where factions and schisms hold sway in the Church.

units.la: Ego enim accepi à domino, quod& tradidi uobis,quod dominus Iesus in ea nocte qua traditus est,accepit panê, & cum gratias egisset,fregit ac dixit,acci pite,edite,hoc meũ est corpus quod ,p uobis frangitur,hoc facite in mei reme morationem.Ad eũdem modum & po culum,peracta cœna dicens: hoc pocu lũ Nouum testamentum est in meo san guine,hoc facite quotiescunq; biberi tis in mei rememorationê. Quotiescun que enim ederitis panem hunc,&de po culo hoc biberitis, mortê domini annũ ciatis donec uenerit.
units.tr: For I received of the Lord that which I also delivered to you: that the Lord Jesus, the same night in which he was betrayed, took bread, and when he had given thanks, he broke it and said: "Take, eat; this is my body, which is broken for you; do this in remembrance of me." In the same way also the cup, after supper, saying: "This cup is the New Testament in my blood; do this, as often as you drink it, in remembrance of me." For as often as you eat this bread and drink this cup, you proclaim the Lord's death until he comes. [1 Cor. 11.23-26]

units.la: Reprehédithactenus in Corinthijs schisma ticis,quod dum conuenirent ineundem cœtũ ecclesiam scindebát,priuatas suas ac proprias cœnas,nő expectata fideliũ multitudine præ- sumebant,ecclesiam Dei contênebant,& pau peres qui in illa erant,pudefaciebant, & bisc de causis dixit eos non edere cœnam domini, nec laudare se talia facientes,iam vt ostendat, quàm sint hæc aliena ab instituto cœnæ do minicæ,& remota ab eo quod ipse illis tradi derat,recitat ipsam dominicam institutionê. Ego enim, inquit,accepi à domino, quod & tradidi vobis.Quasi dicat:Ego vobis non tra didi,quod facitis,neq; quicquam à me exco gitatum,sed ab ipso domino traditum per me accepistis,à quo procul absunt quæ vos in cô uentibus vestris facitis.Non instituit dominus in ecclesia sua schismata,nô tradidit nobis cœ nas priuatas,nec discreuit inter suos discipu los, sed communem omnibus cœnam, ab om nibus ex æquo & concorditer celebrandâ in stituit ac tradidit.Et ego nihil vobis aliud tra didi,quàm quod ab illo accepi,à quo vos iam deficere cœpistis. Hoc sensu di&ũ puto. quod de dominica traditione memorat dicés : Ego enim accepi à domino,qd & tradidi vobis,vt non minus neget eos à se accepisse, & institu tioni dominicæ conforme esse quod faciebát, quàm quid ipsis à domino acceptum tradiâ- rit commemoret.
units.tr: Thus far the Apostle has rebuked the Corinthians, who in their schismatic gatherings, while coming together into one assembly, divided the church, presumed on their own private dinners without waiting for the multitude of the faithful, despised the church of God, and shamed the poor who were in it. For these reasons he said that they did not eat the Lord's Supper, nor did he praise them for acting thus. Now, to show how far such things are foreign to the institution of the Lord's Supper, and remote from what he himself had delivered to them, he recites the Lord's own institution: "For I received from the Lord," he says, "what I also delivered to you." It is as if he said: I did not deliver to you what you are doing, nor anything devised by myself, but you received through me what was handed down by the Lord himself, from whom the things you do in your gatherings are far removed. The Lord did not institute schisms in his church; he did not hand down to us private dinners, nor did he distinguish among his disciples, but he instituted and handed down one common supper, to be celebrated by all equally and in harmony. And I delivered to you nothing other than what I received from him, from whom you have now begun to fall away. I think this is meant in the sense that, when he mentions the tradition about the Lord's Supper, saying "For I received from the Lord what I also delivered to you," he wishes to show that what they did was not less alien to him, and not in conformity with the Lord's institution, than he is himself to deny that they received it from him; and so he recalls what was received from the Lord and handed on to them.

units.la: Est hoc loco diligenter obseruandũ,ad quâ sint regulam corrigendi sacramentorum abu sus.Nihil rectè nisi ad certam regulam corrigi tur.Certa autê regula est nô humani Magiste- rij,quantumuis annosa & inueterata præsum ptio,sed dominica institutio.Ad hanc reuocat Corinthios Apostolus,& præuaricationem il lorum,qua vsum cœnæ dominicæ corruperât corrigit.Nô dicit:Ego enim vester Apostolus
units.tr: Here we must carefully observe by what rule the abuses of the sacraments are to be corrected. Nothing is rightly corrected except by a certain rule. The certain rule, however, is not the institution of any human teacher, however long-standing and entrenched the presumption may be, but the institution of the Lord. It is to this that the Apostle recalls the Corinthians, and by it he corrects their transgression, by which they had corrupted the practice of the Lord's Supper. He does not say, "For I, your Apostle, have handed this down to you by apostolic authority," but: "For I received from the Lord that which I also handed down to you."

units.la: s ȝ ApostaApostolica vobis authoritate sic tradidi, sed: Ego enim accepi à domino, quod & tradidi vobis. Ad eandem & nobis respiciendum est hodie, videndumq; ne à norma illius quolibet declinemus. Non sunt audiendi qui praetexût praetres, cocilia, Magisterium spiritus, potestatem ecclesiae, catholicâ consuetudinem, &c. Omnia haec posterius sunt inducta. Nobis regula veritatis esse debet, quae veniat à Christo, per illius Apostolos transmissa. Et vt cum Tertull. dicam, non licet nobis nostro hic indulgere arbitrio, sed nec eligere quod aliquis de arbitrio suo induxit. Apostolos domini habemus, qui nec ipsi de suo quicquâ quod inducerent elegerunt, sed acceptâ à Christo disciplinam, nationibus fideliter assignauerunt, &c.
units.tr: We too must look to that same rule today, and take care that we do not turn aside from its standard in any direction. Those who put forward the fathers, councils, the teaching office of the spirit, the authority of the Church, Catholic custom, and so on, are not to be heard. All these things were introduced afterwards. The rule of truth ought to be ours: it comes from Christ and was handed down through his Apostles. And, to say with Tertullian, we are not permitted to indulge our own judgment here, nor even to choose what someone has introduced at his own discretion. We have the Apostles of the Lord, who did not themselves choose anything of their own to introduce, but, having received the discipline from Christ, faithfully handed it on to the nations, and so on.

units.la: Deinde proponitur hic fidelis ministri exemplum. Huius est tradere quidem ecclesiae, quae sint credenda & facienda, veùm non alia quâ accepta à domino, vt sit uox illius: Ego accepi à domino, quod & tradidi vobis. Disputant de potestate ministrorum in ecclesia. Potestatem habent docendi & praescribendi quae tradita sunt à domino. Si illa ritè vtantur, abûde satis habent quod agât. Perfidi sunt, qui nô tradita à domino praescribunt ecclesijs, & tradita ab illo interuertunt, atque interim autoritatem ac potestatem suam iactant. Magistri synagogae dicebant: Lex est in terra, nô est in coelo, significantes esse illam suae potestati subiectam. Sic isti. Sacramenta, inquiunt, & ecclesiae & scripturae sunt in terra, non sunt in coelo. Licet hoc verbis non dicant, reipsa tamen eodem in istis Magisterio quod volunt statuunt, quo Rabini Iudaeorum usi sunt inlegalibus statutis.
units.tr: Next, the faithful example of the minister is set before us here. It belongs to him to deliver to the Church what is to be believed and done, but nothing other than what he received from the Lord, so that his voice is: "I received from the Lord that which I also handed down to you." They dispute about the power of ministers in the Church. They have the power of teaching and prescribing what has been handed down by the Lord. If they use it rightly, they have quite enough to do. Those are faithless who prescribe to the churches things not handed down by the Lord, and overturn what was handed down by him, while meanwhile boasting of their authority and power. The masters of the synagogue used to say, "The Law is on earth, not in heaven," meaning that it was subject to their power. So do these men. They say that the sacraments and the Church and Scripture are on earth, not in heaven. Although they do not say it in words, in fact they establish by that same teaching office what they want, just as the rabbis of the Jews used to do with their illegal statutes.

units.la: QVOD dominus Iesus nocte qua tradebatur accepit panem, &c.) Pertinet ista ad secundâ partem, qua uerus usus dominicae coenae ex ipsius institutione proponitur. Cum dicit: Quod dominus Iesus exprimit ipsum autorem huius sacri. Vocat eum dominum, ut admoneat domesticos de illius authoritate, quo de exhibenda illi cōuenieti, ac debita obseruatia cogitet.
units.tr: "That the Lord Jesus, on the night in which he was betrayed, took bread, etc." This belongs to the second part, in which the true use of the Lord's Supper is set out from its own institution. When he says "That the Lord Jesus," he names the very author of this sacred rite. He calls him "Lord" so as to remind the household of his authority, that they may think about the fitting honour and due reverence to be shown to him.

units.la: NOCTE, inquit, qua tradebatur.) Meminit temporis quo sacrorū hoc à domino est institutū. Sic specificat ultimā coenā dni. Et ipse do minus signanter eam notauit, cum diceret: Dico enim uobis, quod nô sum ex hoc manduca turus, &c. Item, quodnon sum bibiturus de generatione uitis, donec regnū Dei ueniat. Admonet hac temporis cōnotatione supremam esse dispositionem moriturī domini in mystica illius coenā propositam, quo plus illa afficiamur, & simul auocat carnales Corinthios à studio periturī cibi ad cōtemplationem testamenti, quod à domino nobis est ex hoc saeculo iam iam migraturo relictum.
units.tr: Nor is it without reason that these things were done by the Lord at night. The law so prescribed that the Passover lamb was to be eaten at night, in remembrance of the passing of the angel, by which the children of Israel were freed from Egypt when all the firstborn of the Egyptians were slain. So we read in Exodus 12: "And they shall eat the flesh that night, roasted with fire." Again: "And I will pass through the land of Egypt that night, and smite every firstborn." And: "This night is to be observed to the Lord, when he brought them out of the land of Egypt. All the children of Israel must observe it in their generations." The Lord confirmed this legal ordinance, not only by eating the old Passover with his disciples at night and instituting the sacrament of the New Testament, but also by beginning the work of our redemption that same night, since its beginning was the betrayal by which, through Judas, he was handed over to the priests and Pharisees at night. Thus on that night the Passover of the Old Testament came to its end, as it had begun, and the sacrament of the New was instituted.

units.la: Non est autem praeter rationem, quod nocte sunt haec à domino gesta. Sic erat lege constitutum, ut agnus ille paschalis nocte edere tur, propter rememorationem transitus angelici, quo cunctis Aegyptiorum primogenitis caesis liberati sunt ex Aegypto filij Israel. Sic Exod. 12. legimus. Et edent carnes nocte illa assas igni. Item: & transibo per terram Aegypti nocte illa, percutiamq; omne primogenitum. Et: Nox istaerit obseruabilis domino, quando eduxit eos de terra Aegypti. Hanc obseruare debet omnes filij Israel in generationibus suis. Huic constitutioni legali confirmauit se domi nus, non modo edendo pascha vetus cum suis discipulis nocte, & sacramētū Noui testamenti instituendo, sed & opus redēptionis nostrae ea nocte inchoando, quatenus principiū illius erat traditio, qua per Iudam sacerdotib. ac phari saeis nocte illa prodebatur. Nocte igitur ea vt coeperat, terminabatur Veteris testamenti pascha, & Noui instituitur sacramentum.
units.tr: It is not out of place that these things were done by the Lord at night. By law it was ordained that the paschal lamb be eaten at night, in remembrance of the passing of the angel, by which the children of Israel were freed from Egypt when all the firstborn of the Egyptians were slain. So we read in Exodus 12: "And they shall eat the flesh that night, roasted with fire." Again: "And I will pass through the land of Egypt that night, and will smite every firstborn." And: "This night is to be observed to the Lord, when he brought them out of the land of Egypt. This all the children of Israel must observe in their generations." The Lord confirmed this legal ordinance, not only by eating the old Passover with his disciples at night and instituting the sacrament of the New Testament, but also by beginning on that night the work of our redemption, inasmuch as its beginning was the betrayal, by which he was handed over that night by Judas to the priests and Pharisees. Thus on that night, as it had begun, the Passover of the Old Testament was brought to an end, and the sacrament of the New was instituted.

units.la: Nec est, vt dicat quisquam. Ergo & nobis edenda est coena dominica, nô interdiu, sed nocte, quo temporis quoq; institutionis illius rationem habeamus. Licet enim damnare nolim si citra superstitionem temporib. perfequutionum nocte conueniant fideles, cū interdiu non liceat, & vnanimi spiritu memoriam dominicae mortis celebrent, concedendum tamē non est, requiri hoc à nobis, vt nōnisi nocte secundum exemplū Christi, ad communicationem mysticae mensae conueniamus. Etenim quod nocte fecit dominus, legi dabatur. Qd' vero fidelibus suis instituit, nullis nec noctis, nec diei articulis alligauit, sed liberum vniuscuiusq; ecclesiae commoditati reliquit. Nô dixit discipulis: Erit vobis nox ista obseruabilis, per cunctas vestras generationes, sed, quotiescunque ederitis ac biberitis, hoc facite in mei rememorationem. Deinde licet institutum sit hoc memoriale ipsius nocte, non est tamē nocte, sed clara luce corpus ipsius in morte pro nobis datum, & sanguis effusus in cruce, cuius sacrificij memoriam per mysticam mensam celebramus. Sit ergo liberum ecclesiae, vel nocte vel interdiu conuenire adcoenam dominicam peragendam. Qui nocte conueniunt, nocte m habent, in qua traditus est dominus, & Noui Paschatis sacramentum institutum, de qua viliter cogitare possunt. Qui panem domini in terdiu edunt, ac calicem bibunt, diem habent, in qua immolatus est in cruce agnus, & sanguis Noui testamenti, pro peccatis nostris effusus, ad quam respiciant. Seruiat haec libertas cōmoditatibus ecclesiae, non faciat ad contentiones & odia, quibus opus domini destruitur. Dum haec dicimus, non moramur canone qui de consecr. dist. in ct. 1. vetat nocte fieri Missas, dempta nocte Natalis domini. Antiquū hoc est Romanis Pontificibus, vt libertatem ecclesiae Magisterio suo opprimant. Sed pergamus.
units.tr: Nor is there anyone who should say: "Therefore the Lord's Supper must also be eaten by us at night, not by day, so that we may also have regard to the reason for the time of its institution." For although I would not wish to condemn it if, in times of persecution, the faithful gather at night when it is not permitted by day, and with one spirit celebrate the memory of the Lord's death, yet it must not be conceded that we are required to come together to the communion of the mystical table only at night, after the example of Christ. For what the Lord did at night was given under the Law. But what he instituted for his faithful people he bound to no hour of night or day, and left it to the convenience of each church. He did not say to the disciples: "This night shall be observed by you through all your generations," but: "As often as you eat and drink, do this in remembrance of me." Moreover, although this memorial was instituted at night, it was not at night, but in clear daylight, that his body was given for us in death, and his blood shed on the cross, whose sacrifice we commemorate through the mystical table. Let it therefore be free for the Church to assemble for the celebration of the Lord's Supper either at night or by day. Those who gather at night have the night in which the Lord was betrayed and the sacrament of the New Passover was instituted, and they may think on it fittingly. Those who eat the Lord's bread and drink the cup by day have the day on which the lamb was sacrificed on the cross, and the blood of the New Testament shed for our sins, to which they may look. Let this liberty serve the advantage of the Church; let it not lead to contentions and hatreds, by which the work of the Lord is destroyed. While we say these things, we do not dwell on the canon in Distinction 1 on Consecration, which forbids Masses to be said at night, except on the night of the Lord's Nativity. This is an old practice of the Roman Pontiffs, to oppress the liberty of the Church by their teaching office. But let us go on.

units.la: ACCEPIT panem, inquit.) Recitat institutionē dominicā, cuius duae sunt partes, vna quid fecerit dominus, altera, quid nos facere iusserit. Quid fecerit, exprimit dicens: Accepit panem, egit gratias, Deofcilicet patri. fregit ac dixit, &c. Consimiliter & poculum peracta cena, &c. na,&c. Et huius facti externi mens ac sensus exprimitur istis verbis. Hoc est corpus meum quod pro vobis frangitur. Et: Hoc poculum nouum testamentum est in meo sanguine, ne se discipuli vulgari modo, vel etiam iuxta religionem veteris Pascatis, panem manducare, ac vinum bibere putarent, praesertim cum generetur ista in ipsa coena veteris Pascatis, i qua cofederat secundu Mosaicę legis praescriptu.
units.tr: "He took bread," he says. He recites the institution of the Lord, of which there are two parts: one, what the Lord did; the other, what he ordered us to do. What he did, he sets out, saying: "He took bread, gave thanks to God," namely the Father, "broke it and said," etc. Likewise, with the cup, when the supper was ended, etc. And the meaning and sense of this external action is expressed in these words: "This is my body, which is broken for you." And: "This cup is the New Testament in my blood." This was so that the disciples should not think that he was eating bread and drinking wine in the ordinary way, or even in the manner of the religion of the old Passover, especially since this was being done in the very supper of the old Passover, which was being celebrated according to the prescription of the Mosaic law.

units.la: ACCEPIT panem, inquit.) Intellige, post quā esum agni Paschalis absoluerat, id quod videre est in Luca. Panem ac vinum vsurpauit res vsitatas, parabiles, naturae nostrae amicas, & ad confortandum nos exhilarandumq; diuinitus datas.
units.tr: "He took bread," he says. Understand: after he had finished eating the paschal lamb, as is to be seen in Luke. He took bread and wine, common and easily available things, friendly to our nature, and given by God to strengthen and gladden us.

units.la: GRATIAS egit, inquit.) Hoc habebat in more, sicuti patet Ioa. 6. Matth. 14. & in poculo Pascatis, Luc. 22. Quomodo autē Seruatori vnigenito Dei conuenerit, vt gratias ageret Deo patri, Ioan. 6. annotauimus. Euangelistae verbis εὐλογεῖν & εὐχαριστεῖν, eodē sensu pro gratiarum actione vtuntur, ne quis hic locum esse putet Papisticae consecrationi, quasi benedicere idem sit quod consecrare. Matthaeus, Lucas, & Paulus dicunt Christum in coena accepto pane, ac poculo, gratias egisse, Deo patri videlicet, Marcus vero solus dicit eum benedixisse, accepto pane, qui tamen & ipse, vbi de poculo loquitur, gratias illum egisse dicit. Quare manifestum est, idem esse benedicere, quod gratias agere, quod & infrà cap. 14. manifeste videre licet, vbi dicit Apostolus: Alioqui εἰ ἐνλογῇς {B}σης, id est, si benedixeris spiritu, is qui implet locum indocti, quomodo dicturus est, Amen, ἐπὶ τῇ σῇ εὐχαριστίᾳ, id est, ad tuam gratiarū actionem. Accepto itaq; pane Christus, gratias egit Deo patri, de consecratione vero, qua panem hisce verbis mutauerit in suum corpus, non legimus quicquam.
units.tr: "He gave thanks," he says. This was their custom, as is clear from John 6, Matthew 14, and over the paschal cup, Luke 22. How it was fitting for the only-begotten Son of God to give thanks to God the Father, we have noted at John 6. The evangelists use the words [εὐλογεῖν] and [εὐχαριστεῖν] in the same sense for giving thanks, so that no one may think there is room here for the Papistical consecration, as if to bless were the same as to consecrate. Matthew, Luke, and Paul say that Christ, having taken the bread and the cup at the supper, gave thanks, namely to God the Father; Mark alone says that he blessed, having taken the bread, yet he too, when he speaks of the cup, says that Christ gave thanks. Therefore it is plain that to bless is the same as to give thanks, which can also be clearly seen in 1 Cor. 14, where the Apostle says: "Otherwise, if you bless [εὐλογῇς] with the spirit," that is, if you bless with the spirit, "he who fills the place of the unlearned, how will he say Amen at your [ἐπὶ τῇ σῇ εὐχαριστίᾳ] thanksgiving," that is, at your giving of thanks. Christ therefore, having taken the bread, gave thanks to God the Father; but about the consecration, by which he changed the bread into his body by these words, we read nothing.

units.la: Optandum sanè esset, vt quibus verbis Christus Deo patri gratias egerit, Euangelistae expressissent. Verum cum illud factum non sit, cōsiderandum nobis est, qua in re gratias egerit. Habebat hoc quidem in more vt ad quemlibet cibum ageret Deo patri gratias, quam consuetudinem pijs hominibus, praesertim patribusfamiliās, in eo populo fuisse traditur, verum dubio procul in hac causa singularib& & praecipuis verbis vsus est, quibus discipulorū suorum animos ad intellectum eorum quae agebat induceret, quemadmodum in oratione quoq; fecit, quam Ioan. cap. 17. commemorat. Primū in re non magis ipsum, quàm nos concernente, gratias egit. Cogitemus ergo quid nos facere deceat in hac causa, quorum gratia filius Dei patri gratias egit. Deinde non solū in re aliena, sed & tali gratias egit, quae morte ipsius poscebat, vt impleretur & confirmaretur. Quis non videt igitur, quàm ad moriendū pro nobis animo fuerit propenso? Hinc illud: Desiderio desideraui, hoc pascha manducare vobiscū, antequā patiar. Seruit ergo nobis hic locus, non modo ad exemplum, sed & ad do-
units.tr: It would surely have been desirable for the evangelists to record the words with which Christ gave thanks to God the Father. But since that was not done, we must consider the matter for which he gave thanks. It was his custom to give thanks to God the Father over any food, a practice said to have been held among the pious of that people, especially heads of households. Yet undoubtedly in this case he used singular and outstanding words, by which he might lead his disciples' minds to understand what he was doing, as he also did in the prayer that John records in chapter 17. First, he gave thanks in a matter that concerned himself no less than us. Let us consider, then, what it becomes us to do in this matter, we for whose sake the Son of God gave thanks to the Father. Next, he gave thanks not only in a matter concerning another, but in one that his death required, so that it might be fulfilled and confirmed. Who does not see, then, how ready his mind was to die for us? Hence that saying: "With desire I have desired to eat this Passover with you before I suffer." This place therefore serves us not only as an example but also as a teaching,

units.la: cumentum, vnde cognoscamus, quàm parato & prompto animo mortē pro nobis obierit dns.
units.tr: from which we may learn with how prepared and ready a mind the Lord died for us.

units.la: FREGIT, inquit.) Panis erat tostus, placenta azyma, quā Germanice vocamus kuochen, vt posset frangi. Eiusmodi namq; placentis vtebantur in festo Paschatis, iuxta legem vsus est illis & dominus, non necessitate aliqua quasi non alio pane liceret vti in hac causa, sed quoniam non referebat quo pane vteretur, modo cibario, & qd alius noadesset, nec sine offendiculo alium vsurpare posset. Eratautem consuetudo hæc domini, vt in morem patrisfamiliās panē ipse frangeret, & discipulis vescendum distribueret, vnde ipsum post resurrectionem duo ex illis in Emaus tum demum cognouerunt, vbi panem ipsis fregisset. Et cognouerunt eū, inquit Lucas cap. 24. in fractione panis.
units.tr: "He broke it," he says. The bread was toasted, an unleavened cake, which we in German call a kuchen, so that it could be broken. Cakes of this kind were used at the feast of Passover, and the Lord too used them according to the law. He did not do so from any necessity, as if it were not permitted to use other bread in this matter, but because it made no difference what bread he used, provided it was ordinary food and nothing else was at hand, and another could not be taken without offence. Moreover, it was the Lord's custom to break bread himself in the manner of a head of a household and distribute it to his disciples to eat. That is why the two at Emmaus recognised him after the resurrection only when he had broken bread for them. "And they recognised him," says Luke in chapter 24, "in the breaking of bread."

units.la: Lucas dicit: & dedit eis: Mat. vero, & dedit discipulis. Aderant duodecim, de alijs non legimus. An & Iudas tum adfuerit, in quæstione venit. Adfuisse illum negat Hilar. & Rupertus Abbas Tuitiensis, quorū sententiae quomodo contradicere debeā non video. Illud video, si ordo narrationis rectè consideretur, nō posse certò probari, quod adfuerit, vbi mysterium hoc corporis ac sanguinis sui instituit ac commendauit discipulis suis dominus.
units.tr: Luke says, "and gave to them"; Matthew, "and gave to the disciples." Twelve were present; of the others we do not read. Whether Judas too was present then is a matter of dispute. Hilary and Rupert, abbot of Deutz, deny that he was present, and I do not see how I could rightly contradict their opinions. This much I see: if the order of the narrative is rightly considered, it cannot be certainly proved that he was present when the Lord instituted and commended this mystery of his body and blood to his disciples.

units.la: An ipse prior comederit ex hoc pane, & biberit de hoc vino, non est certum, quamuis sic senserit Chrysostomus, homil. super Matthæū 8j. dicens: Ipse quoq; bibit ex eo, ne auditis verbis illis dicerent: Quid igitur? Sanguinem bibimus? & carnem comedimus? ac ideo perturbaretur. Nam & quando prius de hoc verba fecit, multi propter verba tantum scandalū passi sunt. Ne igitur nunc quoque id accideret, primus ipse hoc fecit, vt eos tranquillo animo ad communicationem mysteriorum induceret. Hæc ille. Et de consec. distin. 2. cap. Nec Moses, tribuitur Christo quod fuerit & conuiua & conuiuium, ipse inquit, comedes & qui comeditur. Sanè multum lucis adferret ad intelligendum hanc causam, non dico illis, qui nimium sunt contentiosi, sed rudioribus, si certo constaret Chrysostomi hac in re sententia.
units.tr: Whether he himself first ate of this bread and drank of this wine is not certain, although Chrysostom thought so, in his homily 81 on Matthew, saying: "He himself also drank of it, lest, having heard those words, they should say, 'What then? Do we drink blood and eat flesh?' and so be disturbed. For when he had spoken of this earlier, many took offence at the words alone. Lest this happen now too, he himself did it first, so as to lead them with a calm mind to communion in the mysteries." Thus he. And in De consecratione, distinction 2, the chapter "Nec Moses", it is attributed to Christ that he was both guest and feast: "he himself," it says, "will eat and be eaten." Certainly it would shed much light on this question, I do not say for those who are too contentious, but for the simpler folk, if Chrysostom's opinion on this point were firmly established.

units.la: Et dixit, accipite, edite, &c. Ad eundem modum & poculum peracta coena. Mat. 26. dedit illis dicens: bibite ex hoc omnes. Et Marcus, & biberunt exeo omnes. Sic dedit illis panem à se fractum, & vinum, neq; ad includendum (vide Origen. super Leuiticum homel. 5.) neque ad ostentandum, neq; ad circumgestandum, neq; ad adorandum, sed ad edendum & bibendum. Deinde non dedit vni tantum ex illis, nec Petro, nec Iacobo, qui reliquorum nomine ederet & biberet, sed dedit omnibus, vt ederent ac biberent singuli. Faciebat enim hoc ad mysterium, cuius communicatio exeo proponebatur omnibus.
units.tr: "And he said, 'Take, eat,' etc." In the same way the cup, after supper was over. Matthew 26: "he gave it to them, saying: Drink of this, all of you." And Mark: "and they all drank of it." Thus he gave them the bread broken by himself, and the wine, not to be enclosed (see Origen on Leviticus, homily 5), nor to be displayed, nor carried about, nor adored, but to be eaten and drunk. Further, he did not give it to only one of them, not to Peter or to James, so that he might eat and drink on behalf of the rest; he gave it to all, so that each might eat and drink. For he did this for the sake of the mystery, whose communion was set forth to all from it.

units.la: Neque otiosum est, quod de poculo peculiariter dixisse meminoratur. Bibite ex eo oēs, & Marcus addit, & biberunt ex eo omnes. Facie bat enim eâ pars sacramenti potissimum ad te stamenti Noui confirmationem. Quare omni no magna est eorum temeritas, qui illâ ex vsu fidelium Christi ademerunt.
units.tr: Nor is it idle that he is recorded to have spoken specifically about the cup: "Drink of it, all of you"; and Mark adds, "and they all drank of it." For this part of the sacrament was especially for the confirmation of the New Testament. Hence the rashness of those is great who have taken it away from the use of Christ's faithful.

units.la: Hactenus de externo Christi facto, tàquam prima præsentis materiæ parte, iam uidedum est de illius mysterio mête ac sensu. Quod pa nem accepit, gratias egit, fregit, deditque discipulis, ac poculum consimiliter exhibuit, poterat vtrunque ex more fecifle videri, nec aliquid subesse mysterij. Quare facti sui mysterium exposuit inductione vsus omnium commodissima, ex sacramento VeterisPascatis desumpta, ad cuius esum ac potum pro ritu legis considerant, qua de re Lucæ 22. sic legimus: Euntes autem inuenerunt sicut dixerat illis, & parauerunt Pascha. Et cum iam esset tempestiuum, accubuit, ac duodecim Apostoli cum eo. Et ait illis: Desiderio desideraui HOC pascha máducare vobiscum, antequam patiar. Dico enim vobis posthac non edam vltrà ex eo, donec compleatur in regno Dei. Erat hoc ultimum Veteris testamenti pascha, & terminandus iam erat figuralis illius usus, complendusque in regno Dei per mastationem viri ac Noui testamenti Paschatis, agni videlicet Dei, cuius sanguine totum genus mortalium à peccatis erat liberandum. Et hoc est quod dicit: Posthac enim non edam ex eo donec cópleatur in regno Dei, hoc est, in Noui testamenti gratia. Hæc adimpletio figuralis Paschatis, statim est altero die facta in cruce. Huius desiderio vltimum hoc Pascha cupide edebat. Ardebat enim ad perficiedam generis humani redemptionem. Nec dubito quin accepto in manus agno Pischali, ac figuralí gratias egerit Deo patri, & hæc uerba ad discipulos protulerit. Quemadmodum & de poculo Paschali subijcitur. Et accepto poculo gratias egit ac dixit, accipite hoc & diuidite inter uos: Dico enim vobis quod non bibam de fructu vitis, donec regnum Dei ueniat. Videmus itaque dominum non comedisse delegali agno ac poculũ illius bibisse prorsus mutum, sed egisse patri gratias, & mysterium quoque illius sic exposuisse, vt ad institutionem Noui Paschatis collimaret. Quare hac inductione præmissa mox absoluto Paschati legali institutionem Noui subiecturus, accepit panem, gratias egit, fregit, dedit discipulis dicens, accipite, edite, hoc meum est corpus quod pro uobis frangitur, uel, ut Lucas habet, datur. Similiter & poculum paracta cœna dicens: Hoc poculum Nouum testamentum est in sanguine meo, qui pro uobis effundi-tur. Sic igitur explicat factum suum, significans Vetus se Pascha terminare, ac Nouũ instituere, quasi dicat: Hactenus durauit Vetus testamétum, cuius cófirmatio fuit in sanguine agni, quem sub Mose patres nostri in Ægypto iussu Dei mastauerůt, ac sanguine illius ab an gelo sunt percussori liberati, cui» liberationis typicum, ac memoriale sacramentum singulis
units.tr: So far concerning the outward act of Christ, as the first part of the present matter. Now we must see into the mystery and meaning of it. That he took bread, gave thanks, broke it, and gave it to the disciples, and likewise handed over the cup, might have seemed to have been done merely according to custom, with no mystery underlying it. Therefore he set out the mystery of his deed by the most suitable kind of introduction, drawn from the sacrament of the Old Passover, whose eating and drinking they observed according to the rite of the law. On this Luke 22 reads thus: "And they went and found it as he had told them, and they prepared the Passover. And when the time had come, he reclined, and the twelve apostles with him. And he said to them: 'With desire I have desired to eat THIS Passover with you before I suffer. For I tell you that from now on I will not eat of it until it is fulfilled in the kingdom of God.'" This was the last Passover of the Old Testament, and that figurative observance was now to be ended and fulfilled in the kingdom of God, through the slaying of the Lamb of the New Testament Passover, namely the Lamb of God, by whose blood the whole human race was to be freed from sins. And this is what he means: "For from now on I will not eat of it until it is fulfilled in the kingdom of God," that is, in the grace of the New Testament. This fulfilment of the figurative Passover took place the very next day on the cross. He ate this last Passover eagerly, out of longing for it, for he burned to accomplish the redemption of the human race. Nor do I doubt that, having taken the paschal lamb into his hands, and the figurative food, he gave thanks to God the Father and spoke these words to the disciples. Just so, concerning the paschal cup, it is added: "And having taken the cup he gave thanks and said: 'Take this and divide it among yourselves; for I tell you I will not drink of the fruit of the vine until the kingdom of God comes.'" We see, therefore, that the Lord did not eat the legal lamb and drink its cup in silence, but gave thanks to the Father, and set out its mystery in such a way as to aim at the institution of the New Passover. Hence, with this introduction set forth, and about to add the institution of the New once the legal Passover was finished, he took bread, gave thanks, broke it, and gave it to the disciples, saying: "Take, eat; this is my body, which is broken for you," or, as Luke has it, "given for you." Likewise also the cup, after supper was over, saying: "This cup is the New Testament in my blood, which is poured out for you." So he explains his deed, signifying that he was ending the Old Passover and instituting the New, as if to say: "Hitherto the Old Testament has lasted, whose confirmation was in the blood of the lamb which our fathers under Moses slew in Egypt by God's command, and by whose blood they were freed from the destroying angel. The typical and memorial sacrament of that deliverance they celebrated each year with this solemn rite."

units.la: annis ritu hoc solenni celebrarunt. Iam uero vt instat Veteris testamenti terminus, & principium Noui, sic finem habet typicum étiá & memoriale hoc Pascha, & inchoandũ est Nouum. Habuit vetus suum typicum agnum, & annuũ illius sacramentũ, habet nouum quoq; suum agnum, nó typicum, sed verũ, cuius sanguis effusus auferet peccata mundi, auertetq; iram & ultionem Dei. Hic agnus ego sum. Immolabor pro uobis, & sanguine meo testamétum Nouũ confirmabo. Quare nó est ut posthac typicum Veteris testameti Pascha edatis. Ecce instituo vobis Nouum. Panis hic, quem frango, & ad edendum uobis distribuo, & poculum quod bibédum uobis porrigo, nó sunt uobis accipienda simpliciter, ut panis & uinũ, pro cibando ac potando corpore, sed ut sacramentum, ac mysterium Noui testameti. Commendo uobis corpus ac sanguinem meũ quorum sacramentũ instituo in hoc pane & uino. Panis hic corpus meũ est, corpus ueri ac Noui agni, paulo post pro uobis immolandum. Poculum hoc Nouum testametum est in sanguine meo, sanguine ueri agni, qui ॥ uobis effundetur. Quod eni iṁ Veteri test. tuit agnus Paschalis, & ritus edendi illius, hoc erit posthac in Nouo panis huius fractura, ac poculi istius distributio. Sicus agnus hic typicus, & memoria lis habetur pro sacramento nõ ueteris testamenti: ita panis hic, cum poculo habeatur pro sacramẽto immolari meí corporis, & effusi san guinis in Nouo testamento. Hæc meo iudicio, mens Christi est in præsenti causa. Quem admodum Moses Exod.12. de agno Paschatis præcepit, ac memoriale illius annuũ, ac solen ne instituit, priusquam ille mactaretur, ac sanguine suo angelũ percussoré auerterēt, atq; i ta Veteris testamenti sacramentũ condidit, ita & Christus terminaturus Vetus & inchoatur Nouum test. sacramentũ Noui Paschatis insti tuit, priusquá ipse illius agnus in cruce immo laretur. Hac inductione puto facillimum erat discipulis intelligere quid vellet hic Nouus ri tus, quë instituebat dominus. Neq; existiimo commodiore esse ratione consequędi intelle-ctus in hac causa, quàm si quę Lucas scribit di-ligenter considerentur, & sine hac inductione nemo de mysterio hoc suopte sensu iudicare ac pronunciare præsumat.
units.tr: Now indeed, as the limit of the Old Testament presses and the beginning of the New, so this typical and memorial Passover also has its end, and the New is to be begun. The Old had its typical lamb and its yearly sacrament of it; the New has its own lamb too, not typical but true, whose poured-out blood will take away the sins of the world and turn away the wrath and vengeance of God. "I am this lamb. I shall be sacrificed for you, and with my blood I will confirm the New Testament. Therefore it is not right that you should any longer eat the typical Passover of the Old Testament. Behold, I institute the New for you. This bread, which I break and distribute to you to eat, and the cup which I hold out to you to drink, are not to be taken by you simply as bread and wine for feeding and refreshing the body, but as the sacrament and mystery of the New Testament. I commend to you my body and blood, whose sacrament I institute in this bread and wine. This bread is my body, the body of the true and New Lamb, soon to be sacrificed for you. This cup is the New Testament in my blood, the blood of the true Lamb, which will be poured out for you. For what in the Old Testament was the paschal lamb, and the rite of eating it, will in the New be the breaking of this bread and the distribution of this cup. As that typical lamb was held to be a sacrament and memorial of the Old Testament, so this bread, with the cup, is held to be a sacrament of the immolation of my body and the outpouring of my blood in the New Testament." These, in my judgment, are Christ's intentions in the present matter. Just as Moses in Exodus 12 commanded concerning the paschal lamb, and instituted its yearly and solemn memorial before it was slain and its blood turned away the destroying angel, and so established the sacrament of the Old Testament, so Christ, about to end the Old and begin the New, instituted the sacrament of the New Passover before he himself, as its lamb, was sacrificed on the cross. By this introduction I think it was very easy for the disciples to understand what this new rite, which the Lord was instituting, meant. Nor do I think there is a more suitable way to reach understanding in this matter than if what Luke writes is carefully considered, and no one presumes to judge and pronounce on this mystery from his own opinion without this introduction.

units.la: Cum itaq; dicit: Accipite, edite, hoc meũ est corpus quod pro uobis frangitur, nó debe mus hærere in pane, sed intendere in mysteriũ corporis Christi, tàquam agni immaculati, & pro nobis in cruce immolati & ad edendũ, non tá détibus, q fide instrucți accedere, qua creda mus corpus unigeniti Dei in mortem pro no bis esse datũ, & sanguinem illius pro peccatis nostris effusum. Huc nó respiciebát Corinthij cũ ex cœna domini priuata facerét cóiuia & symposia. Et utinã huc respiciat fratres nostri, q de uerbis istis: Hoc meũ est corpus, ita dispu tát ut magis quærát ubi sit corp» Christi q my steriũ mortis illius, ac redéptionis nostrę syn-cera cera fide perpédât. Exo.12. legimus ad hûc mo dum. Cû dixerint vobis filij vestri, quid est vobis hic cultus? Dicetis, victima transitus domini est, quo transiuit super domos filiorum Israel in Ægypto, cû percuteret Ægyptios & domos nostras liberaret, &c. Hisce verbis de sacramento ac ritu Veteris Pasc. iussu dei instruebantur filij Iudæorum. Et tamè haud quaquâ disputabât quomodo agn<bl>ꝰ</bl> ille Paschatis, què singulis annis edebát, victima esset trâsit<bl>ꝰ</bl> dni semel facti in Ægypto. Intelligebant enim esse eum illius <bl>זכרון</bl>, id est, memoriale. Cósimili modo instruendi sunt, & nostri de pane hoc & ritu cœnæ dominicæ, dicendûq; illis: Panis hic, victima est corporis dni, quà sese pro nobis Deo patri obtulit in cruce. Poterat dominus simpliciter dicere: Accipite, edite in mei rememorationé, vel, accipite, edite, hoc est memoriale meû, nisi voluisset mysterium mortis suæ ac nostræ redemptionis exprimere, & ecclesiæ suæ corporis ac sanguinis sui sacramentum commendare. Vt hoc faceret dixit: Accipite, edite, Hoc meum est corpus, quod pro vobis frangitur, quod perinde est, ac si dixisset: Hoc est sacramentum MEI corporis, pro vobis paulo post in cruce moriturî : Hoc est, victima corporis mei. Hoc est agnus Dei, qui pro vobis mactabitur. Hoc nouum Pascha est in corpore meo, quod pro vobis immolabitur: Hoc est memoriale corporis mei, quod pro vobis dabitur.
units.tr: Therefore, when he says, "Take, eat; this is my body, which is broken for you," we ought not to stop at the bread but to fix our attention on the mystery of Christ's body, as of the unblemished Lamb, sacrificed for us on the cross. We should come to eat it not merely with our teeth but instructed by faith, believing that the body of the only-begotten God was given to death for us and his blood poured out for our sins. The Corinthians did not keep this in view when they turned the Lord's supper into private feasts and drinking parties. Would that our brethren would keep it in view, those who dispute about these words, "This is my body," and seek more where Christ's body is than weigh with pure faith the mystery of his death and of our redemption. In Exodus 12 we read in this manner: "When your children say to you, 'What does this rite mean to you?', you shall say, 'It is the sacrifice of the Lord's passover, by which he passed over the houses of the children of Israel in Egypt, when he struck the Egyptians and delivered our houses,' etc." By these words the children of the Jews were instructed, at God's command, about the sacrament and rite of the Old Passover. Yet they never disputed how that paschal lamb, which they ate every year, could be the sacrifice of the Lord's passing over, which had happened once in Egypt. They understood that it was the memorial [זכרון] of that event. In the same way our people too must be taught about this bread and the rite of the Lord's supper, and told: "This bread is the sacrifice of the Lord's body, which he offered himself to God the Father for us on the cross." The Lord could simply have said, "Take, eat, in remembrance of me," or "Take, eat; this is my memorial," unless he had wished to express the mystery of his death and of our redemption, and to commend to his Church the sacrament of his body and blood. So that he might do this, he said, "Take, eat; this is my body, which is broken for you." This is the same as if he had said: "This is the sacrament of my body, which shortly after will die for you on the cross. This is the sacrifice of my body. This is the Lamb of God, who will be slain for you. This is the new Passover, which will be offered in my body for you. This is the memorial of my body, which will be given for you."

units.la: Hæc omnia de pane hoc cœnæ dominicæ re ctissimè prædicari possunt. Et istis prædicatis aliter facienda est ecclesia, ut discat neq; superstitiosè cum Papistis, neq; irreligiosè cum carnalibus Corinthijs & Capernaitis, sed pie & vtiliter de pane hoc dominifentire ac loqui, sensu & intellectu uidelicet sacramentis ac mysterijs conuenienti.
units.tr: All of this can be rightly preached about this bread of the Lord's supper. And once these things have been preached, the Church must be taught otherwise, so that she learns to think and speak about this bread of the Lord neither superstitiously, as the Papists do, nor irreligiously, as the carnal Corinthians and Capernaites did, but piously and profitably, with a sense and understanding suited to sacraments and mysteries.

units.la: HOC est corpus meum, inquit, quod pro uobis frangitur.) Referunt aliqui uerbum frangendi ad panem cœnæ dominicæ, quasi dicat: Hic panis meum corpus est, quipro uobis iam frangitur. Verùm panis ille frangitur quidem, at non illius, sed corporis sui fracturam, id est, mortem, quam in Ioanne templi destructione uocauit, tanquam mysterium fide amplectendum commendat, cum dicit: Hoc est corpus meum quod pro uobis frangitur . Poterat dicere, quod pro uobis tradetur & occidetur. Verùm ut accommodaret se sacramentali fractioni panis dixit: quod pro uobis frangitur.
units.tr: "This is my body," he says, "which is broken for you." Some refer the word "broken" to the bread of the Lord's supper, as if he said: "This bread is my body, which is now broken for you." But that bread is indeed broken, yet not as his body; rather, he commends to faith, as a mystery to be embraced, the breaking of his own body, that is, his death, which he called the destruction of the temple in John, when he says, "This is my body which is broken for you." He could have said, "which is handed over and killed for you." But to accommodate himself to the sacramental breaking of the bread, he said, "which is broken for you."

units.la: Vt enim panis dum frangitur, pro illis frangitur, quibus ad edendum distribuitur, propterea quod nisi trangatur, distribui & edi nequit, sic corpus domini, panis uiuus de cœlo missus ut cibus noster fieret, in cruce pro nobis est fractum, id est, occisum , id quod alijs uerbis expressit dominus ipse, cum dixit: Nisi granum frumenti cadës in terrâ mortuû fuerit, ipsum solum manet, &c. Hactenus ergo fractû, p nobis est in cruce corpus domini, quatenus pro nobis est morti datum, ut ipsius oblatione à peccato & morte redimeretur ac uiuificaremur.
units.tr: For just as the bread, while it is broken, is broken for those to whom it is distributed for eating, because unless it were broken it could not be distributed and eaten, so the body of the Lord, the living bread sent down from heaven to become our food, was broken for us on the cross, that is, slain. The Lord himself expressed this in other words when he said: "Unless a grain of wheat falls into the earth and dies, it remains alone," etc. So the body of the Lord was broken for us on the cross, insofar as it was given over to death for us, so that by its offering we might be redeemed from sin and death and made alive.

units.la: Nec impedit quod in præsenti legitur, quod pro vobis frangitur, cum tamen non in cœna frangeretur, sed sequenti demum die frangendum esset in cruce. In Græco quidem legitur <bl>κλώμενον</bl>, id est, quod frangitur, sicut & in Luca <bl>διδόμενον</bl>. i. qd datur. Certû tamè est, Seruatorem nostrum nô esse Græce, sed Syriace loquutum, quæ lingua non potest dicere in præsenti frangitur, aut, datur, sed pro præsenti utitur, vel præterito, vel futuro, vt, <bl>הוא גופי אשר</bl>, <bl>בעבורכם ינתן</bl>, id est, hoc corpus meum quod pro vobis dabitur, aut <bl>ישבר</bl>, id est, frangetur, aut participio præterito <bl>נתרך</bl>, id est, datum, vel <bl>שבור</bl>, id est fractum . Quoniam sacramentum instituebat, cuius vsus post mortem ipsius seruiret ecclesiæ, verosimile est dixisse eû ad hunc modum, <bl>הוא גופי</bl>, vel, <bl>הוא גמשי</bl>, id est, hoc corpus meum, <bl>בעבורכם שבור</bl>, id est, pro vobis fractum . Et huic respondere videtur Græcum <bl>κλώμενον</bl>. Sunt quidem hæc minuta, & tamè ne scio quomodo fiat, vt qui sanctæ linguæ sunt prorsus ignari, in uerbis domini subinde hallucinentur, & pro rebus parerfis ac minutis acerbè digladientur.
units.tr: Nor does it count against this that the present tense is read, "which is broken for you," when yet it was not broken at the supper but was to be broken on the cross the following day. In Greek indeed it reads κλώμενον [klōmenon], that is, "which is broken," just as in Luke διδόμενον [didomenon], that is, "which is given." It is certain, however, that our Saviour did not speak Greek but Syriac, a language which cannot say "is broken" or "is given" in the present, but uses the present for the past or the future. So he may have said הוא גופי אשר בעבורכם ינתן [hu gufi asher be'avurkhem yittën], that is, "This is my body which will be given for you," or ישבר [yishbor], that is, "will be broken," or the past participle נתרך [nitrakh], that is, "given," or שבור [shavur], that is, "broken." Since he was instituting a sacrament whose use would serve the Church after his death, it is likely that he said it in this way: הוא גופי [hu gufi], or הוא גשמי [hu gashmi], that is, "This is my body," בעבורכם שבור [be'avurkhem shavur], that is, "broken for you." And the Greek κλώμενον seems to answer to this. These are indeed small points, yet I do not know how it happens that those who are utterly ignorant of the holy tongues keep going astray in the words of the Lord, and fiercely contend over matters that are trivial and of little account.

units.la: HOC poculû, Nouû testamentû est in meo sanguine, inquit.) Exponit mysterium poculi. Vtrobiq; aût & de pane & de poculo sacramentaliter loqtur, Sacramento externo tribues, qd est ipsius rei. In Math. dicit: Hic est enim sanguis meus, qest Noui test. qui pro multis effunditur in remissionè peccatorû. Sic & Marc. nisi qd illud, in remissionè peccatorum, omisit, Lucas &Paul. sic recitât. Hoc poculû Nouû test. est in meo sanguine, &Lucas addit, qui pro vobis effunditur, quod Paul. nô habet. Viderint hic, q p verbis in ecclesia digladiatur. Nô sunt eadé verba vbiq; posita ab Euâgelistis & Apostolo. Et tamè nemo vsq; adeò insanit, vt putet Christû, sic esse de poculo loquutum, vt omnia hæc verba protulerit, quæ à Matth. Marc. Luc. & Paulo recitantur. Si dixit: Hic est sanguis meus, q est Noui test. quorsum adiecisset: Hoc poculum Nouum test. est in meo sanguine . Si uero dixit: Hoc poculû Nouû test. est in meo sanguine, nulla erat ratio ut adijceret: Hic est sanguis meus, qui est Noui testamêti. Vtrumuis dixerit, alterû non dixit. Quare necesse est, ut sensus utrobiq; sit idem, & alterû per alterû uelut exponatur. Quod Matt. Ebraicè scripsit, הוא דמי הברית החדשה. i. Hic est sanguis meus Noui testamenti, id Lucas & Paulus expo suif se uidentur ad hûc modû. Hoc poculum Nouû testamentûest in meo sanguine. Ergo idem est poculum hoc esse sanguinem Christi, quod est, esse Nouum testamentû in sanguine Christi. Et exi stimo Lucâ hoc accepisse à Paulo, ut sensum uerborû Christi hoc pacto exponeret. Quêadmodû igitur poculû domini ob id Nouum test. uocatur, quod sacramêtû est Noui testamenti, ita etiâ sanguis Christi propterea uocatur, quod sacramentû est sanguinis Christi. Et sicut Nouum testamentum confirmatû est sanguine Christi in cruce pro peccatis nostris effuso effusio, ita sanguis Christi, sanguis Noui testamenti dicitur, ad differentiam pecuini sangui nis, in quo Veteris erat testamenti confirmatio, qua de re videre licet Ebr. 9. Dicit itaque: Hoc poculum Nouum testamentum est in MEO sanguine, quasi dicat: Hactenus Veteris testamenti confirmatio fuit in sanguine pecudum, iam Nouum confirmabitur in MEO sanguine, cuius sacramentum hoc vobis poculo instituo, commendo, ac trado.
units.tr: "This cup is the New Testament in my blood," he says. He explains the mystery of the cup. In both places he speaks sacramentally of both the bread and the cup; you will attribute to the external sign what belongs to the thing itself. In Matthew he says: "For this is my blood of the New Testament, which is poured out for many for the remission of sins." Mark does the same, except that he omits "for the remission of sins." Luke and Paul recite it thus: "This cup is the New Testament in my blood." Luke adds "which is poured out for you," which Paul does not have. Let them see how people quarrel in the Church over words. The words are not the same everywhere in the Evangelists and the Apostle. Yet no one is so mad as to think that Christ spoke about the cup in such a way that he uttered all the words recited by Matthew, Mark, Luke and Paul. If he said, "This is my blood, which is of the New Testament," why would he add, "This cup is the New Testament in my blood"? And if he said, "This cup is the New Testament in my blood," there was no reason for him to add, "This is my blood, which is of the New Testament." Whichever he said, he did not say the other. So it is necessary that the sense be the same in both, and that one be explained through the other. What Matthew wrote in Hebrew, הוא דמי הברית החדשה [hu demi ha-berit ha-ḥadashah], that is, "This is my blood of the new covenant," Luke and Paul seem to explain in this way: "This cup is the New Testament in my blood." Therefore, that this cup is the blood of Christ is the same as saying that the New Testament is in the blood of Christ. I think Luke received this from Paul, so as to explain the sense of Christ's words in this way. Just as the Lord's cup is called the New Testament because it is a sacrament of the New Testament, so also Christ's blood is called such because it is a sacrament of Christ's blood. And just as the New Testament was confirmed by the blood of Christ, poured out on the cross for our sins, so Christ's blood is called the blood of the New Testament, in contrast to the blood of animals, in which the Old Testament was confirmed. On this matter see Ebr. 9. He therefore says: "This cup is the New Testament in MY blood," as if to say: "Hitherto the Old Testament was confirmed in the blood of animals; now the New will be confirmed in MY blood, the sacrament of which I institute, commend and hand over to you in this cup."

units.la: HOC poculum, inquit, Nouum testamentum est in MEO sanguine.) Ergo Nouum testamentum est poculum hoc a domino traditum? Sacramentaliter est, realiter non est. Testamentum extrema est moriturivoluntas, qua certis amicis legatur hereditas, quae legatio tum demum valet, quando testamentum morte testatoris confirmatur. Haec communis est testamenti ratio et conditio. In sacris scripturis accipitur vox בריתquam vertunt testamentum pro foedere, quod inijt cum populo suo dominus. Et quoniam duplex est illius dispensatio, prior sub Mose seruilis, carnalis, vmbratilis, ac figuralis, tradita Israeli secundum carnem, posterior vero sub Christo libera, spiritualis, et veritatis habens adimpletionem: Vocata est prior Vetus, posterior Nouum testamentum, cuius gratiam dominus ipse Hieremiae 31. expressit, et a priori separauit dicens: Ecce dies venient dicit dominus, et confirmabo super domum Israel, et super domum Iehudah testamentum Nouum, non secundum testamentum quod fe-ci patribus eorum in die, qua apprehendi manum eorum, vt educerem eos e terra Aegypti. Quoniam ipsi non permanserunt in testamento meo, et ego neglexi eos dicit dominus. Hoc est aute testamentum quod disponam domui Israel post dies illos dicit dominus, dabo leges meas in mentem eorum, et in corda eorum inscribam eas, et ero eis in Deum, et ipsi erunt mihi in populum. Et non docebit quisque proximum suum, ac fratre suum dicens, cognosce dominum, quoniam omnes cognoscet me, a minore usque ad maiorem, quia propicius ero iniquitatis eorum, et peccatorum ipsorum non recordabor. Haec ibi quae in Epistola ad Ebr. ca. 8. et 10. de gratia Noui testamenti citantur. Huius mediator est, non Moses, sed Christus, huius doctrina non est vetus lex, sed nouum Euangelium, non litera, sed spiritu, huius sacramenta sunt, non circumcisio carnis et Pascha vetus, sed lauacrum regenerationis, et quod hic sub pane et poculo, ad Noui hominis alimentum instituitur. Hanc igitur testamenti innouatione expressurus dominus, non dicit: Hoc poculum testamentum Dei, vel, testamentum meum, sed, Hoc poculum est testamentum NOVVM est, qua voce omnino Vetus abrogauit, et animos discipulorum suorum ad Nouam, quae aderat, caelestis gratiae dispensationem dirigebat, et ab obseruantia Veteris ac legalis auoca bat. Cogitemus igitur, quoties de hoc poculo domini bibimus, esse nos filios, haeredes, consortes, et poculum, non Veteris, sed Noui testi.
units.tr: THIS cup, he says, is the New Testament in MY blood. Is this cup, then, handed over by the Lord, the New Testament? It is so sacramentally, but not really. A testament is the last will of a dying man, by which an inheritance is bequeathed to certain friends. That bequest takes effect only when the testament is confirmed by the testator's death. This is the common nature and condition of a testament. In the Holy Scriptures the word בריתberith [covenant] is used, which they render "testament" for the covenant the Lord made with his people. Since that dispensation is twofold, the former under Moses servile, carnal, shadowy and figurative, given to Israel according to the flesh, and the latter under Christ free, spiritual, and having the fulfilment of truth, the former is called the Old Testament and the latter the New. The Lord himself expressed this grace in Jeremiah 31 and set it apart from the former, saying: "Behold, the days come, says the Lord, and I will make a New Testament with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah, not according to the testament that I made with their fathers in the day that I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt, because they did not continue in my testament, and I disregarded them, says the Lord. But this is the testament that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, says the Lord: I will put my laws in their mind and write them in their hearts, and I will be their God, and they shall be my people. And no one shall teach his neighbour or his brother, saying, Know the Lord, for all shall know me, from the least to the greatest, because I will be merciful to their iniquities and will not remember their sins." These are the words cited in the Epistle to the Hebrews, chapters 8 and 10, concerning the grace of the New Testament. Its mediator is not Moses but Christ; its doctrine is not the old law but the new Gospel, not the letter but the Spirit; its sacraments are not the circumcision of the flesh and the old Passover, but the washing of regeneration and that which is here instituted under the bread and the cup for the nourishment of the new man. Therefore, intending to express this renewal of the covenant, the Lord does not say, "This cup is the testament of God," or "my testament," but "This cup is the NEW testament," a word which entirely abrogates the Old and directed the minds of his disciples to the new dispensation of heavenly grace that was now present, and called them away from the observance of the Old and of the law. Let us therefore consider that, as often as we drink of this cup of the Lord, we are sons, heirs and partners, and that the cup is of the New, not the Old, testament.

units.la: Et vt huius admoneamur optarim obtinere in ecclesia, vt communicaturi de hoc sacramento, ad communionem se Noui testamenti accedere dicant. Non est otiosum, quod non modo ipsa gratia per Christum dispensata, sed et doctrina illius, et codex Euangelicus et Apostolicus, et poculum mysticum, Noui testamenti elogio, vocantur et ornantur.
units.tr: And that we may be reminded of this, I wish it were the custom in the Church that those who are about to communicate in this sacrament should say that they approach the communion of the New Testament. It is not idle that not only the grace itself dispensed through Christ, but also his doctrine, the Gospel and Apostolic writings, and the mystical cup are called and adorned with the title of the New Testament.

units.la: IN MEO sanguine, inquit.) Emphasis est in pronomine MEO. Dicit Nouum testamentum esse in SVO sanguine, non in sanguine pecorum. Dicis, quomodo testamentum est in sanguine, cum fit remissio peccatorum? Audi Apostolum Ebr. 9. Vbi testamentum est, inquit, mors necesse est intercedat testatoris. Testamentum enim in mortuis confirmatum est. Alioqui nodum valet, dum viuit qui testatus est. Vnde nec primum sine sanguine dedicatum fuit. Cum enim Moses omne mandatum iuxta legem exposuisset omni populo, sumpto sanguine vitulorum et hircorum, cum aqua et lana coccinea, et hyssopo, simul et ipsum librum et totum populum aspersit dicens: Hic est sanguis testamenti quod mandauit vobis Deus. Insuper autem et tabernaculum, et omnia vasa ministerij sanguine cosimiliter aspergebat. Et omnia fere secundum legem sanguine purifi cantur, et absq; sanguinis effusione non fit remissio. Itaq; necesse est vt exemplaria quidem eorum quae sunt in coelis, hisce rebus purificetur ipsa vero coelestia potioribus, quam haec sint victimis mundentur, &c. quibus verbis satis indicatur, hactenus Nouum testamentum esse in sanguine Christi, quatenus Vetus fuit in sanguine vitulorum et hircorum, ratione videlicet dedicationis et confirmationis, propterea quod testamentum hoc, morte testatoris est confirmatum, eaq; non vulgari, sed cruenta, qualem conueniebat esse victimae pro peccatis totius mundi oblatae. Vnde et non simpliciter dixit: Hoc poculum Nouum testamentum est in morte mea, sed, in sanguine meo.
