Neq; sic tatu, sed adiecit, qui effundetur, et vt rationem effusionis huius exprimeret, subiecit, pro vobis et multis in remissionem peccatorum. Loquitur ipse agnus Dei, mediator inter Deum et homines, de morte sua, qua erat tanqua victima Deo patri immolanda pro totius mundi peccatis, in cruce subiturus, ac testamentu Nouum confirmatu rus. Hac ratione dicit illud esse in suo sanguine ad remissionem peccatorum effundendo.
units.tr: "IN MY blood," he says. The emphasis lies on the pronoun MY. He says the New Testament is in HIS OWN blood, not in the blood of beasts. You ask, how is a testament in blood, since it effects the remission of sins? Hear the Apostle in Hebrews 9: "Where there is a testament, the death of the testator must necessarily intervene. For a testament is confirmed over the dead; otherwise it has no force while the one who made it lives. Hence not even the first was dedicated without blood. For when Moses had set out every commandment according to the law to all the people, taking the blood of calves and goats, with water, scarlet wool and hyssop, he sprinkled both the book itself and all the people, saying, This is the blood of the testament which God has commanded you. Moreover, he likewise sprinkled the tabernacle and all the vessels of the ministry with blood. And almost all things are purified with blood according to the law, and without shedding of blood there is no remission. Therefore it is necessary that the copies of the things in heaven be purified with these things, but the heavenly things themselves with better sacrifices than these," and so on. By these words it is sufficiently indicated that the New Testament is in the blood of Christ in the same way as the Old was in the blood of calves and goats, namely by way of dedication and confirmation, because this testament was confirmed by the death of the testator, and that by a death not ordinary but bloody, such as was fitting for the victim offered for the sins of the whole world. Hence he did not simply say, "This cup is the New Testament in my death," but "in my blood." Nor did he stop there, but added, "which shall be poured out," and to express the reason for this pouring out he added, "for you and for many, for the remission of sins." The Lamb of God himself, the mediator between God and men, speaks of his death, by which he was to undergo the cross as a victim to be offered to God the Father for the sins of the whole world, and by which he was to confirm the New Testament. For this reason he says that it is in his blood, poured out for the remission of sins.

units.la: Videmus itaq;, quare separatim de hoc poculo dixerit, esse illud Nouum testamentum in suo sanguine, et q; friuola fit eorum ratio, qui dicut: Et in corpore sanguis est, ideoq; laici non priuantur sanguine Christi, qui sub vna tantum specie comunicant, et corpus domini accipiunt. At Christus instituit sacramentum sanguinis sui, non quatenus illum habebat adhuc in corpore viuo, sed quatenus erat illi in cruce pro peccatis nostris moriedo effusurus. Aperitur nobis hic intellectus, quomodo sanguini Christi in literis Apostolic. tribuatur, q; sit propitiatio
units.tr: We see, therefore, why he spoke of this cup separately, saying that it is the New Testament in his blood, and how futile is the reasoning of those who say: "Blood is also in the body, and therefore the laity are not deprived of the blood of Christ, who communicate under one kind only and receive the body of the Lord." But Christ instituted the sacrament of his blood not as he then had it in his living body, but as he was about to pour it out on the cross, dying for our sins. Here the meaning is revealed to us of how the blood of Christ is ascribed in the Apostolic writings to the fact that it is propitiation

units.la: {ε} Ebr. 9.
units.tr: {ε} Heb. 9.

units.la: propitiatio pro peccatis nostris, Ro.3. quod in illo iustificemur, Ro.5. redemptionem habeamus: Eph.1. pacificemur: Coloss.1. fiduciam acquirimus ad introitum sanctorum: Ebr. 10. sanctificemur: Ebr. 13. ab omni peccato emundemur. 1.Ioan. 1. & stolas nostras dealbemus: Apoc. 7. Omnium horum ratio est, quod sanguis Christi, sanguis est Noui testamenti, sanguis mediatoris pro peccatis nostris in cruce effusus. Sed pergamus.
units.tr: propitiation for our sins (Rom. 3); that in him we are justified (Rom. 5); that we have redemption (Eph. 1); that we are reconciled (Col. 1); that we gain confidence to enter into the holy places (Heb. 10); that we are sanctified (Heb. 13); that we are cleansed from all sin (1 John 1); and that we whiten our robes (Rev. 7). The reason for all of these is that the blood of Christ is the blood of the New Testament, the blood of the mediator, poured out on the cross for our sins. But let us go on.

units.la: Diximus supra duas esse in hac causa domini nicæ institutionis partes, unâ, quid fecerit do minus, altera, quid nos facere iusserit. De priori hactenus, iam de posteriori videamus. Ea sic proponitur. Hoc facite in mei rememoratione. Manifesta verba. Nihil manifestius dici potuit. Vnde nec Apostoli vel verbulo desensu institutionis huius interrogasse legûtur. de sacramentalibus locutionibus clamat nônulli: Manifestum verbum, manifestū verbum. Hic sacramentali ac mystico verbo mādatū subijci-tur omnino ad nos pertinens, & nullo mystico inuolucro obscurum. Hoc, inquit, facite ad mei rememorationem. Haud opus est operosa indagatione. Manifestum est quid nos, manifestum ad quid facere iubeat. Hoc facite inquit. Non dicit: Hoc sacrificate. Non enim nos facere voluit, quod ipse ,p nobis in cruce erat facturus, sed quod iam fecerat. Non autem sacrificauerat, sed in cruce demum semetipsum erat Deo patri sacrificaturus. Non dicit: Hoc dicite, & mutate panem in corpus meum, sed, hoc facite. Neq; dicit: Hoc porro faciam, neq; enim de re aliqua loquitur, quæ nobis sit præstitu impossibilis, ideoq; non à nobis, sed ab ipso fieri debeat. Si mutasset ipse panem in corpus, & vinum in sanguinem suum, eamq; mutatione porrò in ecclesiā sua fieri voluisset, nô dixisset: Hoc facite, sed, Hoc porrò faciâ. Cum ergo dicit: Hoc facite, satis significat se loqui de opere quod non ipse sit facturus, sed quod à nobis fieri debeat, & possit etiam. Quod autem illud sit, patet ex præcedentibus, quæ in duo membra diuidi ac separari possunt, ita vt vnum ipsi domino, alterum discipulis compe tat. Primum est, quod Noui testamenti sacramentum est institutum. Hæc institutio pertinet ád authoritatē domini, non ad discipulos. Non iubet ergo vt sacramentum instituant & faciant. Verbum faciendi non est hic referendum ad opus, quod domini ipsius est, & semel ab ipso factum, nullam iterationem requirit. Testatoris est condere testamentum, non haeredum. Et semel conditum testamentum, vt annihilandum non est, ita nec mutandum nec iterandum. Alterum est, quod panem ab ipso fractum acceperunt & comederunt, & poculum consimiliter ab ipso traditum biberunt. Iam cum pronomen Hoc, ad institutionem sacramêti referri nequeat, manifestum est, referendum esse ad id quod ipsi discipuli iam fecerant, & porrò facere debebant, vt quod dicit, hoc facite, perinde sit, ac si dicat: Quod iam facitis de pane hoc communiter edentes, & de poculo illo bibētes, hoc eadem communicatione in posterum communiter inter vos facite.
units.tr: We said above that in this matter of the Lord's Supper there are two parts: one, what the Lord did; the other, what he commanded us to do. We have discussed the former so far; now let us look at the latter. It is set forth thus: "Do this in remembrance of me." The words are plain; nothing plainer could be said. Hence we read that not even the Apostles asked a single word about the meaning of this institution. Some cry out about sacramental expressions, "The word is plain, the word is plain." Here a command wholly pertaining to us is subjoined in a sacramental and mystical word, and it is not obscured by any mystical wrapping. "This," he says, "do in remembrance of me." There is no need for laborious investigation: it is clear what he bids us do, and clear for what purpose. "Do this," he says. He does not say, "Sacrifice this." For he did not want us to do what he himself was to do on the cross, but what he had already done. He had not sacrificed, but was to sacrifice himself to God the Father on the cross at last. He does not say, "Say this, and change the bread into my body," but "do this." Nor does he say, "I will do this hereafter," for he is not speaking of some matter that is impossible for us, and which therefore ought to be done not by us but by him. If he himself had changed the bread into his body and the wine into his blood, and had wished that change to take place thereafter in his Church, he would not have said, "Do this," but "I will do this hereafter." Therefore, when he says "Do this," he sufficiently indicates that he is speaking of a work which he himself will not do, but which ought to be done by us, and can be done. What that work is is clear from what precedes, which can be divided into two members and separated, so that one belongs to the Lord himself and the other to the disciples. The first is that he instituted the sacrament of the New Testament. This institution pertains to the authority of the Lord, not to the disciples. Therefore he does not command them to institute and make the sacrament. The verb "do" is not to be referred here to a work that belongs to the Lord himself and, once done by him, requires no repetition. It belongs to the testator to make the testament, not to the heirs; and once a testament is made, it is not to be annulled, nor changed, nor repeated. The second is that they took the bread broken by him and ate it, and likewise drank the cup handed to them by him. Now since the pronoun "this" cannot be referred to the institution of the sacrament, it is clear that it refers to what the disciples themselves had already done and were to continue doing. So that when he says "do this," it is as if he said: "What you now do, eating this bread together in common and drinking from that cup, do this same communal thing among yourselves in the future."

units.la: Quemadmodum in Marco animaduertere licet, tum demum dixit: Hic est sanguis meus Noui testamenti, &, hoc facite quotiescunque biberitis in mei rememorationem, cum iam de tradito ipsis poculo bibissent omnes. Nec dubium est cõsimili ordine dictum esse de pane, vbi illum comederat. Hoc est corpus meū, quod pro vobis frangitur. Hoc facite in mei rememorationem. Illa, hoc est corpus meum, quod pro vobis traditur, &: Hoc poculum Noùum testamentum est in meo sanguine, ad institutionem sacramenti pertinent, quare ad ea non est referendum quod dicit: Hoc facite. Reliquum ergo est, vt referatur ad id quod iâ discipuli fecerant, traditum panem comedentes, & de tradito poculo bibentes. Vnde & dixit: Hoc facite quotiescunq; biberitis, in mei rememorationē. Et Apostolus cū dicit: Quotiescunq; comederitis panem hunc, & de poculo hoc biberitis, mortem domini annuncia tis, & quæ sequuntur satis exprimit quo sensu dictum sit à domino, Hoc facite. Tali uideli cet: Hunc panem cum gratiarum actione inter vos frangite & comedite, & hoc poculum communiter omnes bibite.
units.tr: As we may observe in Mark, he said, "This is my blood of the New Testament," and "Do this, as often as you drink, in remembrance of me," only after all of them had drunk from the cup handed to them. There is no doubt that he spoke in the same order about the bread, when he had eaten it: "This is my body, which is broken for you. Do this in remembrance of me." The words "This is my body, which is given for you" and "This cup is the New Testament in my blood" belong to the institution of the sacrament, so "Do this" does not refer to them. It remains, then, that it refers to what the disciples had already done, eating the bread that was handed to them and drinking from the cup that was handed to them. Hence he also said, "Do this, as often as you drink, in remembrance of me." And when the Apostle says, "As often as you eat this bread and drink this cup, you proclaim the Lord's death," and what follows, he sufficiently expresses in what sense the Lord said "Do this." It means this: break and eat this bread among you with thanksgiving, and drink this cup together, all of you.

units.la: Nisi hoc mandasset, non esset authenticum quicquid ad imitationem illius humana præsumptio instituisset. Authoritate mandati huius sacramentū hoc, corporis ac sanguinis domini celebramus & vsurpamus in ecclesia. Et intellexerunt apostoli, nó esse hoc ipsis tantū, sed simul & ecclesiæ fidelium traditū à domino, quare & ecclesijs illud fideliter tradiderūt. Ego accepi à domino, inquit, quod & tradidi vobis. Intellexerunt Apostoli institutum esse à domino nouum Noui testamenti pascha, cui ius communicatio non est ad ipsos tantū, sed & ad omnem fidelium multitudinem, nô minus quàm vetus pascha ad multitudinē Israëlis, pertineat. Quare nó sunt argutati ad hunc modū: Nobis apostolis dedit dominus panem hunc & poculū, ac iussit, vt quod fecit ipse & nos faciamus. Non dedit alijs, nec dixit, tradite hæc alijs, sed, Hoc facite, ad quem modū nō stra hac ætate Sophistæ nônulli argutati sunt, nó pertinere hoc sacramêtū ad laicos fideles, sed ad solos sacerdotes, tāquā Apostolorū suc cessores. Quod autem vna species in vsu est lai cis, esse hoc ex permissu, liberalitate & gratia ecclesiæ, tanquē abesse, vt de negata communione calicis conqueri debeant, vt magis agē dæ sint ecclesiæ gratię pro communione corporis. Sunt hæc à mente tam Christi quàm Apostolorum omnium alienissima, & nonnisi magnum & impudentissimum sacrilegium spirantia. Quemadmodum ipsius Testamenti consors vniuersa est ecclesiæ Christi multitudo, ita consors est & sacramenti huius, cuius poculum Nouum est testamentum à domino vocatum, sic vt inter ministros verbi, & plebem bem fidelium, nihil in hac communicatione mysteriorum Christi sit discriminis, nisi quod illi traditum à domino sacramentum multitudini fidelium ex officia dispensant, sicut & canunt, quibus sic congruit, ut sumant & dent cæteris.
units.tr: Unless he had commanded this, whatever human presumption had instituted in imitation of it would not be authentic. By the authority of this command we celebrate and use this sacrament of the body and blood of the Lord in the Church. And the apostles understood that this was handed down by the Lord not only to themselves but at the same time to the congregations of the faithful, and so they faithfully handed it on to the congregations as well. "I received from the Lord," he says, "what I also handed on to you." The apostles understood that the new Passover of the New Testament had been instituted by the Lord, and that the right to share in it belongs not only to themselves but to the whole multitude of the faithful, no less than the old Passover pertained to the whole multitude of Israel. Therefore they did not argue in this way: "The Lord gave this bread and cup to us apostles, and ordered that we do what he himself did." He did not give it to others, nor did he say, "Pass these on to others," but "Do this." In the same way, in our own age some Sophists have argued that this sacrament does not pertain to the faithful laity but only to priests, as successors of the Apostles. As for the fact that the laity use only one kind, they say this is by permission, liberality and grace of the Church; so far from having reason to complain of the denial of the cup, they ought rather to give thanks to the Church for the communion of the body. These claims are most alien to the mind of Christ and of all the Apostles, and they breathe nothing but great and shameless sacrilege. Just as the whole multitude of the Church of Christ shares in the Testament itself, so it shares in this sacrament, whose cup the Lord called the New Testament. Thus, between the ministers of the Word and the common people of the faithful, there is no distinction in this sharing of the mysteries of Christ, except that the ministers faithfully dispense to the multitude of the faithful the sacrament handed down by the Lord, just as they also sing, and since they are fitted for this, they take and give to the others.

units.la: Legant saltem Chrysostomum super posteriorem ad Corinthios, humil. 18. vbi sic dicit: Est autem vbi nihil differt sacerdos à subdito. Vt quando fruendum est tremendis mysterijs. Similiter enim omnes vt illa percipiamus digni habemur. Non sicut in veteri lege, partem quidem sacerdos edebat, partem autem populus, & non licebat populo participem esse eorum, quorum particeps erat sacerdos, sed nunc non sic, verum omnibus unum corpus proponitur, & POCVLVM VNVM.
units.tr: At least let them read Chrysostom on the second letter to the Corinthians, homily 18, where he says: "There are times when the priest does not differ from the one under him, as when the awesome mysteries are to be enjoyed. For in the same way we are all deemed worthy to receive them. It is not as in the old law, where the priest ate one part and the people another, and the people were not allowed to share in those things of which the priest partook. But now it is not so; rather one body is set before all, and ONE CUP."

units.la: Hæ ille. Et Theophylactus: Præsertim, inquit cum tremendus hic calix pari conditione traditus. Si pro solis Apostolis traditum esset in cruce dominicum corpus & sanguis illius effusus, non immeritò panem hunc & calicem solis illis traditum esse sentiremus. Iam vero cum non pro illis tantum, sed & reliquis fidelibus omnibus sit mortuus domin, & Matthæus palam dicat: qui pro multis effunditur in remissionem peccatorum, manifestum est, & sacramentum hoc corporis ac sanguinis domini, non ad solos Apostolos, sed post illos ad omnes quoque pertinere fideles & redemptos. Cogor hac de re admonere, propter impudentes Sophistas, qui rem manifestum ausi sunt negare, & dominicam institutionem ad solos referre sacerdotes.
units.tr: So he. And Theophylact: "Especially," he says, "since this awesome cup is handed over on equal terms. If the Lord's body had been given up on the cross and his blood shed for the Apostles alone, we would rightly judge that this bread and cup were handed over to them alone. But since the Lord died not for them alone but for all the other faithful as well, and Matthew plainly says, 'which is poured out for many for the forgiveness of sins,' it is clear that this sacrament of the body and blood of the Lord pertains not only to the Apostles but after them to all the faithful and redeemed as well." I am compelled to say this on this matter, because of the shameless Sophists, who have dared to deny what is manifest, and to refer the Lord's institution to priests alone.

units.la: Sed hactenus de eo quid nos facere iusserit, dicens: Hoc facite. Iam de eo uidedu est, ad quid nos hoc facere uelit. Non est ut diuinet ac statuat hic humana præsumptio: nec est vlla contentiosis hominibus contendendi ac disceptandi relicta occasio. Ipse qui sacramentum hoc instituit, non modo quid, sed & ad quid facere debeamus expressit. Non dixit autem: Hoc facite in mei oblationem, id quod se Papistæ quotidie facere iactant. Nec dixit: Hoc facite in remissionem peccatorum uestrorum & aliorum, quo sensu Missatores suâ missam & nonnulli cœnam dominicam fidelibus commendant, sed hoc facite in mei rememorationem. Quasi dicat: Hactenus celebraustis in veteri Pascate transitus angelici & agni in Ægypto mactati memoriam, donec Vetus testamentum durauit. Iam illo finito, in posterum non edetis agnum typicum, sed facietis hoc quod modo fecistis in mei rememorationem. Hoc erit memoriale sacramentum Noui testamenti, quo mortis meæ, ac redemptionis uestræ memoriā in cordib. uestris communi ac solenni ritu alatis, ac gratiam hac animis gratis ample stamini, ac bene collocetis. Chrysostomus super Matthæum hom. 83. hæc verba tali paraphra si exponit dices: Nā sicut illud (loquitur de agno pascatis) in rememorationem miraculorum, quę in Ægypto patres vestri viderūt, facieba-
units.tr: So far we have considered what he ordered us to do when he said "Do this." Now we must consider for what purpose he wishes us to do it. Human presumption should not guess or decide this, and no occasion is left for quarrelsome people to contend and dispute. He who instituted this sacrament has expressed not only what we ought to do but also for what purpose. He did not say, "Do this as an offering of me," which the Papists daily boast that they do. Nor did he say, "Do this for the forgiveness of your sins and of others," in which sense the Missa-mongers commend their mass, and some commend the Lord's Supper to the faithful. Rather he said, "Do this in remembrance of me." As if he said: Hitherto you have celebrated in the old Passover the memory of the angel's passing over and of the lamb slain in Egypt, as long as the Old Testament endured. Now that it is finished, from now on you will not eat the typical lamb, but you will do what you have just done, in remembrance of me. This will be the memorial sacrament of the New Testament, by which you will nourish the memory of my death and of your redemption in your hearts, in a common and solemn rite, and will freely and well store up grace in your minds. Chrysostom, in his eighty-third homily on Matthew, explains these words in this paraphrase, saying: "For just as that (he speaks of the Passover lamb) you did in remembrance of the miracles which your fathers saw in Egypt, so do this in me, make remembrance, etc.

units.la: tis, sic & hoc in me, facite rememorationem, &c. Et quemadmodum Moses, hoc æternum memoriale vobis erit, dicebat, sic & ipse, in mei, ait, rememorationem donec veniam. hoc facite.
units.tr: And just as Moses said, 'This will be an everlasting memorial for you,' so he himself, says, 'in my remembrance until I come, do this.'

units.la: Et Augustinus cōtra Faustum Manichæum libro. 20. cap. 21. Sacramentum hoc, sacramentum memoriæ uocat dicens: Huius sacrificij caro & sanguis ante aduentum Christi per uictimas similitudinum promittebatur, in passione Christi per ipsam ueritatem reddebatur, post ascensum Christi, per sacramentum memoriæ celebratur. Hæc ille. Libera esset ecclesia à uarijs & multis superstitionibus, quæstionibus, & contentionibus, si quorum officium est docere alios à simplicitate hac dominici mandati nunquam recessissent.
units.tr: And Augustine, against Faustus the Manichaean, book 20, chapter 21, calls this sacrament a sacrament of remembrance, saying: "The flesh and blood of this sacrifice were promised before the coming of Christ through the victims of likenesses; in the passion of Christ they were rendered through the truth itself; after the ascension of Christ they are celebrated through the sacrament of remembrance." So he. The Church would be free of many and various superstitions, questions and contentions, if those whose office is to teach others had never departed from this simplicity of the Lord's command.

units.la: Sed dicet hic quisquam: Ergo nihil aliud facimus in cœna dominica, quàm quod panem edimus, & uinum bibimus, & hoc facientes, domini recordamur? Respondeo. Panem quidem edimus, & uinum bibimus, uerum non ut uulgarem corporis cibum ac potum, sed ut panem ac poculum domini, sicuti nominatur ab Apostolo, & à prisicis patribus, ut panem ac poculum sanctificatum, sicut appellatur à Cyriano, ut sacramentum corporis ac sanguinis domini, in quibus, teste Augustino, aliud uidetur & aliud intelligitur, ut symbola ac mysteria gratiæ noui testamenti, quæ de mensa domini accipientes, non corporis tantum, sed & fidei ore manducamus & bibimus, & hoc facientes mortem domini cum gratiarum actio ne annunciamus, inque fide illius corroboramur. Sic comedentes ac bibentes, non uescimur nudo pane, sed mystico, nec hæremus in cortice, sed illo aperto nucleum omnium suavissimum dominici uidelicet corporis pro nobis crucifixi, ac sanguinis pro nobis effusi, gratiam fide gustamus & recreamur. Qui sic edūt ac bibunt, non habent ieiunam & inanem cœnam, sed eam ipsam quam instituit dominus, & tanquam Noui testamenti sacramentū suæque mortis memoriale fidelibus suis commendauit, in qua de corpore ac sanguine domini participant, secundum illud capite præcedenti: Panis quem frangimus, nonne communicatio corporis domini est? Et, poculum benedictionis, cui benedicimus, nonne communicatio corporis Christi est? Quod enim semel ecclesiæ suę instituit, dedicauit, ac dedit, ad finem usque mundi durat nec ulla quantumuis multorum sæculorum uetustate labefactari, & in spongiam abire potest. Nostrum est quod iussi fumus facere, idque in rememorationem mortis eius, qui nos sanguine suo redemit. Faciendum autem nobis hoc est fide, per quam in sacramento hoc de corpore ac sanguine domini participamus.
units.tr: But someone here will say: "Then in the Lord's Supper we do nothing else than eat the bread and drink the wine, and in doing so remember the Lord?" I answer: we indeed eat the bread and drink the wine, but not as common food and drink of the body; rather as the bread and cup of the Lord, as the Apostle names them, and as the ancient Fathers named them, the sanctified bread and cup, as Cyprian calls them, the sacrament of the body and blood of the Lord. In these, as Augustine witnesses, one thing is seen and another is understood. They are the symbols and mysteries of the grace of the New Testament, and when we receive them from the Lord's table, we eat and drink not only with the mouth of the body but with the mouth of faith, and in doing so we proclaim the Lord's death with thanksgiving, and are strengthened in his faith. Eating and drinking in this way, we do not feed on bare bread but on the mystical bread, and we do not cling to the shell, but when it is opened we taste by faith the sweetest kernel, namely the body of the Lord crucified for us and his blood shed for us, and are refreshed. Those who eat and drink in this way do not have an empty and fasting supper, but that very supper which the Lord instituted and commended to his faithful as the sacrament of the New Testament and the memorial of his death, in which they partake of the body and blood of the Lord, according to what is said in the previous chapter: "The bread which we break, is it not the communion of the body of the Lord? And the cup of blessing which we bless, is it not the communion of the blood of Christ?" For what he once instituted, dedicated and gave to his Church, endures until the end of the world, and cannot be weakened by any antiquity of many ages, nor pass away into smoke. What is ours is that we do what we have been commanded, and that in remembrance of his death, who redeemed us with his blood. We must do this by faith, through which in this sacrament we partake of the body and blood of the Lord.

units.la: Hoc facite, inquit, quotiescūq; biberitis, in mei rememorationē. Magna cautione non semel tātū, sed secūdo expressit, ad qd nos panē hunc suū edere, & de poculo suo bibere uelit, sic vt ad vtranque sacramenti huius partem di{A}xerit, hoc facite in mei rememorationem.
units.tr: "Do this," he says, "as often as you drink, in remembrance of me." With great care he expressed this not once only but a second time, that we should eat this bread of his and drink from his cup. So to each part of this sacrament he said, "Do this in remembrance of me."

units.la: Quare uehementer temerarium est alteram ex illis ecclesiae Dei adimere, & vbi dominus ipse dixit: hoc facite quotiescunq; biberitis in mei rememorationem, contraria inhibitione dicere, hoc ne feceritis. Qui aureum vel argenteum calicé è teplo interuertit, sacrilegij damnatur, & interea, qui calicem domini ecclesiae traditum abstulerunt, sancti patres, pastores, ac pontifices vocatur. Quis nó videt tato grauius hic sacrilegium admitti, quanto maioris momenti est sacramentū sanguinis domini, quàm calix manibus hominū ad dispensationē illius factus? De consecr. dist. 2. ca. Comperimus, manifeste sic legitur. Diuisio vnius eiusdéq; mysterij sine gradi sacrilegio puenire nó potest.
units.tr: It is therefore exceedingly rash to take either part away from the Church of God, and, where the Lord himself said, "Do this as often as you drink, in remembrance of me," to answer with the contrary prohibition, "Do not do this." Whoever carries off a golden or silver chalice from the temple is condemned for sacrilege, and yet those who removed the chalice handed down to the Church of the Lord are called holy fathers, ministers and pontiffs. Who does not see that a far graver sacrilege is committed here, the more the sacrament of the Lord's blood is of greater importance than a chalice made by human hands for its dispensing? De consecr. dist. 2, ca. Comperimus: it is plainly read thus: "The division of one and the same mystery cannot occur without great sacrilege."

units.la: QVOTIESCVNQVE biberitis, inquit.) Quoniam fiebat ista à domino in coena Paschatis, poterat ipsa quoq; haec institutio ad exemplum veteris Paschatis nonnisi semel in anno, idq; tempore Iudaici Paschatis, celebrada videri. Hanc igitur opinionem verbis istis excludit dicens: Hoc facite quotiescunque biberitis, in mei rememorationem. Permittit ecclesiae liberum quando de pane suo edat & de poculo bibat, nullum prorsus tépus prescribens, sed vnum hoc inculcans, vt faciamus hoc ad sui rememorationem. Haud igitur refert quando & quoties mystica domini mensa vtamur, modo hoc rite, integre, fideliter, & ad destinatum finem competenter faciamus. Libertas{B} ista magnam hac in causa dissimilitudinem, imo & contentiones, peperit in ecclesia. Contendebant alij vesperi tantum ad exemplum Christi, alij mane tantum etiamnum contendunt celebrandum esse hoc sacrum. Et Augustini tempore alij quotidie, sicut hodie Papistae de sua Missa sentiunt, alij rarius communicandum esse censebant, qua de re vide Epistolam illius 118. ad Ianuarium. In Chrysost. super Matt. homil. 16. legimus in omni ecclesiae congregatione celebrata fuisse apud veteres haec mysteria. Et in Isychio super Leuit. lib. 2. cap. 8. sic legimus: Erat enim dies, qui appellatur dominicus in quo oportebat omnibus modis agere apostolos mystica & sacra. Nam & nos sequentes illorum traditionem dominicā diem diuinis conuentibus sequestramus. Tandé eo negligentiae deuentum est, vt ter duntaxat in anno celebrata sit publica haec & ecclesiastica communio. Sic statuit Agathense concilium, ca. 18. Saeculares qui in Natali domini Pasca, & Pent. non communicant, catholici nó credantur, nec inter catholicos habeatur. Nouisime ne hoc quidé mansit, sed semel tatum in anno, Pascatis videlicet tempore, idq; sub pontificali praecepto communicare coepimus. Hodie reperies quàmplurimos qui multis annis ne semel quidé comunicent, praesertim Schwenckfeldiani, qui sic ecclesiasticam communionem quarumcunq; ecclesiarum reijciunt, vt interim ipsi prorsus habeant nullam. Huius sectae au-
units.tr: "As often as you drink," he says. Since this was done by the Lord at the Passover supper, this institution might also seem to be celebrated, after the pattern of the old Passover, only once a year, at the time of the Jewish Passover. He therefore excludes this opinion by these words: "Do this as often as you drink, in remembrance of me." He leaves it free to the Church when it eats of its bread and drinks from its cup, prescribing no time at all, but only impressing this, that we do it in his remembrance. It therefore matters little when and how often we use the Lord's mystical table, provided we do it duly, wholly, faithfully and suitably to the appointed end. This liberty has caused great dissimilarity, and indeed contention, in the Church on this matter. Some contended that this sacred rite must be celebrated only in the evening, after Christ's example; others that it must be celebrated only in the morning. In Augustine's time some thought it should be received daily, as the Papists today think of their Mass, and others that it should be received more rarely; on this matter see his Epistle 118 to Januarius. In Chrysostom on Matthew, homily 16, we read that these mysteries were celebrated among the ancients in every assembly of the Church. And in Isychius on Leviticus, book 2, chapter 8, we read thus: "For there was a day called the Lord's day, on which the apostles had to be occupied in every way with mystical and sacred things. For we too, following their tradition, set aside the Lord's day for divine assemblies." At length negligence reached such a point that this public and ecclesiastical communion was celebrated only three times a year. So the Council of Agde decreed, canon 18: "Laymen who do not communicate at Christmas, Easter and Pentecost are not to be believed Catholics, nor counted among Catholics." Last of all, even this did not remain, but we began to communicate only once a year, at Easter-time, and that under pontifical command. Today you will find very many who do not communicate even once in many years, especially the Schwenckfeldians, who so reject the ecclesiastical communion of every church that they themselves have none at all.

units.la: thorem cum Augustae aliquando rogare, quándo nam cum ecclesia Christi de pane & poculo domini communicasset, diserte respondebat, annos se tum circiter duodecim à communione hac abstinuisse. Rogatus quare hoc faceret, regerebat, nondum se aliquam reperisse ecclesiam, quae verae esset sponsae Christi dotibus ac virtutibus intus ac foris ornata, ideoque expectare se, ac differre communionem, donec ecclesiam aliquam veram ac rite institutam inueniat. Sic illius quoq; discipuli cum nulla vspiam ecclesia communicant. Et praeter hos magnam videmus eorum esse multitudinem in ecclesijs quibusdam liberis & Euangelicis, qui quoniam nullo humano praecepto ad communionem vrgentur, nunquam communicant. Hi instar palearum quas impellit ventus, mox atq; communio est inchoanda cateruatim è coetu sacro euolant. Olim clamabat diaconus, discedite prophani, accedite sancti. Hic nulla est excommunicationis eiusmodi necessitas, quandoquidem maior feré pars vltro seipsa excommunicat.
units.tr: When someone once asked the author of this sect at Augsburg when he had last communicated with the Church of Christ in the bread and cup of the Lord, he answered plainly that he had abstained from this communion for about twelve years. Asked why he did this, he replied that he had not yet found any church adorned, within and without, with the endowments and virtues of Christ's true bride; so he was waiting and deferring communion until he found some true and rightly constituted church. His disciples too communicate with no church anywhere. Besides these, we see a great number of them in certain free and evangelical churches who, since they are urged to communion by no human precept, never communicate. Like chaff driven by the wind, these people, as soon as communion is to begin, fly out of the sacred assembly in crowds. In former times the deacon used to cry, "Depart, profane ones; come forward, holy ones." Here there is no need for such excommunication, since the greater part excommunicate themselves of their own accord.

units.la: QVOTIESCVNQVE enim ederitis panem hunc, & de poculo hoc biberitis, mortem domini annunciatis donec venerit.)
units.tr: "For as often as you eat this bread and drink from this cup, you proclaim the Lord's death until he comes."

units.la: Hactenus dominicam institutionem ad hoc recitauit, vt abusus illi contrarios redargueret, quos nonnulli Corinthiorum in coenam domini introducebant, quibus id efficiebant, vt nihil minus quàm dominicam coenam ederent: Iam de suo quaedam adijcit, quorū alia ad eam dem redargutionem faciunt, alia adhortationem & comminationem habent. Ad eandem redargutionē quae hic dicit faciunt. Hanc ego dominicae coenae institutionem ab ipso domino acceptā vobis tradidi, vnde intelligere poteritis, edere vos coenam non vniuscuiusq; priuatam, sed communem & mysticam, ad memoriam communis Redemptoris nostri institutam. Et hoc ignorare non potestis.
units.tr: Hitherto he has recited the Lord's institution in order to refute the abuses contrary to it, which some of the Corinthians introduced into the Lord's supper, by which they made it anything but the Lord's supper. Now he adds some things of his own: some serve the same refutation, others contain exhortation and warning. What he says here serves the same refutation: "I have handed down to you this institution of the Lord's supper, received from the Lord himself, whereby you can understand that you eat a supper not private to each one, but common and mystical, instituted in memory of our common Redeemer. And you cannot be ignorant of this."

units.la: Nam quotiescunq; panem hunc editis, & de poculo hoc bibitis, mortē dñi, sic à me instituti, annunciatis ac depraedicatis, cuius participes estis non aliqui separatim tantum, sed communiter omnes. Vnde satis admoneri poteratis, qua fide & quàm concordi communicatione coenam hanc domini in memoriā mortis illius edere debeatis. Huc sensum puto esse germanum, quàuis vulgata versio habeat ista in futuro ad huc modum: Quotiescunq; enim manducabitis panē huc, & calicé bibetis, mortem domini annunciabitis donec veniat. Erat tamen vertit, quemadmodum nos legimus & exponimus. Sūt qui verbū καταγγέλλετε in imperatiuo legat, annunciate. Verū ei lectioni cauc falis vocula γάρ, i. enim, non admodū fauet. Illi iudicant Apost. istis verbis exponere ac simul mandare, quomodo rememorationē dñi celebrare debeant Corinthij, sic videlicet, vt quotiescúq; panē huc edát & de poculo hoc bibát morte illius annúciet, quasi & hoc in illis desiderauerit, quod morte dñi in coena hae mystica
units.tr: "For as often as you eat this bread and drink from this cup, you proclaim and preach the death of the Lord, as instituted by me, of which you are partakers not separately only, but all together in common. From this you could have been sufficiently reminded with what faith, and with how harmonious a communion, you ought to eat this supper of the Lord in memory of his death." I think this is the genuine sense, although the Vulgate renders it in the future in this manner: "For as often as you shall eat this bread and drink this cup, you shall proclaim the Lord's death until he comes." Yet the Vulgate translator rendered it as we read it and expound it. There are those who read the word καταγγέλλετε [announce] in the imperative, "announce." But the little particle γάρ [for] does not much favour that reading. They judge that the Apostle by these words both explains and at the same time commands how the Corinthians ought to celebrate the remembrance of the Lord, namely so that as often as they eat this bread and drink from this cup, they proclaim his death, as if he wanted this too in them, since they did not proclaim the Lord's death in this mystical and memorial supper

units.la: ftica&memoriali non annunciarent,quemad modum Papistarū sacrificulos missas suas sic celebrare videmus,vt prorsus nullam faciant dominicę mortis annunciationem.Nā ea quæ separatim dicūt,pro annunciatione hac habe ri nō possunt.Dicunt enim & auersi à plebe & lingua ecclesię incognita,&sub silentio tali vt ne a Latine quidem scientibus percipi queat.
units.tr: as we see the Papists' little priests celebrate their masses in such a way that they make no proclamation of the Lord's death at all. For what they say separately cannot be counted as a proclamation of this kind. They speak with their backs to the people and in a tongue unknown to the Church, and in such silence that not even those who know Latin can perceive it.

units.la: Obseruet hic pius lector,quod non simpli citer dicit: Quotiescunq; ederitis panē, & de poculo biberitis,sed cū specificatione, Quo tiescunq; ederi is panē hunc,& de poculo hoc biberitis.Quoniam dictum est à domino, hoc facite,quotiescunq; biberitis inimei rememo rationem,existimant nonnulli fratres, loquu tum illum esse de quotidianis ac domesticis si delium suorum prandijs,sicq; memoriam hāc sui instituisse,ut quoties domi suę eduntac bi bunt,in sui hoc rememorationem faciant. No lim damnare talem feruorē ac fidem erga Ser uatorem nostrū Christum, si qui singulis suis prandijs memoriam illius adiungeret, uerum hoc sensu institutam esse mysticam hanc cœ nam,ex uerbis Christi probari posse nō puto. Quare uigilāter ab Apostolo factum est,quod cum specificatione dixit: Quotiescunq; enim ederitis hunc panem,&de poculo hoc biberi tis,mortem domini annunciatis, significās se nō de priuatis fidelium cœnis,sed de ecclesia stica loqui.Hanc si dominus instituit nō com munem & ecclesiasticam, sed priuatam & do mesticam, non video quomodo firmum esse possit,quod paulo supra.dixit:Igitur cum cō uenitis in eundem cœtum, nō est dominicam cœnam edere, propterea quod unusquisque proprium præsumit edendo. Nam istis uerbis palam admonet dominicam cœnā sic esse insti tutam,ut communiter&in cœtu fidelium ce lebretur quod stare non potest, si dominus do mesticas cœnas instituit. Nec est, ut dicamus, reprehendere Apostolum diuisionem quæ in ipso ecclesiastico cœtu fiebat,non damnare, si qui domi suæ cœnam dominicam cum dome sticis suis absq; spiritu schismatis quotidie co medant,&mortem domini annuncient. Nam si hoc egisset, non dixisset, an domus nō habe tis ad manducandum&bibēdum? Sed potius adhunc modum, an domus non habetis, in quibus separatim ac priuatim cœnam domi nicam edatis?
units.tr: Here let the pious reader observe that he does not say simply, "as often as you eat the bread and drink from the cup," but with specification: "as often as you eat this bread and drink from this cup." Since the Lord said, "Do this as often as you drink, in remembrance of me," some brethren think that he was speaking of the daily meals of his faithful at home, and that he instituted this remembrance of himself so that whenever they eat and drink in their houses they should do it in his remembrance. I would not condemn such fervour and faith toward our Saviour Christ in those who add a remembrance of him to each of their meals; but I do not think it can be proved from Christ's words that this mystical supper was instituted in this sense. Therefore it was deliberately done by the Apostle that he said, with specification, "For as often as you eat this bread and drink this cup, you proclaim the Lord's death," signifying that he speaks not of the private suppers of the faithful but of the ecclesiastical supper. If the Lord instituted this not as common and ecclesiastical but as private and domestic, I do not see how what he said a little above can stand: "When therefore you come together into one place, it is not to eat the Lord's supper, because each one presumes to eat his own." For by these words he plainly admonishes that the Lord's supper was so instituted that it is celebrated in common and in the assembly of the faithful, which cannot stand if the Lord instituted domestic suppers. Nor is it right to say that the Apostle, in reproving the division that arose in the ecclesiastical assembly itself, does not condemn those who daily celebrate the Lord's supper at home with their household, without a spirit of schism, and proclaim the Lord's death. For if he had meant this, he would not have said, "Have you not houses to eat and drink in?" but rather, in this manner, "Have you not houses in which you may eat the Lord's supper separately and privately?"

units.la: Deinde obseruandum est,quod dicit:mor tem domini annunciatis. Animaduertēda hic est Apostolica traditio,secundum quam mors domini annūciáda est in cœna dominica.Vsq; adeo non est hæc annunciatio leuis ducenda momenti,ut primarium in illa dominicæ cœ næ scopum præfixum esse sentire debeamus. Video tam veterum quàm recensiorum sub tiles quasdam cogitationes eò tēdere,vt quod simpliciter propositum est à Domino&tradi tum ab Apostolis,quasi non satis amplitudini causæ huius respondens, etsi nō prorsus abij citur,uix tamen postremo loco habeatur.Glo-
units.tr: Next we must observe what he says: "you proclaim the death of the Lord." Here we should note the apostolic tradition according to which the death of the Lord is to be proclaimed in the Lord's Supper. This proclamation is not to be regarded as a matter of slight importance, so that we should understand the chief aim of that Supper to be set before us. I see that some subtle speculations, both of the ancients and of more recent writers, tend in a direction where what was plainly proposed by the Lord and handed down by the apostles is hardly given even the last place, as though it did not match the greatness of the cause.

units.la: rificationem,deificationem& claritatem cor poris Christi in hanc eaufam inferunt, & inde non mirabilia modo,sed& portentiosa de illo figmenta comminiscūtur, quibus sic fidelium mentes à scopo dominico abductas confun dunt & intricatas reddunt,ut tandem prorsus nesciat qd de corpore Christi sentire debeat. Scimus Christum verum esse Deum & uerum hominem,Deo patri secundum diuinitate,no bis vero secundum carnis nostri assumptioně homousion. Scimus illum secundum carnem resurrexisse à mortuis, & glorificato sorpore ascendisse in cœlos,illicq; sedere à dextris pa tris,&regnare super omnia. Verū cum sit ma nifestum instituisse illum nobis non gloriæ,in qua nunc est,sed mortis suæ,non corporis sui glorificati,sed ,pnobis traditi,crucifixi ac mor tui,& sanguinis non quale iam habet, sed quæ in cruce pro peccatis nostris effudit,sacramen tum& rememorationē, ideoq; Apostolus hic non dicat,gloriam,sed mortem domini annū ciatis quotiescunque de pane hoc editis, &de poculo hoc bibitis , existimo uehementer ab errare à legitimo causę huius scopo,omnia illa argumēta, quæ de glorificato Christi corpore ac diuinitate à nonnullis adferuntur. Nimis di scedunt à mente Christi& proposito sancti il lius instituti, qui morte & effusionem sangui nis illius contenentes de sublimioribus in ec clefia spiritu contentionis perciti disputant. Paulus cū diceret, Nihil me iudicaui scire nisi Christū Iesum,magno cōsilio adiecit, & hunc crucifixū.Et:Absit à me vt glorier, nisi in cru ce domini nostri Iesu Christi.Gal.6.
units.tr: They bring in the glorification, deification and brightness of Christ's body for this purpose, and from this they invent not only wonderful but monstrous fictions about him. By these they draw the minds of the faithful away from the Lord's aim, confuse them and entangle them, so that in the end they no longer know what they ought to think about the body of Christ. We know that Christ is true God and true man, consubstantial [ὁμοούσιον] with the Father according to his divinity, and consubstantial with us according to the assumption of our flesh. We know that according to the flesh he rose from the dead, ascended into heaven with a glorified body, sits there at the right hand of the Father, and reigns over all things. But since it is clear that he instituted this supper for us to remember not the glory in which he now is, but his death; not his glorified body, but his body given for us, crucified and dead; and not the blood as he now has it, but the blood he poured out on the cross for our sins, as a sacrament and a remembrance: therefore the apostle does not say "glory" here, but "you proclaim the death of the Lord, as often as you eat this bread and drink this cup." I think those who bring forward all those arguments about the glorified body and divinity of Christ stray badly from the true aim of this cause. They depart far from the mind of Christ and the purpose of that holy institution, which concerns his death and the shedding of his blood, when they dispute about higher matters in the Church with a spirit of contention. When Paul said, "I determined to know nothing among you except Jesus Christ," he wisely added "and him crucified." And: "God forbid that I should glory, except in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ." (Gal. 6.)

units.la: Nec illud transeundū est, quod non simpli citer dicit ἀγγέλλετε,id est, nūciatis, sed καταγ γέλλετε, id est, maximopere nunciatis. Habet enim κατὰ in cōpositione hac vim intendendæ significationis.Tradidit illis Apostolus nō le uem aliquā dominicæ mortis memoria tribus quatuor uerbis obiter& perfunctorie, sed ma gno serio ac publica annunciatione,tanquam incomparabilis ac stupēdi beneficij, per quod ab ęterna miseros nos morte redemit,perage dam ac depræďicandam.
units.tr: Nor should we pass over the fact that he does not simply say ἀγγέλλετε [announce], that is, "you announce," but καταγγέλλετε [proclaim], that is, "you announce with the greatest earnestness." For the prefix κατά in this compound has the force of intensifying the meaning. The apostle did not hand down to them merely some passing and perfunctory remembrance of the Lord's death in three or four words, but a solemn and public proclamation, to be carried out and proclaimed as an incomparable and wonderful benefit, by which he redeemed us wretched people from eternal death.

units.la: DONE Cuenerit,inquit.) Signicat hūc ri tum cœnæ mysticæ&annunciandæ mortis do minicæ esse,nec alterāduὺm,nec deserendū ad ipsum ufq; aduentum domini,quo uēturus est in fine mundi.Vbi uenerit, nulla erit amplius ratio celebrādæ ipsius memoriæ,quādoquidē præsentes tū illi erimus,unaq; cū ipso in sem piternum agemus. Dum sumus in hoc corpo re peregrinamur à domino.Per fidē enim am bulamus,&non per speciem. In hoc mūdo nō fruimur specie,qua fruemur in futuro,sed fide sustentamur,& vere pietatis exercitijs,studijs & affectibus cum domino agimus, quo & hic dominicæ memorię ritus pertinet. Adest qui dem nobis spiritu suo dominus, & per hunc exercitia hæc fidei nostrae efficacia reddūtur, haud tamen pari iucunditate sumitur cortex sacramenti, sicuti Bernardus alicubi dicit, & adeps
units.tr: "Until he comes," he says. This signifies that the rite of the mystical supper and of proclaiming the Lord's death is not to be changed or abandoned until the Lord's own coming, when he will come at the end of the world. When he has come, there will be no further reason to celebrate the remembrance of him, since then we shall be present with him and shall live with him forever. While we are in this body we are away from the Lord. For we walk by faith, and not by sight. In this world we do not enjoy the sight which we shall enjoy in the future, but we are sustained by faith, and we deal with the Lord through the exercises of true godliness, zeal and affections; and to these the rite of remembering the Lord also belongs here. The Lord is indeed present with us by his Spirit, and through the Spirit these exercises of our faith are made effective. Yet the outward part of the sacrament is not received with equal delight, as Bernard somewhere says, and [the sacrament is] the fat

units.la: In Cantica Serm.33. adeps frumenti, fidei & species, memoria & praesentia, æternitas & tempus, vultus & speculum. Vbi per speciem praesentis Christi gloria fruemur, finem habebunt Noui huius testamenti sacramenta. Praesenti tempori deputata est Christi memoria, futuro vero praesentia, quia hoc fidei est, illud speciei.
units.tr: (In Canticum Sermo 33) "the fat of wheat; faith and sight, memory and presence, eternity and time, face and mirror." Where, through the sight of the present glory of Christ, we shall enjoy him, the sacraments of this New Testament will come to an end. Remembrance of Christ is assigned to the present time, but presence to the future, because the one belongs to faith and the other to sight.

units.la: Haud vero praeter rationem est, quod particulam hanc de reditu domini, pro peccatis nostris mortui adiecit. Qui maiorum suorum memorias iuxta saeculum agunt, nulla pe reditus illorum afficiuntur. Ne tale quid carnalibus Corinthijs memoriam domini celebrantibus accideret, vbi dixit: Quotiescunque panem hunc ederitis, & de poculo hoc biberitis, mortem domini annunciatis, adiecit, donec veniret, qua particula monet & rediturum ad nos esse dominum, & qua spe ac perseuerantia memoriam illius celebrare ac mortem annunciare debeamus. Spes ista rediturî ad nos domini plurimum habet efficaciae ad excitandum animos nostros, ne cum hoc mundo dormiamus & aduentu illius imparati adobruamur.
units.tr: It is not without reason that he added this clause about the Lord's return, in addition to "who died for our sins." Those who keep the memories of their ancestors merely according to the world are not affected at all by the return of those they remember. Lest anything of this kind should happen to the carnal Corinthians while they celebrate the memory of the Lord, where he said, "As often as you eat this bread and drink this cup, you proclaim the death of the Lord," he added "until he comes." By this clause he reminds us that the Lord will return to us, and with what hope and perseverance we ought to celebrate his memory and proclaim his death. This hope of the Lord's return to us has great power to stir up our souls, so that we do not sleep with this world and are not overwhelmed, unprepared, by his coming.

units.la: Itaque quisquis ederit panem hunc, aut biberit de poculo domini indigne, reus erit corporis ac sanguinis domini. Probet autem homo seipsum, & sic de pane illo edat, & de poculo illo bibat. Nam qui edit ac bibit indigne, iudicium sibi ipsi edit ac bibit, non diiudicans corpus dni.
units.tr: Therefore whoever eats this bread or drinks the cup of the Lord unworthily will be guilty of the body and blood of the Lord. But let a man examine himself, and so let him eat of that bread and drink of that cup. For he who eats and drinks unworthily eats and drinks judgment to himself, not discerning the body of the Lord.

units.la: Habet haec tertia pars grauissimam commi nationem contra eos qui coena dominica abu tuntur, cui & fidelem admonitionem adiugit, propter eos, quos emendari posse sperabat. Colligit autem vtrunque ex praemissa dominicae institutionis commemoratione dicens: Itaque quisquis ederit panem hunc aut biberit de poculo domini indigne, reus erit corporis ac sanguinis domini. Quasi dicat. Dum schismata in coenam dominicam introducitis, dum vnusquisque vestrum propriam coenam praesumit, dum alius ebrius est, alius esurit, dum alius alium non expectatis, dum perinde de pane ac poculo domini editis ac bibitis, ac si ad ppha-num conuiuium conueniatis, dum ecclesiam Dei contemnitis, dum pudefacitis eos qui non habent, admodum indigne panem hunc editis, & de poculo hoc domini bibitis. At hoc faci entes non leue peccatum admittitis. Peccatis non enim simpliciter in ecclesiam quâ scindi tis & contemnitis, & in mensam mysticam, cuius vsum peruertitis, sed & in ipsum corpus ac sanguinem domini. Audistis enim dixisse dominum, cum panem hunc frangeret ac discipulis daret, accipite, edite, hoc meum est corpus quod pro vobis frangitur, & cum poculum hoc porrigeret: Hoc poculum Nouum testamentum est in meo sanguine, qui pro vobis effundetur. Quare omnino consequitur vt quisquis panem hunc ederit, aut de poculo hoc domini biberit indigne, reus fiat corporis ac san-
units.tr: This third part contains a most grave denunciation against those who abuse the Lord's Supper, and he joins to it a faithful admonition for the sake of those whom he hoped could be corrected. He draws both from the aforementioned recollection of the Lord's institution, saying: "Therefore whoever eats this bread or drinks the cup of the Lord unworthily will be guilty of the body and blood of the Lord." As if he said: While you introduce divisions into the Lord's Supper, while each of you presumes upon his own supper, while one is drunk and another hungry, while you do not wait for one another, while you eat and drink the bread and cup of the Lord just as if you were gathering at a profane banquet, while you despise the Church of God, while you shame those who have nothing, you eat this bread and drink this cup of the Lord in a most unworthy manner. Doing these things, you commit no small sin. For you sin not only against the Church, which you divide and despise, and against the mystical table, whose use you pervert, but also against the very body and blood of the Lord. For you have heard that the Lord, when he broke this bread and gave it to his disciples, said: "Take, eat; this is my body, which is broken for you." And when he handed over this cup: "This cup is the New Testament in my blood, which will be poured out for you." Therefore it certainly follows that whoever eats this bread, or drinks of this cup of the Lord, unworthily, becomes guilty of the body and blood of the Lord.

units.la: guinis domini. Hunc puto esse verborum istorum sensum, de quibus paucum quaedam annotâda sunt, priusq; ad sequetia pgrediamur.
units.tr: I think this is the sense of those words, on which some things should be noted briefly before we proceed to what follows.

units.la: Principio non debet hoc pius lector leuis momenti iudicare, quod Apostolus de sacramento hoc dominici corporis ac sanguinis loquens, quamuis contemptum illius contra carnalis Corinthios reprehendat, constanter tamen panem uocat & poculum, idq; no modo ante sed & in ipsa communicatione, qua editur ac bibitur, dicens: Quotiescunque enim ederitis panem hunc, & de poculo hoc biberitis. Item. Quisquis ederit panem hunc, & biberit de poculo domini indigne. Et tertio. Probet autem homo seipsum, & sic de pane illo edat, & de poculo illo bibat. Respectu papistarum parum religiosus fuit Apostolus, quod toties panem & poculum uocat, quod illi pertinaciter panem & uinum esse negant. Cum initio uenissem Augustam Vindelicorum, illo ad praedicandum Euangelium Christi uocatus, cum doctore Sebastiano Meyer, piae memoriae, sacrificulo quedam concionatem audiui, cuius thema, ut uocant, erat: Probet autem seipsum homo, & sic de pane illo edat, & de poculo illo bibat, quae uerba cum pro ipsorum more Latine ad populum Latine nescientem protulisset, mox interpretationem hanc subiecit. Der mensch aber probier sich selbs, vnd also esse er vo disem fleisch, vnd trinck von disem blüot. Apostolicam loquutionem non audebat, uel certe nolebat, impostor proponere rudi populo, quo fucu illi faceret. Friuolum est quod Lyranus exponit dicens: Panem uocat propter species panis remanetes. Consimili modo dicat: Poculu uocat propter species poculi post consecrationem remanentes. Apostolus ignarus huius fascinationis panem uocat panem, poculum poculū. Nec est, ut pronomen, hunc, referant ad corpus domini quemadmodum nonnulli ex illis faciunt, quasi cum dicit, panem hunc, alium panem à uisibili, nempe ipsum Christi corpus, panem uitae, intelligat. Non loquitur de alio pane quem frangebant, & edebant digni & indigni, quemadmodum nec de alio poculo quàm uini de quo bibebant omnes. Adijcit autem specificationem, qua panem ac poculum domini à prophano pane ac uino discernat.
units.tr: First, the godly reader should not judge it a matter of small importance that the apostle, speaking of this sacrament of the Lord's body and blood, though he rebukes the contempt of it among the carnal Corinthians, nevertheless consistently calls it bread and cup, and does so not only before but also during the very communion in which it is eaten and drunk, saying: "As often as you eat this bread and drink this cup." Likewise: "Whoever eats this bread and drinks the cup of the Lord unworthily." And a third time: "Let a man examine himself, and so let him eat of that bread and drink of that cup." The apostle was not very careful, with regard to the Papists, in calling it bread and cup, since they stubbornly deny that it is bread and wine. When at the beginning I came to Augsburg, called there to preach the Gospel of Christ, I heard with Doctor Sebastian Meyer, of blessed memory, a certain priest preaching, whose text, as they call it, was: "Let a man examine himself, and so let him eat of that bread and drink of that cup." When he had recited these words in Latin, as is their custom, to a people who did not know Latin, he at once added this translation: Let a man examine himself, and so let him eat of this flesh and drink of this blood. The impostor either did not dare, or certainly did not want, to put the apostolic expression before the untaught people, by which he would deceive them. It is frivolous what Lyra explains, saying: "He calls it bread because of the appearances of bread that remain." In the same way one might say: "He calls it cup because of the appearances of the cup that remain after consecration." The apostle, unaware of this enchantment, calls bread bread and cup cup. Nor does the pronoun "this" refer to the body of the Lord, as some of them do, as if when he says "this bread" he meant another bread, distinct from the visible one, namely the body of Christ, the bread of life. He is not speaking of another bread which they broke and ate, both worthy and unworthy, nor of another cup than the wine from which all of them drank. Moreover, he adds a specification by which he distinguishes the bread and cup of the Lord from profane bread and wine.

units.la: Quaesierit quisquam, quare non potius augustius loquens dixerit: Itaque quisquis ederit corpus domini aut biberit sanguinem domini indigne, cum tamen panem hunc dominus ipse sacramentaliter loquendo corpus suum, & poculum hoc sanguinem suum uocarit. Respondeo. Non est hoc temere factum ab Apostolo. Iudicabant Corinthij in coena domini panem se tantum edere ac uinum bibere, parū de mysterio corporis ac sanguinis domini cogitantes. Carnalem hanc illorum sententiam correcturus haud quidem negat esse panem ac poculum uini in coena domini, verum adiecta specificatione monet eum panem alium esse à quolibet pane mensario ac prophano, panem uideli-
units.tr: One might ask why he did not rather speak more solemnly and say: "Therefore whoever shall eat the body of the Lord or drink the blood of the Lord unworthily," since the Lord himself, speaking sacramentally, called this bread his body and this cup his blood. I answer that the Apostle did not do this carelessly. The Corinthians judged that in the Lord's Supper they were only eating bread and drinking wine, thinking little of the mystery of the body and blood of the Lord. To correct this carnal opinion, he does not deny that in the Lord's Supper there is bread and a cup of wine. But by adding a specification he warns that this bread is other than any common, profane bread, namely the bread of the Lord,

units.la: t
units.tr: t

units.la: videlicet domini,& poculū hoc aliud à quo libet prophano poculo, nempe poculum domini, ideoque haud prophanis, sed religiosis modis utrunq; vsurpādum. Et hæc instructio melius conueniebat carnalibus adhuc Corinthijs, quàm si dixisset, quisquis ederit corpus domini & biberit sanguine domini indigne. Deinde, quoniam adhuc carnales erant, & sacramentalibus loquutionibus insueti, non conueniebat ut diceret, quisquis ederit corpus domini indigne. Neq; enim corpus domini per se indigne potest edi à quoquam, neq; ipsi hoc de sacramento corporis dni rite intellexissent.
units.tr: and that this cup is other than any profane cup, namely the cup of the Lord, and therefore both are to be used in a religious, not a profane, manner. This instruction suited the still carnal Corinthians better than if he had said, "whoever shall eat the body of the Lord and drink the blood of the Lord unworthily." Furthermore, since they were still carnal and unaccustomed to sacramental modes of speech, it was not fitting for him to say, "whoever shall eat the body of the Lord unworthily." For the body of the Lord cannot in itself be eaten unworthily by anyone, nor would they have rightly understood this of the sacrament of the Lord's body.

units.la: Deinde in eo qd' dicit, quisquis ederit aut biberit indigne, uidédum est, quid sit rem aliquam facere digne. Est unicuiq; rei, operi, persone, cùm in sacris tum in prophanis suum mispatius, ac decorum dare secundum quod q se gerit, vel aliquid facit, ἀξίως, id est, conuenienter, rite, competēter ac decenter facit, id uidelicet faciens quod vel personæ suæ, uel operi quod facit, cōuenit: qui uero secus facit quàm conuenit, ἀναξίως, id est, inconuenienter & inde céter facere dicitur. Et hac uoce utitur hic Apostolus dicēs: quisquis ederit aut biberit ἀνα ξίως, id est, secus quàm decet & conuenit. Verterunt interpretes, quisquis ederit aut biberit indigne, haud quidem male, interea tamē obscurius quàm, vt ab imperitioribus recte possit intellīgi. Illi cogitant, &quis est qui dignus possit ad sacramentū hoc corporis ac sanguinis domini accedere, deq; illo edere ac bibere non indigne. atq; ita reclamante plerunq; conscientia comunicant. At Apostolus non dicit: qui ederit aut biberit ἀναξίως, id est, indignus, sed aduerbialiter ἀναξίως, id est, secus quàm conuenit, aliter quàm ipsa cœna dominica poscit. Non loquitur de dignitate communicantium, sed de seruando dominicæ cœnæ decoro. Si personæ nostræ respiciantur, dicēdum est singulis: Domine, non sum dignus ut particeps sim mensæ tuæ. Verum ubi decorum mensæ domini, ad quam uocamur, consideramus, quis inuitamur ad illam indigni, cauere tamen possumus ac debemus, ne modis indignis ac secus quàm conuenit de illa participemus. Si pauper ad mensam regiam uocetur, uocatur utiq; indignus, id quod illi absq; ullo est periculo: uocatur enim per gratiam regis, uerū si se in mensa regis scuriliter ac secus gerat q de cet, quod multis modis fieri potest, id demū il lum reum constituet contemptæ maiestatis regiæ. Tale est, quod sine veste nuptiali in cōuiuio cœlestium nuptiarum comparemus. Talē erat, quod Corinthij in cœnam dominicam introducebant schismata, seindētes quod omnium debebat esse unitisimū, quod propriā unusquisq; cœnam non expectatis alijs præsumebat, quod esurientibus alijs alij inebriabantur, quod de pane ac poculo domini edebant ac bibebant perinde ac si in prophano cō uiuio sederent, quod ecclesia Dei contemnebant, ac pudefaciebant eos, qui nihil habebāt.
units.tr: Next, in what he says, "whoever shall eat or drink unworthily," we must consider what it is to do something worthily. To every thing, work, or person, whether in sacred or in profane matters, there belongs its proper measure and fitting form, according to what a person is or what he does. He who acts ἀξίως (that is, fittingly, rightly, suitably and becomingly) does what agrees with his own person or with the work he undertakes. But he who acts otherwise than is fitting is said to act ἀναξίως (that is, unfittingly and inappropriately). The Apostle uses this word here, saying, "whoever shall eat or drink ἀναξίως," that is, otherwise than is proper and fitting. The translators rendered it, "whoever shall eat or drink unworthily." This is not wrong, yet it is more obscure than it needs to be for the less learned to understand it rightly. They think of who is worthy to approach this sacrament of the body and blood of the Lord, and to eat and drink of it not unworthily; and so, while conscience often protests, they communicate. But the Apostle does not say, "whoever shall eat or drink ἀναξίως," that is, "unworthy," but adverbially ἀναξίως, that is, otherwise than is fitting, otherwise than the Lord's Supper itself requires. He is not speaking of the worthiness of the communicants but of preserving the decorum of the Lord's Supper. If we look at our own persons, we must say to each one of us, "Lord, I am not worthy that you should come under my roof." But when we consider the decorum of the Lord's table, to which we are invited, we who are unworthy are invited to it. Still, we can and must take care not to partake of it in unworthy ways and otherwise than is fitting. If a poor man is called to a royal table, he is certainly called unworthy, yet this is no danger to him, for he is called through the grace of the king. But if he behaves in the king's presence in a boorish or unseemly way, as can happen in many ways, that alone will make him guilty of despising royal majesty. This is like coming without a wedding garment to the feast of the heavenly marriage. This was the case with the Corinthians, who introduced divisions into the Lord's Supper, tearing apart what ought to have been most united; each one anticipated his own supper without waiting for the others; while some went hungry, others became drunk; they ate and drank the bread and cup of the Lord as if they were sitting at a common meal; they despised the Church of God and shamed those who had nothing.

units.la: His modis edere panem ac bibere de poculo domini prorsus est ἀναξίως, id est, secus quàm conuenit, ac præter decorum cœnæ domini-cæ edere ac bibere.
units.tr: To eat the bread and drink from the cup of the Lord in these ways is altogether ἀναξίως, that is, otherwise than is fitting, and beside the decorum of the Lord's Supper.

units.la: Hoc pacto indigne panem domini edebāt & de poculo illius bibebant Corinthij, adulterantes ritum cœnæ dominicæ, & ab institutio-ne illius discedētes. Est autem in cœna domini non modo externus ritus conueniēter mo-disq; dignis seruandus, sed & competenti intelligētia, fide, gratitudine, syncero erga Christum & ecclesiam illius affectu, cum dilectio-ne fratrum, &uita pura communicandū. Quare qui externa tantum signa sine illorum intelectu usurpant, ex mystica & sacra cœna prophanam facientes, qui licet omnia rite intelligant, quatenus verbo Christi traduntur, uera tamen esse nō credunt, historica fide distituti: hoc est, non credūt mortem Christi ualere ad redemptionem mundi, remissionem peccatorum nostrorum, & recōciliationem cum Deo patre, &c. qui tametsi credunt Christū pro peccatis mundi Deo patri morte sua satisfecisse, eam tamen redemptionem ad se quoq; pertinere non credunt, sed nescio quibus sanctis & iustis deputant, qui etiamsi pro se quoq; mortuum esse Christum credunt, id tamen benefi-cij haud admodum magnifaciunt, neq; recordatione illius ad gratiarum actionem mouen-tur, qui non tota animi sui fiducia sincere & obediēter à Christo domino redemptore suo pendent, qui non sunt fraternæ charitatis affectu erga ecclesiam Christi &quoscunq; fratres illius membra præditi, & qui vita flagitiosa declarant se esse membra nō Christi sed Satanæ, ideoq; nullam habere in regno Dei partem, hi omnes quoties communicant de pane ac poculo domini, communicant ἀναξίως. Nam non modo mutatus & corruptus dominicæ institutionis ritus, sed & sensus mere carnalis, incredulitas, ingratitudo, infinceritas animi erga Christum, contemptus ecclesiæ, animus alienus à fraterna charitate, & uita flagitiosa, omnium debent esse remotissimā à communi cantibus de hoc pane & poculo domini. Red dunt enim indignos, qui ad mensam domini accedant.
units.tr: In this way the Corinthians ate the Lord's bread and drank from his cup unworthily, corrupting the rite of the Lord's Supper and departing from its institution. In the Lord's Supper, however, not only the external rite must be observed fittingly and in a manner worthy of it, but the communicant must also partake with suitable understanding, faith, gratitude, and a sincere affection toward Christ and his Church, with love for the brothers and a pure life. Therefore those who use only the external signs without understanding them, making the mystical and sacred supper into a profane one, though they understand everything correctly as far as it is delivered in the word of Christ, do not believe it to be true, lacking historical faith. That is, they do not believe that the death of Christ avails for the redemption of the world, the forgiveness of our sins, and reconciliation with God the Father, and so on. Even those who believe that Christ satisfied God the Father for the sins of the world by his death, yet do not believe that this redemption pertains to themselves, but assign it to I know not what holy and just persons; and even those who believe that Christ died for themselves, yet do not esteem this benefit very highly, nor are they moved by the remembrance of it to give thanks; those who do not sincerely and obediently depend with the whole confidence of their soul on Christ the Lord, their redeemer; those who do not have the affection of brotherly love toward the Church of Christ and all its brothers and members; and those who by a shameful life show that they are members not of Christ but of Satan, and therefore have no part in the kingdom of God: all of these, whenever they communicate of the bread and cup of the Lord, communicate ἀναξίως. For not only a changed and corrupted rite of the Lord's institution, but also a purely carnal mind, unbelief, ingratitude, insincerity of soul toward Christ, contempt of the Church, a mind alienated from brotherly love, and a shameful life must all be kept as far as possible from those who communicate in this bread and cup of the Lord. For such things make men unworthy who approach the table of the Lord.

units.la: Tertiò & illud videndum est, quod dicit: Reus erit corporis ac sanguinis domini. Reū esse corporis ac sanguinis domini, est reū esse peccati & iniuriæ in corp⁹ ac sanguiné Christi admissæ. Peccatum hoc tripliciter admittitur.
units.tr: Thirdly, we must also consider what he says: "He will be guilty of the body and blood of the Lord." To be guilty of the body and blood of the Lord is to be guilty of sin and injury committed against the body and blood of Christ. This sin is committed in three ways.

units.la: 1 Primò ab illis qui ipsi corpori ac sanguini domini iniuriam inferunt. Factum hoc est à Iudæis, qui corpus domini crucifixerunt & sanguinem illius effuderunt, quorum uox est, sanguis eius super nos & super filios nostros.
units.tr: (1) First, by those who inflict injury on the very body and blood of the Lord. This was done by the Jews, who crucified the body of the Lord and poured out his blood; their cry is, "His blood be on us and on our children."

units.la: 2 Deinde ab illis qui sibimetipsis filiū Dei crucifigunt, Ebr.6. & sanguinem testaméti pō lutum ducunt, dum à uia ueritatis semel cognita relabuntur, & mortem domini qua redempti sunt, irritam sibi reddunt.
units.tr: (2) Second, by those who crucify the Son of God again for themselves, Hebrews 6, and count the blood of the covenant unclean, as they fall back from the way of truth once known, and render void for themselves the death of the Lord by which they were redeemed.

units.la: 3 Tertiò, ab illis quoque, qui sacramentum corpo-
units.tr: (3) Third, by those also who handle the sacrament of the body

units.la: Quidsit reū esse corporis ac sanguinis domini. corporis ac sanguinis domini aliqua afficiunt iniuria, siue id faciat sensu, siue uerbis, siue abu su. Etenim quicquid in hunc panem & poculum domini peccatur, in ipsum corpus & sanguinem domini peccatur, quorum sunt sacramentum. Intellige de peccato quod illis non simpliciter vt pani & vino ab eo qui sacramentum corporis ac sanguinis domini esse nescit, sed scienter vt sacramento infertur. Corinthij sciebant se conuenire ad edendum cœnam dominicam, cuius ritum ab Apostolo acceperat, quare quod hic in panem ac poculum domini peccabant, ad iniuriam corporis ac sanguinis domini cedebat, quorum sacramentum indignis modis tractabant. Peccabant in ipsam Christi institutionem, quam corrumpebant, peccabant in ecclesiam Christi quam contemnebant, peccabant in membra Christi quæ pudefaciebat, ut recte dici queat, quod in ipsum Christum peccauerint, verum quoniam hoc genus peccati in sacramentū corporis ac sanguinis Christi peculialiter admittebatur, gravitatem illius significantius exprimere uoles dixit, quisquis ederit hunc panem & biberit de hoc poculo domini indigne, reus erit corporis ac sanguinis domini.
units.tr: What it is to be guilty of the body and blood of the Lord. They inflict some injury on the body and blood of the Lord, whether they do so by their feelings, by words, or by abuse. For whatever sin is committed against this bread and cup of the Lord, is committed against the body and blood of the Lord itself, of which they are the sacrament. Understand this of a sin committed not simply against the bread and wine by one who does not know that they are the sacrament of the body and blood of the Lord, but knowingly, as against a sacrament. The Corinthians knew that they came together to eat the Lord's Supper, the rite of which they had received from the Apostle. Therefore what they sinned here against the bread and cup of the Lord fell back as an injury to the body and blood of the Lord, whose sacrament they handled in unworthy ways. They sinned against Christ's own institution, which they corrupted; they sinned against the Church of Christ, which they despised; they sinned against the members of Christ, whom they shamed. So it may rightly be said that they sinned against Christ himself. But since this kind of sin was committed especially against the sacrament of the body and blood of Christ, to express its gravity more forcefully he said: "whoever shall eat this bread and drink from this cup of the Lord unworthily will be guilty of the body and blood of the Lord."

units.la: Nec otiosum est, quod non simpliciter dicit, peccat in corpus ac sanguine domini, sed, reus erit corporis ac sanguinis domini. Græcè ἔνοχος, quæ uox sonat non solum peccatorem, sed eum qui propter peccatu obnoxius est iudicio & condemnationi, quem alias uocant τίμωρον. Cū ergo dicit, reus erit corporis B ac sanguinis domini, non solum exponit genus peccati, sed & minatur illis certum graue-que condemnationem ac pœnam qui de pane ac poculo domini indigne edunt & bibūt. Et reuera sic graue est hoc peccatum, ut merito graui sit condemnationi obnoxium. Horrere conuenit Christiano, si audiat se reum fieri corporis ac sanguinis domini, per quæ est a peccato & morte redemptus.
units.tr: It is not idle that he does not simply say, "sins against the body and blood of the Lord," but says, "he will be guilty of the body and blood of the Lord." The Greek is ἔνοχος [enochos], a word that means not only one who sins but one who is bound over, because of his sin, to judgment and condemnation; other writers call such a person τίμωρος [timoros]. When he says "he will be guilty of the body and blood of the Lord," he therefore not only describes the kind of sin, but also threatens those who eat the bread and drink the cup of the Lord unworthily with a certain, grave condemnation and punishment. Indeed this sin is so serious that the one who commits it rightly becomes liable to a grave condemnation. A Christian ought to shudder if he hears that he will become guilty of the body and blood of the Lord, through which he has been redeemed from sin and death.

units.la: Dū hæc cogitamus mirari definimus, unde tot iam malorum ac calamitatum generibus obrutæ faceant ecclesiæ, in quibus sacramentum hoc dominici corporis ac sanguinis tot sæculis nepharijs modis contra manifestā ipsius institutionem quotidie prophanatur.
units.tr: As we think on these things, we cease to wonder how the churches, now overwhelmed by so many kinds of evils and calamities, are in such a state, in which this sacrament of the Lord's body and blood has for so many centuries been profaned every day in countless impious ways, against his own plain institution.

units.la: Probet autem seipsum homo, inquit, & sic de pane illo edat & de poculo illo bibat. Comminationi nondum absolutæ adhortationem immisicet, qua monet, quid facere debeat priusquam de pane hoc & poculo domini communicet, ne se tam graui condemnationi obnoxios reddat. Probet autem seipsum, inquit, homo. Græcè est δοκιμαζέτω. Significat hoc uerbum experimentum de re aliqua capere, & inquirere in illam ad cognoscedum qualis nam existat, ne per im prudetiam vel frustra vel cū detrimento etiam usurpetur. Cum hoc faciat prudentes in rebus terrenis ne quod moliuntur frustra moliantur, aut damnum aliquod accipiant, quanto magis faciendum est in re-
units.tr: "But let a man examine himself," he says, "and so let him eat of that bread and drink of that cup."
