Igitur & qui obdormierunt in Christo perierūt. Si in uita hac spem in Christo tantum fixam habemus, maxime miserabiles omnium hominum sumus.
units.tr: "But if Christ is preached as having risen from the dead, how do some among you say that there is no resurrection of the dead? If there is no resurrection of the dead, then Christ has not risen. But if Christ has not risen, then our preaching is empty, and your faith is empty too. Moreover we are found to be false witnesses of God, because we have testified of God that he raised up Christ, whom he did not raise, if indeed the dead do not rise. For if the dead do not rise, neither has Christ risen. And if Christ has not risen, your faith is futile; you are still in your sins. So also those who have fallen asleep in Christ have perished. If in this life we have only hope fixed in Christ, we are the most miserable of all men."

units.la: Hactenus duobus primis membris reuocauit Corinthijs in memoriam, quod nam & quomodo prædicauerit ipsis Euangelium de morte, sepultura ac resurrectione Christi, ac simul Apostolatū suum contra pseudapostolos asseruit, & Euangelium suum per id quod & ab aliis apostolis omnibus concorditer praedicaretur, & ab ipsis fide esset acceptum confirmauit: iam inde colligit tertio membro ex resurrectione Christi, quantum absurditatis ex eo consequatur, quod nonnulli resurrectionem mortuorum negabant, id quod diligenter argumentando facit, quo magis errorem illorum confutet. Seruat hac in re decorum fidelis Apostoli, qui non statim excommunicat, & Satanae tradit errantes, sed curat & satagit, quomodo eos ab errore liberet ac seruet, idq; per declarationem veritatis & confirmationem erroris. Ad hunc igitur scopum collimans argumentatur ex resurrectione Christi ad hunc modum.
units.tr: Up to this point, with the first two parts, he has reminded the Corinthians of what and how he preached the gospel to them concerning the death, burial and resurrection of Christ. At the same time he has asserted his apostleship against the false apostles, and has confirmed his gospel by the fact that it was preached in harmony with all the other apostles and was accepted in faith by them. From this point, in the third part, he draws from the resurrection of Christ how much absurdity follows from the view of some who denied the resurrection of the dead. He does this by careful argument, so that he may refute their error more thoroughly. In this matter he keeps to the proper conduct of a faithful apostle, who does not at once excommunicate, or hand over to Satan, those who err, but takes care and labours to free and keep them from error, and does so by declaring the truth and by confirming the error to be false. Aiming at this goal, then, he argues from the resurrection of Christ in the following way.

units.la: Quod si Christus praedicatur a mortuis resurrexisse, quomodo dicunt quidam inter uos resurrectionem mortuorum non esse? Statim initio argumentationis aperit, quorsum praecedentia de morte, sepultura, ac resurrectione Christi in medium attulerit. Ad confutandum uidelicet eos qui resurrectionem mortuorum negabant. Poterat dicere: Quod si Christus praedicatur a mortuis resurrexisse, consequitur & mortuos esse resurrecturos. Verum, ut errorum illorum tanquam manifeste praedicationi Euangelicae, de resurrectione Christi repugnantem admodum impudentem esse significet, uelut admirans dicit: Quod si Christus praedicatur a mortuis resurrexisse, quomodo dicut quidam inter uos resurrectionem mortuorum non esse? Quasi dicat: Mirum est, quomodo non uideant hanc suam opinionem pugnare cum doctrina & praedicatione Euangelij, qua communiter non a me tantum, sed & ab omnibus aliis apostolis de Christo praedicatur, quod sit mortuus ac sepultus, & quod tertio die resurrexit a mortuis. Quomodo admittunt errorem, inquit, qui tam manifeste Apostolicae praedicationi aduersatur?
units.tr: "But if Christ is preached as having risen from the dead, how do some among you say that there is no resurrection of the dead?" At the very start of the argument he reveals why he has brought forward what precedes about the death, burial and resurrection of Christ. Namely, to refute those who denied the resurrection of the dead. He could have said: "If Christ is preached as having risen from the dead, it follows that the dead will also rise." But in order to show that their error is very shameless, since it openly contradicts the evangelical preaching about the resurrection of Christ, he says in wonder: "But if Christ is preached as having risen from the dead, how do some among you say that there is no resurrection of the dead?" As if he said: "It is strange how they do not see that their opinion fights against the teaching and preaching of the gospel, which is preached about Christ by all the apostles in common, not by me alone, that he died and was buried, and that on the third day he rose from the dead. How do they admit," he says, "an error that so plainly opposes the apostolic preaching?"

units.la: QVOMODO dicut quidam, inquit, inter uos resurrectionem mortuorum non esse? Non dicit, quomodo dicitis uos: sed, quomodo dicunt quidam. Ergo non omnes sic dicebant, sed nonnulli tantum. Parcit itaq; reliquis.
units.tr: "How do some among you say," he says, "that there is no resurrection of the dead?" He does not say, "How do you yourselves say it?" but, "How do some say it?" So not all were saying this, but only some. He therefore spares the rest.

units.la: Neque dicit, quomodo cogitant quidam: sed, quomodo dicunt quidam. Ergo errorem suum non premebant in pectore, sed palam spargebant. Et hanc ob causam non agit cum illis separatim, sed publico scripto, cum tota ipsorum ecclesia, quo uirus noxium, quod spargebatur, cohibeat, ne totum corpus corripiat & inficiat.
units.tr: Nor does he say, "How do some think?" but, "How do some say?" So they were not keeping their error hidden in their breast, but were spreading it openly. And for this reason he does not deal with them separately, but by a public letter, addressed to their whole congregation, so that he may check the harmful poison that was being spread, lest it seize and infect the whole body.

units.la: Nec dicit simpliciter, quomodo dicut quidam: sed, quomodo dicunt quidam inter uos. Si illud ἐν ὑμῖν, id est, in uobis, referas ad quidam, significatur negatores istos resurrectionis pertinuisse ad ecclesiam fidelium. Si uero referas ad uerbum, dicunt, perstringitur illorum impudentia, qua non sunt ueriti articulum hunc de resurrectione mortuorum negare palam in medio fidelium. Quocunque re-
units.tr: Nor does he simply say, "How do some say?" but, "How do some among you say?" If you refer the phrase "among you" [ἐν ὑμῖν] to "some," it signifies that those who denied the resurrection belonged to the church of the faithful. But if you refer it to the verb "say," his shamelessness is exposed, since they did not fear to deny this article about the resurrection of the dead openly in the midst of the faithful. Whichever way you refer it, they were Christians, and they openly denied the resurrection of the dead, to the great offence of others.

units.la: feras, Christiani fuerunt, & resurrectionem mortuorum, magno cum offendiculo palam negarunt.
units.tr: ...whether you take it that way or that, they were Christians, and they openly denied the resurrection of the dead, to great offence.

units.la: QVOMODO dicunt quidam, inquit, inter uos resurrectionem mortuorum non esse? Quare non dicit: futuram non esse, sed in praesenti, non esse. Si de communi omnium resurrectione loquitur, qua in die nouissimo resurgemus, utiq; illa nec tum erat, neque nunc est. Quid igitur falsi erat, quod nonnulli eam non esse dicebant, cum id hodie quoque ueraciter dici queat ab omnibus?
units.tr: "How do some among you say," he says, "that there is no resurrection of the dead?" Why does he not say that it will not be, but that it is not, in the present? If he speaks of the general resurrection of all, by which we shall rise on the last day, then certainly that resurrection neither was then nor is now. What, then, was false in some men saying it was not, when today too it can be truly said by everyone?

units.la: Respondeo. Aliud est si dicas, resurrectio mortuorum nondum est: & aliud si dixeris, resurrectio mortuorum non est. Qui dicit illam nondum esse, futuram non negat. Qui uero simpliciter illam non esse dicit, negat huic fidei, qua mortuos resurrecturos credimus; aliquid inesse ueri, quod rem credamus esse ueram, quae sit falsa.
units.tr: I answer: it is one thing to say, "the resurrection of the dead is not yet," and another to say, "the resurrection of the dead is not." One who says it is not yet does not deny that it will be. But one who says simply that it is not, denies the faith by which we believe that the dead will rise; he implies that there is some truth in what we believe to be true, which is false.

units.la: Quare qui dicit, resurrectio mortuorum non est, perinde est, ac si dicat: resurrectio mortuorum nihil est, nomen est sine re, atque ita non modo in praesenti illam esse negat, sed & futuram non esse contendit. Si dixetis, iudicium quo mundus olim iudicandus creditur, non est, non solum in praesenti nondum esse, sed & futurum non esse dicet. Sic sentiunt impij: finis mundi non est, resurrectio mortuorum non est, iudicium non est, aliud saeculum non est: hoc est, mundus hic nunquam finietur, mortui non resurgent, iudicium mundi non erit, aliud saeculum post hoc praesens non erit. Hac impietatem in pectore fouentes, imo ipso ore spargentes Corinthij, dicebant resurrectionem mortuorum non esse, hoc est, nunquam fore ut mortui resurgant: sed hunc illius articulum merum esse figmentum, & impostu ram ad id excogitatam, ut opinione futuri iudicij, & noui cuiusdam saeculi retineatur mundus in officio, & cohibeantur hominum mentes, ne quid admittant scelerum ac flagitiorum, unde olim sint graues daturi poenas. Vtinam non sint hodie inter sapientes huius mundi, qui impietatem hanc in pectore fouent, eoq; securius huic sese mundo accommodent.
units.tr: So whoever says, "there is no resurrection of the dead," is saying the same as: "the resurrection of the dead is nothing; it is a name without a thing." Thus he not only denies that it is present, but also contends that it will not be in the future. If you were to say, "the judgment by which the world is believed to be judged one day is not," you would be saying not only that it is not yet present, but that it will not come in the future. So the wicked think: the end of the world is not, the resurrection of the dead is not, judgment is not, another age is not; that is, this world will never end, the dead will not rise, there will be no judgment of the world, and after this present age there will be no other age. The Corinthians, nursing this impiety in their breast and indeed spreading it by their very mouths, said that there was no resurrection of the dead, that is, that the dead would never rise; they held that this article was pure fiction and a deceit devised so that the world might be kept in check by the expectation of a future judgment and of some new age, and men's minds restrained from committing those crimes and outrages for which they would one day have to pay heavy penalties. I wish that there were not today among the wise men of this world those who nurse this impiety in their breast, and therefore accommodate themselves to this world all the more securely.

units.la: SI resurrectio mortuorum non est, inquit, neque Christus resurrexit.] Quasi dicat: Recogitent illi, qui resurrectionem mortuorum non esse dicunt, quid ex eo sequatur. Si resurrectio mortuorum non est, sicut ipsi dicunt, consequitur omnino, neq; Christum resurrexisse a mortuis. Argumentatur no affirmatiue a resurrectione Christi, ad generalem nostram resurrectionem, hoc est, a particulari ad uniuersalem: sed negatiue ab uniuersali resurrectione, quam Corinthiorum quidam negabant, ad particularem Christi, quam communiter omnes apostoli per Euangelium Dei praedicabant. Ideo non dicit: Si nanque Christus resurrexit, resurgent utique mortui. Hanc etenim consequentiam a particulari, ad uniuersalem, tanquam quam parum dialecticam, nullo modo rece- cepissent. Perinde nanque est,ac si dicas: Maria mater domini peperit uirgo, ergo omnes uirgines pariunt.
units.tr: "If there is no resurrection of the dead," he says, "neither has Christ risen." As if he said: let those who say there is no resurrection of the dead consider what follows from it. If there is no resurrection of the dead, as they themselves say, it follows altogether that Christ has not risen from the dead. He argues not affirmatively from the resurrection of Christ to our general resurrection, that is, from the particular to the universal, but negatively from the universal resurrection, which some of the Corinthians denied, to the particular resurrection of Christ, which all the apostles commonly preached through the Gospel of God. Therefore he does not say: "If Christ has risen, the dead will certainly rise." For they would in no way have accepted that inference from the particular to the universal, as being poor logic. It is just as if you were to say: "Mary, the mother of the Lord, bore a child while a virgin; therefore all virgins bear children."

units.la: Item, Asinus Bileam loquutus est humana uoce, ergo omnes asini humana uoce loquuntur. Non sequitur. Priuatum ac singulare miraculum non parit generale sui consequentiam. Quod Christus tertio die resurrexit a mortuis, miraculum est priuatu ac singulare, unde dialectica consequetia non sequitur sic omnes esse mortuos resurrecturos. Rectius ergo negatiue ab uniuersali, quam negabant, ad particularem Christi resurrectionem, quam & praedicabant apostoli concorditer omnes, & ipsi catholica fide credebant argumentatur, dicens: Si resurrectio mortuorum non est, neq; Christus resurrexit. Maluit colligere argumentando quid ex ipsorum negatione sequatur absur di ac falsi, quam quid ex communi Apostolorum praedicatione sequatur ueri.
units.tr: Likewise: "The ass of Balaam spoke with a human voice; therefore all asses speak with a human voice." This does not follow. A private and singular miracle does not yield a general consequence. That Christ rose from the dead on the third day is a private and singular miracle, so the dialectical consequence does not follow that all the dead will rise in the same way. It is therefore more correct to argue negatively from the universal, which they denied, to the particular resurrection of Christ, which all the apostles preached in agreement and which they themselves believed by the catholic faith, saying: "If there is no resurrection of the dead, neither has Christ risen." He preferred to draw by argument what absurd and false thing follows from their denial, rather than what truth follows from the common preaching of the apostles.

units.la: Omnino autem firma est consequentia, ab uniuersali ad particulare, qua dicit: Si resurrectio mortuorum non est, neq; Christus resurrexit. Etenim & mortuus fuit Christus & sepultus. Si impossibile est resurgere hominem mortuum, ergo nec Christus resurrexit. Qui infideles sunt, consequentiam hanc: Si resurrectio mortuorum non est, neq; Christus resurrexit, plane recipiunt ac dicunt: Sic est: Nec mortui resurgunt, nec Christus uester resurrexit.
units.tr: Indeed the consequence is wholly firm, from the universal to the particular, in which he says: "If there is no resurrection of the dead, neither has Christ risen." For Christ too died and was buried. If it is impossible for a dead man to rise, then Christ has not risen either. Unbelievers accept this consequence, "If there is no resurrection of the dead, neither has Christ risen," and plainly say: "So it is: neither do the dead rise, nor has your Christ risen."

units.la: Tam enim probandum est Christum uestrum resurrexisse, quam mortuos esse in fine mundi resurrecturos. Quare quod per resurrectionem Christi futuram mortuorum resurrectionem astruitis, infirmum est. Nil etenim ualet exemplum quod litem lite resoluit.
units.tr: For it must be proved that your Christ has risen just as much as that the dead are to rise at the end of the world. Therefore, your claim that by the resurrection of Christ the future resurrection of the dead is established is weak. For an example that resolves one dispute by another dispute is worth nothing.

units.la: Apostolus uero quoniam non agit cum infidelibus, sed cum Christianis, argumentatione utitur, quae illis sit fortissima. Hi nanque sic resurrectionem Christi credunt, ut propter illius firmitudinem retinendam resurrectionem mortuorum facile recipiat. Alijs plane argumentis usurus erat, si infidelibus resurrectionem mortuorum comprobandam suscepisset.
units.tr: But the apostle, since he is not dealing with unbelievers but with Christians, uses an argument that would be most forceful for them. For these believe in the resurrection of Christ in such a way that, in order to hold fast to its certainty, they readily accept the resurrection of the dead. Had he undertaken to prove the resurrection of the dead to unbelievers, he would clearly have used other arguments.

units.la: Cogitandum igitur nobis, uniuersam capitis huius argumentationem ac doctrinam sic esse comparatam, ut fidem Christianam requirat, quae resurrectionem Christi, tanquam Christi, unigeniti Dei, ac unici nostri Redemptoris, indubitato teneat. Nam huic tanquam fundamento omnis haec structura innititur.
units.tr: We must therefore consider that the whole argument and teaching of this chapter is so framed that it presupposes Christian faith, which holds the resurrection of Christ, as the Christ, the only-begotten Son of God and our only Redeemer, beyond doubt. For all this structure rests upon this as its foundation.

units.la: Verum pseudochristiani, qui mysterium mortis Christi, ac redemptionis nostrae, non tenentes sic credunt resurrexisse Christum, ut interim futuram mortuorum resurrectionem iudicium ac finem mundi, uitamque futuri saeculi non credant, argumentationem hanc Apostoli: Si resurrectio mortuorum non est, neque Christus resurrexit, quoniam in causa miraculosa est, & praeter seriem naturae insolita, non recipiunt: sed dicunt, Christus est non homo tantum, sicuti nos sumus, sed simul & uerus Deus, & unigenitus Dei, expers omnis peccati, quare a morte teneri non potuit. Nos uero nec dij sumus, sed homines: nec peccati expertes sicut ipse, sed peccatores, ideoque mortis mancipia, quare longe alia est nostra, quam ipsius conditio, ut non sequatur. Si resurrectio mortuorum non est, ergo nec Christus resurrexit: quemadmodum non sequitur, si uirgines non pariunt absque uirili femine, ergo nec Maria mater domini uirgo fine uirili femine peperit. Huiusmodi miraculosae ac singulares praerogatiuae non euincunt uniuersalem in omnes homines consequentiam.
units.tr: But false Christians, who do not hold the mystery of the death of Christ and of our redemption, believe that Christ rose in such a way that meanwhile they do not believe in the future resurrection of the dead, the judgment, the end of the world, and the life of the age to come. They do not accept the apostle's argument, "If there is no resurrection of the dead, neither has Christ risen," because it concerns a miraculous cause and something unusual beyond the order of nature. They say that Christ is not only a man, as we are, but at the same time true God and the only-begotten of God, free from all sin, and so could not be held by death. But we are neither gods nor men of that kind; we are sinners, not free from sin as he was, and therefore slaves of death. So our condition is far different from his, and the consequence does not follow: "If there is no resurrection of the dead, therefore neither has Christ risen," just as it does not follow: "If virgins do not bear children without a man, therefore neither did Mary, the mother of the Lord, a virgin, bear a child without a man." Such miraculous and singular privileges do not establish a universal consequence for all men.

units.la: Huiusmodi elusio retundenda est fortiter. Resurrexit enim Christus, quatenus est mortuus. Mortuus est autem, primum non ut Deus, sed ut homo, morte tam uera quam qua nos morimur: quare non resurrexit ut Deus, sed ut homo.
units.tr: Such an evasion must be firmly refuted. For Christ rose insofar as he died. But he died first not as God but as man, with a death as true as that by which we die. Therefore he rose not as God but as man.

units.la: Quod autem per diuinam potentiam morti exemptus resurrexit, nihil demit huic argumentationi. Etenim per eandem nos quoque resurgemus. Nec Apostolus cum dicit: Si resurrectio mortuorum non est, sic de illa loquitur, ut potentiam Dei excludat, ac dicat, Si homines mortui suis ac naturae uiribus non resurgunt, neque Christus resurrexit: sed potius hoc sensu, Si Deo posibile non est, ut mortuos excitet, ut resurgant, neque Christum excitauit ut resurgeret. Et hactenus firma est consequentia.
units.tr: That he was freed from death and rose by divine power takes nothing from this argument. For by the same power we too shall rise. Nor when the apostle says, "If there is no resurrection of the dead," does he speak of it in such a way as to exclude the power of God, as if to say: "If dead men do not rise by their own strength and nature, neither has Christ risen." Rather he means it in this sense: "If it is not possible for God to raise the dead so that they rise, neither has he raised Christ that he might rise." And so far the consequence is firm.

units.la: Deinde mortuus est Christus, non modo ut homo, sed ut mediator inter Deum & homines, nec mortuus est sine peccatis. Nam etsi per se ab omni fuit peccato alienus, nostra tamen uniuersa delicta & peccata, cum debita omnium condemnatione, in se suscepit, portauitq; in corpore suo super ligno, quo Deo patri pro illis satisfaceret, nosque ab aeterna morte & condemnatione liberaret, & cum Deo reconciliatos uitae aeternae participes redderet. Quod itaque resurrexit, resurrexit non ut homo simpliciter, sed ut Mediator, Redemptor, ac Seruator humani generis, deleto in cruce peccatorum nostrorum chirographo, uictor peccati & mortis, & aeternae uitae per Adamum amissae restitutor. Quod si peccata nostra non potuerunt ipsum retinere in morte, quam propter illa subijt, sed tanquam uicta & deleta liberum ac solutu dimiserunt: multo minus nos retinere poterunt, in quos nihil iuris habent amplius.
units.tr: Next, Christ died not only as man but as mediator between God and men, and he did not die without sins. For although in himself he was free from all sin, yet he took upon himself all our offences and sins, with the condemnation due to all, and bore them in his body upon the tree, so that he might make satisfaction to God the Father for them, free us from eternal death and condemnation, and make us, reconciled to God, partakers of eternal life. Therefore, he rose not simply as man, but as Mediator, Redeemer and Saviour of the human race, with the bond of our sins cancelled on the cross, victor over sin and death, and restorer of the eternal life lost through Adam. If our sins could not hold him in the death which he undertook on their account, but, overcome and cancelled, let him go free and released, much less will they be able to hold us, over whom they have no further right.

units.la: Quare Christi resurrectio non modo exemplum est futurae nostrae, sed ipsissima uirtus & causa. Necesse est igitur ut resurgamus. Verum hac de re in sequentibus. Hoc mortis ac resurrectionis Christi mysterium, si pseudochristiani inspicerent, & fide tenerent, haudquaquam argumentationi huic Apostoli contradiceret.
units.tr: Therefore Christ's resurrection is not only an example of our future resurrection but its very power and cause. It is necessary, then, that we rise. But more on this in what follows. If pseudo-Christians were to consider this mystery of Christ's death and resurrection and hold it by faith, they would by no means contradict this argument of the Apostle.

units.la: Nos admonemur, quam aliter fit argumentandum cum ueris Christianis, quam uel cum falsis, uel cum infidelibus. Habet fides nostra certa quę dam ac fundamētalia principia, contra quæ nihil sit recipiendum, nec disputandum cum illis, qui aliquod ex eis negare præsumunt. Tale est, quod Christus mortuus est pro peccatis nostris. Ergo non debemus eam recipere doctrinam, quæ humana merita aut satisfactiones statuit, quibus à peccatis liberemur. Potest enim hic tam firmiter colligi: Si nondum sumus à peccatis liberati, uel, Si pro peccatis nostris satisfaciendum nobis est, ergo Christus non est pro peccatis nostris mortuus, quàm firmiter colligit hic Apostolus: Si resurrectio mortuorum non est, Christus non resurrexit. Si quis neget mūdum hunc esse factum, nō est recipiendum quod tradit. Pugnat enim cum principio fidei nostræ, qua Deum credimus esse factorem cœli & terræ, ut recte argumentemur: Si mundus hic non est factus, ergo Deus non fecit cœlum & terram. Si quis dixerit: Deus non habet filios, argumentabitur Christianus: Si Deus non habet filios, ergo Christus non est filius Dei.
units.tr: We are reminded how differently one must argue with true Christians than with false ones or with unbelievers. Our faith has certain fundamental principles, and nothing contrary to them is to be accepted, nor is one to dispute with those who presume to deny any of them. Such a principle is this: that Christ died for our sins. Therefore we ought not to receive that teaching which sets up human merits or satisfactions by which we are freed from sins. For one can argue firmly here: If we are not yet freed from sins, or, If we must make satisfaction for our sins, then Christ did not die for our sins. This is as firm a conclusion as the Apostle's: If there is no resurrection of the dead, Christ has not risen. If anyone should deny that this world was made, what he teaches is not to be received, for it clashes with the principle of our faith, by which we believe God to be the maker of heaven and earth. So we argue rightly: If this world was not made, then God did not make heaven and earth. If someone says God has no sons, the Christian will argue: If God has no sons, then Christ is not the Son of God.

units.la: Argumētum ridiculum quidem iudicio infidelium, uerum haud aspernandum fidelibus, quorū fides est, Christum esse filium Dei. Hæc argumentandi ratio per omnia est fidei nostræ capita ducenda.
units.tr: This argument is indeed ridiculous in the judgment of unbelievers, but believers, whose faith is that Christ is the Son of God, should not scorn it. This mode of arguing is to be carried through all the articles of our faith.

units.la: S I uero Christus nō resurrexit, inquit, inanis igitur est prædicatio nostra, inanis est & fides uestra.] Pergit argumentando colligere quam absurda nascantur, & quanta subuersio religionis ac salutis nostræ sequatur, si Christum non resurrexisse concesserimus.
units.tr: "But if Christ has not risen," he says, "then our preaching is empty, and your faith is empty too." He goes on arguing, to gather how absurd consequences arise and how great an overthrow of our religion and salvation follows if we concede that Christ has not risen.

units.la: Primum, Si uero Christus nō resurrexit, inquit, inanis igitur est prædicatio nostra. Intelligit non de ea tantum Euangelij parte, qua Christus resurrexisse prędicatur, sed de ea tota Euangelij prædicatione & doctrina. Totam summam Euangelicæ prædicationis inanem esse dicit: Si Christus nō resurrexit. Tum enim frustra prædicatur de Deo, de uerbo incarnato, filio eius unigenito, de doctrina illius & miraculis, de morte ac sepultura, de pœnitentia & remissione peccatorum, & quæ alia in doctrina Euangelij continentur.
units.tr: First: "But if Christ has not risen," he says, "then our preaching is empty." He means not only that part of the Gospel in which Christ's resurrection is proclaimed, but the whole preaching and teaching of the Gospel. He says the entire sum of evangelical preaching is empty if Christ has not risen. For then preaching about God, about the incarnate Word, his only-begotten Son, about his teaching and miracles, his death and burial, repentance and the remission of sins, and whatever else is contained in the doctrine of the Gospel, would be in vain.

units.la: Nam hæc omnia pendent à resurrectione Mediatoris, qua mors est uicta, & iustificatio nostri impetrata. Poterat dicere: Si Christus nō resurrexit, ergo adhuc claustris mortis detinetur, nec est uictor mortis, sed à morte uictus. Si Christus non resurrexit, ergo pater deseruit suum filium, ac permisit, ut corruptionem uideret, uanusq; uates fuit Dauid in persona illius, dicens: Non derelinques animam meam in inferno, nec dabis sanctum tuum uidere corruptionem. Verum maluit argumentari ad ea absurda quæ in re tum omnibus nota consequerentur, prædicatione uidelicet Apostolica, magnis signis ac portentis declarata & confirmata.
units.tr: For all these things depend on the resurrection of the Mediator, by which death was conquered and our justification obtained. He could have said: If Christ has not risen, then he is still held in the prisons of death, and is not the conqueror of death but conquered by it. If Christ has not risen, then the Father has forsaken his Son and allowed him to see corruption, and David was a vain prophet in his person when he said: "You will not leave my soul in hell, nor will you suffer your Holy One to see corruption." But Paul preferred to argue from those absurdities which would follow in a matter known to all, namely the Apostolic preaching, declared and confirmed by great signs and wonders.

units.la: Neque enim de sua tantum, sed simul omnium apostolorum concordi prædicatione lo-
units.tr: For he speaks not only of his own preaching, but at the same time of the harmonious preaching of all the apostles, when he speaks

units.la: quitur, cum dicit: Inanis igitur est prædicatio nostra.
units.tr: of "our preaching is therefore empty."

units.la: Est autem prædicatio bifariam inanis. Primum, si nō recipiatur fide. Tum enim nō prodest audisse sermonem, quod is non fit eum fide coniunctus. Et hactenus potest prædicatio Euangelij, quantumuis uera in se & efficax ad saluandum credentes, inanis dici. Deinde, si quæ prædicantur sint, inania figmenta de rebus nihil ueri habentibus. Hoc sensu inanis esset prædicatio Apostolica in uniuersum, si Christus non resurrexisset.
units.tr: Preaching is empty in two ways. First, if it is not received in faith. For then it does not profit to have heard the word, since it is not joined with faith. In this respect the preaching of the Gospel, however true in itself and effective for saving believers, can be called empty. Second, if what is preached is empty fiction about things having no truth. In this sense the apostolic preaching in general would be empty if Christ had not risen.

units.la: Et hanc potissimum ob causam probro noƀis uertitur doctrina Christiana à Gentibus & Iudæis, & Turcis, quod prædicatur nobis de quodam crucifixo & mortuo Iesu Nazareno, esse illum Seruatorem mundi, cū seipsum seruare nequiuerit. Quoniam resurrectionem illius non credunt, existimant eum morte absorptum, nihil minus esse posse quàm quod per Euangelium Dei prædicatur.
units.tr: And for this chief reason the Christian teaching is turned into a reproach against us by Gentiles, Jews and Turks: that we preach of a certain crucified and dead Jesus of Nazareth that he is the Saviour of the world, when he could not save himself. Since they do not believe in his resurrection, they think he was swallowed up by death and can be nothing other than what the Gospel of God proclaims.

units.la: INANIS, inquit, est & fides uestra.] Consequitur hoc ex præcedēti. Etenim secundum qualitatem prædicationis est & qualitas fidei. Nam ex auditu est fides, Roman. 10. Quare necesse est, ut ex inani prædicatione fit inanis fides. Est autem fides inanis, quando uel uanum est quod creditur, ut etsi uerum sit, opinione tamen magis quàm efficaci fide recipitur. Fides mortua, otiosa & inefficax, plane est inanis.
units.tr: "Empty," he says, "is also your faith." This follows from what has gone before. For the quality of faith follows the quality of preaching, since faith comes from hearing, Rom. 10. Hence it is necessary that empty preaching produces empty faith. Faith is empty when what is believed is vain, so that even if it is true, it is received by opinion rather than by an effective faith. Dead, idle and ineffective faith is plainly empty.

units.la: Verum priore sensu loquitur hic Apostolus, significans eos, qui prædicationem inanem fide recipiunt, fidem habere non ueram, sed falsam & inanem. Erant hæc dura auditu coram ecclesia Dei, prædicationem uidelicet de Christo Euangelicam & Apostolicam, & fide Christianam utranque reddi inanem per eos, qui resurrectionem mortuorum negabat. Verum sic oportebat fidelium mētibus perniciosi dogmatis horrorem incutere, malumq; illius statim initio detegere.
units.tr: But the Apostle here speaks in the former sense, signifying that those who receive empty preaching by faith have not true faith but false and empty faith. These things were hard to hear before the church of God: that the preaching about Christ, both evangelical and apostolic, and the Christian faith are both rendered empty by those who deny the resurrection of the dead. But it was fitting thus to strike horror of this pernicious dogma into the minds of believers, and to expose its evil at once from the beginning.

units.la: Sic faciendum est & illis, qui hodie non uerētur dicere. Homines fuisse qui libros Veteris ac Noui testamenti conscripserunt, ideoque sacram scripturam non esse diuinam, sed humanam: nec plus mereri fidei, quàm quatenus certis rationibus ac demonstrationibus possit probari. Dicatur hic: Si sacra scriptura non est diuina, sed humana, inanis est prædicatio Apostolica, inanis est fides Christiana, & Christus cum suis apostolis merito sunt, tanquam seductores orbis reprobati & occisi. Sic impij homines quo dogmata, errores, ac superstitiones Papismi sui tueantur uniuersum Christianismum, doctrinam, fidem, Christum ipsum cum prophetis & apostolis subuertunt. Inculcandum est hoc ecclesię Dei, ueris ac syn ceris fidelibus, quo ad huiusmodi uoces aures ambas & pectus occludant, ac uirus Satanæ detestentur. Regeramus illis: Si satisfaciendum, satis patiendum, ac satis dandum nobis est pro peccatis nostris, secundum dogmata Papistica, ergo Christus uel non est uel frustra est pro peccatis nostris mortuus, & inanis est praedicatio ac fides apostolica.
units.tr: So we must also deal with those who today do not hesitate to say that men wrote the books of the Old and New Testaments, and that therefore Sacred Scripture is not divine but human, and deserves no more faith than as far as it can be proved by certain reasons and demonstrations. Let this be said to them: If Sacred Scripture is not divine but human, then Apostolic preaching is empty, Christian faith is empty, and Christ with his apostles are rightly rejected as seducers of the world and put to death. Thus impious men, in order to defend the dogmas, errors and superstitions of their Papism, overthrow all of Christianity: doctrine, faith, Christ himself, with the prophets and apostles. This must be impressed upon the church of God, upon true and sincere believers, so that they close both ears and heart to such voices and detest the poison of Satan. Let us reply to them: If, according to Papistical dogmas, we must make satisfaction, must suffer enough and must give enough for our sins, then Christ either is not, or has died in vain for our sins, and apostolic preaching and faith are empty.

units.la: Verum absit. Christus uere est & efficaciter pro peccatis nostris mortuus, ideoq; inanis est & praedicatio & fides Papistica. Sacra scriptura non ex hominibus, sed ex Deo ac uera est, ergo cōtraria illi Papisimi doctrina & fides uera esse non potest, sed inanis sit oportet.
units.tr: But far be it. Christ truly and effectively died for our sins, and therefore Papistical preaching and faith are empty. Sacred Scripture is from God, not from men, and it is true; therefore the teaching and faith of Papism, being contrary to it, cannot be true, but must be empty.

units.la: Quæsierit hic quisquam, an omnino inanem oporteat esse fidem in illis locis, ubi inanis est publica praedicatio. At facilis est respondio. Inanem esse oportet, qua inani praedicationi creditur. Verum reperias illic quoque electas Christi ouiculas, quæ uocem falsorum pastorum repudiates uocem ueri sui pastoris audiant & sequantur, ideoque publicæ praedicationi non credat, sed sanctas scripturas potius legant, illisq; uera fide nitantur. Horum fides non est inanis, quantumuis inanis sit publica praedicatio.
units.tr: Someone might ask whether faith must be altogether empty in those places where public preaching is empty. The answer is easy. Faith must be empty when it believes empty preaching. But you will find there too Christ's elect sheep, who reject the voice of false ministers and hear and follow the voice of their true shepherd, and who therefore do not put their trust in public preaching, but rather read the holy Scriptures and rest on them with true faith. The faith of these is not empty, however empty public preaching may be.

units.la: Reperimur autem & falsi testes Dei, inquit, quoniam testificati sumus de Deo, quod Christum excitauerit, quem non excitauit, si uidelicet mortui non resurgunt.
units.tr: Moreover we are found also to be false witnesses of God, he says, because we have testified of God that he raised up Christ, whom he did not raise up, if indeed the dead do not rise.

units.la: Deinceps haec duo absurda, inanis est praedicatio nostra: &, inanis est fides uestra, non nihil exaggerat. Et primum de praedicatione: Reperimur autē & falsi testes Dei, inquit, &c. Quasi dicat: Non solum autem inanis est praedicatio nostra, si Christus non resurrexit, sed & haec consequitur impietas, quod de Deo falsò simus testificati, quod uidelicet excitauerit Christum, quem non excitauit, si mortui non resurgunt: simusque adeo non solum seductores mundi, inania praedicantes, sed & falsi testes Dei, falsum de illo testificantes, atque itaque duplici nomine digni, quos ipsa terra aperto ore absorbeat.
units.tr: He then adds two absurdities, "our preaching is empty" and "your faith is empty," which is not a little exaggeration. And first, concerning the preaching: "We are found also to be false witnesses of God," he says, and so on. It is as if he said: our preaching is not only empty if Christ has not risen, but this impiety follows as well, that we have testified falsely of God, namely that he raised up Christ, whom he did not raise up, if the dead do not rise. Thus we would be not only deceivers of the world, preaching empty things, but also false witnesses of God, bearing false testimony concerning him, and therefore deserving of a double charge, so that the earth itself should swallow us up with open mouth.

units.la: Illud, quoniam testificati sumus de Deo, in Græco est κατὰ θεοῦ, quod uetus interpres reddidit, aduersus Deum, quemadmodum & Ambrosius & Augustinus legunt: & Germanicus interpres uertit, Vuider Gott. Erasmus tamen uertit, de Deo. Sane nonnunquam, præsertim apud dialecticos, reperitur præpositio κατὰ hoc sensu genitiuo iungi, ut cum dicimus animal praedicari κατ' ἀνθρώπου, id est, de homine. Aliquando κατὰ θεοῦ sensu iurandi idem est quod per Deum. At non conuenit ut sic accipiamus hoc loco.
units.tr: The phrase "we have testified of God" is in the Greek κατὰ θεοῦ [kata theou], which the old translator rendered "against God," as both Ambrose and Augustine read it. The German translator renders it "Wider Gott" (against God). Erasmus, however, translates it "of God." Certainly the preposition κατά [kata] is sometimes joined with the genitive in this sense, especially among the dialecticians, as when we say that an animal is predicated κατὰ ἀνθρώπου [kata anthrōpou], that is, "of man." Sometimes κατὰ θεοῦ [kata theou] in the sense of an oath means the same as "by God." But it does not fit to take it in that way here.

units.la: Nascitur ergo alia atque alia particulæ huius expositio. Qui legunt: quoniam testificati sumus aduersus Deum, sic sentiût culpari apostolos hac consequetia, ut extra culpa sit Deus, ipsi uero in illum impij deprehendantur. Et hinc est, quod colligitur ex hoc loco, impium esse testificari de Deo quod fecerit quæ non fecit, aut quod faciat quæ non facit: uel quod facturus sit, quæ facturus nō est, non mala modo ac uituperanda, sed & bona ac laudanda, quale est, excitasse Christum filium suum à mortuis.
units.tr: So there arises one interpretation after another of this phrase. Those who read "we have testified against God" understand the apostles to be blamed by this consequence, so that God is free from fault while they are caught as impious. And from this passage it is gathered that it is impious to testify of God that he has done what he has not done, or that he will do what he will not do, and that this is evil and worthy of reproach, but also when it is good and worthy of praise, as is the case with saying that he raised his Son Christ from the dead.

units.la: Sic Augustinus Epist. octaua ad Hieronymum loco præsenti utitur, dicens: Possunt uideri etiam de laudibus Dei esse officiosa mendacia, apud homines pigriores dilectio eius ardesceat, atque ita nusquam certa erit in libris sanctis castę ueritatis authoritas. Nonne attendimus eundem Apostolum, cum ingenti cura commendandæ ueritatis dicere: Si autē Christus non resurrexit, inanis est praedicatio nostra, inanis est & fides uestra. Inuenimur autē & falsi testes Dei, quia testimonium diximus aduersus Deum, quod suscitauit Christum quem non suscitauit.
units.tr: Thus Augustine, in his eighth epistle to Jerome, uses this passage, saying: "Even concerning the praises of God, officious lies may seem permissible, so that among more sluggish men his love may burn more brightly; and so nowhere will the authority of the holy books of pure truth be certain. Do we not notice that the same Apostle, with great care to commend the truth, says: 'If Christ has not risen, our preaching is empty, your faith is empty also. We are found also to be false witnesses of God, because we have said that we testified against God that he raised up Christ, whom he did not raise up.'"

units.la: Si quis huic diceret, quid in hoc mendacio perhorrescis, cum id dixeris, quod etiamsi falsum sit, ad laudē Dei maxime pertinet? Nonne huius detestatus insaniam, quibus posset uerbis & significationibus in lucem penetralia cordis sui aperiret, clamans, non minore, aut fortasse etiam maiore scelere, in Deo laudari falsitatem, quàm uituperari ueritatem?
units.tr: If someone were to say to him: "Why do you shrink in horror from this lie, since you have said something which, even if false, pertains greatly to the praise of God? Would you not, having abhorred its madness, reveal by whatever words and signs you could the inner sanctuary of your heart, crying out that falsehood praised in God is no less, or perhaps even a greater, wickedness than truth blamed?"

units.la: Hæc ille, quæ ex eo argumentatur, quod legit: quia testimonium diximus aduersus Deū quod suscitauit Christum, quem non suscitauit. Plane sic habet. Quoniam & ueracissimus est Deus & simul iustissimus, non potest aduersus illius ueritatem & iusticiam, grauius peccari, quàm si quis de illo falsum ferat testimonium.
units.tr: So he writes, arguing from what he reads: "because we have testified against God that he raised up Christ, whom he did not raise up." Plainly it stands thus: since God is both most truthful and at the same time most just, no greater sin can be committed against his truth and justice than when someone bears false witness concerning him.

units.la: Est autem falsum testimonium quod contra Deum fieri potest, quadruplex. Etenim per illud aut quod uerum est in Deo negamus, aut quod falsum est afferimus: uel quod malum est tribuendo illi laudamus, uel quod bonum est uituperamus. Quare late patet hoc malum, in quod incurrant necesse est, qui de Deo docere ac praedicare præsumunt, quæ nullis sacris scripturis traditur, sed uel ab alijs uel ab ipsis humanitus sunt excogitata. Verum autem gravius fiat peccatum laudare in Deo quod est falsum, uel uituperare quod est uerum, iudicent alij. Existimo multum referre, quomodo hæc, & quibus circumstantijs, quoque propositio fiant.
units.tr: Now false testimony that can be made against God is of four kinds. For by it we either deny what is true of God, or assert what is false; or by ascribing to him what is evil we praise him, or by disparaging what is good we blame him. Wherefore this evil, into which those necessarily fall who presume to teach and preach about God things that are not handed down in any holy Scripture but have been devised by others or by men themselves, has a wide scope. Whether it is a greater sin to praise in God what is false, or to disparage what is true, let others judge. I think it makes a considerable difference how, and in what circumstances, and with what intention, these things are done.

units.la: Qui uero legunt: quoniam testificati sumus de Deo, fugiunt hac sententiam, qua testimonium falsum de Deo, etiam in re laudabili, aduersarium esse Deo colligitur.
units.tr: Those, however, who read "we have testified concerning God" avoid this sense, by which it is inferred that false testimony concerning God, even in a praiseworthy matter, is hostile to God.

units.la: Nonnulli etiam sic exponunt, ut Deū ipsum hoc falsi testimonij peccato inuoluant, quasi author fuerit apostolis rem falsam de se, laudis gratia testificandi. Sane sic fuerint apostoli testes Dei, ut haud proprio arbitratu munus hoc de morte ac resurrectione Christi testificandi usurparint: sed ad hoc diuinitus sint electi ac constituti, unde & Christus dicebat ad eos, Vos eritis mihi testes, &c. Et Petrus Actor. 10. Huc Deus suscitauit tertio die, & dedit eum manifesmanifestum fieri non omni populo, sed testi- bus præordinatis à Deo, nobis, qui manduca- uimus & bibimus cum illo, postquam resur- rexit à mortuis. Et præcepit nobis prædicare populo & testificari, &c. Quare si testimonium apostolorum quod cōstitutione diuina de Chri- sto tulerunt, falsum fuit, non illi tantum, sed cum primis Deus ipse tanquam illius author, falsi testimonij reus est. Habet hic sensus uim magnam ad incutiendum horrore contra im- piam præsumptionem eorum, qui resurrectio- nem mortuorum negabant, unde absurda hæc & impia colligi potuerunt. Nihil uideo pericu li, utram expositionem accipiamus.
units.tr: Some also explain it in such a way as to involve God himself in this sin of false testimony, as if he were the author for the apostles of a false thing about himself, to be testified for the sake of praise. Certainly the apostles were witnesses of God in such a way that they did not assume this office of testifying about the death and resurrection of Christ by their own choice; rather, they were chosen and appointed to it by God, whence also Christ said to them, "You shall be my witnesses," and so on. And Peter, Acts 10: "God raised him up on the third day and granted that he be made manifest, not to all the people, but to witnesses ordained beforehand by God, to us who ate and drank with him after he rose from the dead. And he commanded us to preach to the people and to testify," and so on. Therefore, if the testimony of the apostles, which by divine appointment they bore concerning Christ, was false, then not only they but chiefly God himself, as its author, is guilty of false testimony. This sense has great force for striking horror into the impious presumption of those who denied the resurrection of the dead, from which these absurdities and impieties could be inferred. I see no danger in adopting either interpretation.

units.la: Obserua quod non simpliciter dicit: Repe- rimur autem & falsi apostoli Dei, quoniā præ- dicamus de Deo, quod excitauerit Christum, &c. sed: Reperimur autem & falsi testes Dei, quoniam testificati sumus de Deo, quod exci- tauerit Christum, &c. Verbum testificandi cō- sulto usurpauit. Erat enim hoc peculiare apo- stolorum munus, ut essent testes Dei, testificā- tes de Deo ac Christo filio eius quæ uiderant, & contrectauerant. Aliud est simpliciter præ- dicare de Christo, quod mortuus ac sepultus tertio die resurrexit, & aliud ista de illo testifi- cari. Prius est omnium uerbi ministrorum usque ad fine mûdi, posterius uero apostolorû tantû, qui dicere potuerût: quod uidimus testamur.
units.tr: Observe that he does not simply say, "we are found also to be false apostles of God, because we preach concerning God that he raised up Christ," and so on, but: "we are found also to be false witnesses of God, because we have testified concerning God that he raised up Christ," and so on. He deliberately chose the verb "to testify." For it was the particular office of the apostles to be witnesses of God, testifying concerning God and his Son Christ what they had seen and handled. It is one thing simply to preach about Christ, that he died and was buried and on the third day rose again, and another to testify these things concerning him. The former belongs to all ministers of the Word until the end of the world, but the latter to the apostles alone, who could say: "What we have seen, we testify."

units.la: QVEM non excitauit, inquit, si mortui non resurgunt.] Non dicit, si mortui nō resurgent: sed in præsenti, si mortui nō resurgunt: quem- admodum & supra nō dixit, quomodo dicunt quidam inter uos resurrectionem mortuorū nō esse futuram: sed simpliciter in præsenti, re- surrectionem mortuorum non esse, ubi ratio- nem reddidimus, quare sic loqui uoluerit.
units.tr: "Whom he did not raise up," he says, "if the dead do not rise." He does not say "if the dead will not rise," but in the present tense, "if the dead do not rise," just as above he did not say "how some among you say that there will be no resurrection of the dead," but simply in the present, "that there is no resurrection of the dead," where we gave the reason why he wished to speak thus.

units.la: Etenim si mortui non resurgunt, inquit, ne- que Christus resurrexit. Quoniam dixit, Qué non excitauit, si mortui non resurgunt: reddit illius rationem, imò supra redditam repetit, di cens: Etenim si mortui non resurgunt, neque Christus resurrexit. Sic supra dixit: Si resurre- ctio mortuorum non est, neq; Christus resurre xit. Sensus supra est expositus. Si Deus nō ex- citat mortuos, mortui non resurgunt: atque i- deo nec Christus resurrexit, quia Deus illū nō excitauit, quod mortuos non excitet.
units.tr: "For if the dead do not rise," he says, "neither has Christ risen." Since he said, "whom he did not raise up, if the dead do not rise," he gives the reason for it, or rather repeats the reason given above, saying: "For if the dead do not rise, neither has Christ risen." So above he said: "If there is no resurrection of the dead, neither has Christ risen." The sense has been explained above: if God does not raise the dead, the dead do not rise; and therefore Christ has not risen either, because God did not raise him up, since he does not raise the dead.

units.la: QVOD si Christus nō resurrexit, inquit, su peruacanea est fides uestra.] Resumit alterum absurdū, nempe, inanis est fides uestra, si Chri stus non resurrexit: illudque quemadmodum prius, penitus explicat. Ideo subiungit: Adhuc estis in peccatis uestris. Quèadmodum enim uera in Christum fides liberat credentes à pec catis, uirtute uidelicet mortis ac resurrectio- nis Christi: ita si Christus nō resurrexit, & fides in illū prorsus est inanis, consequitur esse nos adhuc in peccatis nostris. Neq; enim fieri po- test, ut inani quisquā fide à peccatis liberetur.
units.tr: "But if Christ has not risen," he says, "your faith is vain." He takes up the second absurdity, namely, your faith is empty if Christ has not risen, and he explains this fully, just as he did the first. Therefore he adds: "You are still in your sins." For just as true faith in Christ frees believers from sins, by the power, namely, of the death and resurrection of Christ, so if Christ has not risen, and faith in him is utterly empty, it follows that we are still in our sins. For it cannot happen that anyone is freed from sins by an empty faith.

units.la: ADHVC estis, inq̈t, in peccatis uestris.] Er go, quia Christus à mortuis resurrexit, sic non est fides credentiū in ipsum inanis, ut non sint ampliꝰ in peccatis. Quid igitur est quod 1.Io.1. dicitur: Si dixerimus quod peccatum non ha- beamus, nos ipsos seducimus, & ueritas in no- bis non est. Et quod hic ipse Apost.Ro.7. de eo tantopere queritur, quod peccatum habitet in ipsius carne? An soli Corinthij propter fidem in Christum nō erant amplius in peccatis suis, erat uero adhuc ipse Apostolus, & sunt reliqui fideles omnes donec uiuunt in peccatis?
units.tr: ADHUC you are, he says, in your sins. Therefore, because Christ rose from the dead, the faith of those who believe in him is not so empty that they are no longer in their sins. What then is meant by 1 John 1: "If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us"? And why does this same Apostle complain so much in Romans 7 that sin dwells in his flesh? Or were the Corinthians alone no longer in their sins because of their faith in Christ, while the Apostle himself, and all the other faithful as long as they live, remain in sins?

units.la: Respondeo. Aliud esse in peccatis, & aliud habere peccatum, uel peccatum esse in nobis. Esse in peccatis Apostolo est, esse in reatu pec- catorum, ac condemnationi obnoxiam. Sic in peccatis est omne genus mortaliū, extra Chri- stum. Credentes uero in Christum, habet qui- dem adhuc peccatum in carne sua: uerum quo niam liberati sunt à reatu peccatorum & con- demnatione per sanguinem Christi, non sunt amplius in peccatis, sed fide iustificati. Qui a- lieni sunt à fide Christi, sunt in peccatis om- nes, & peccatum in ipsis regnat ac dominatur. Fideles igitur, quamuis non sunt amplius in peccatis & condemnatione, agnoscunt tamen adhuc in carne sua peccati malitiam, deq; illa cum Apostolo dolenter queruntur, tam abest ut dicant se non habere peccatum.
units.tr: I answer: to be in sins is one thing; to have sin, or to have sin dwelling in us, is another. For the Apostle, to be in sins is to be in the guilt of sins and liable to condemnation. In this sense the whole race of mortals is in sins, apart from Christ. But those who believe in Christ indeed still have sin in their flesh; yet since they are freed from the guilt of sins and from condemnation through the blood of Christ, they are no longer in sins, but justified by faith. All who are estranged from the faith of Christ are in sins, and sin reigns and rules in them. The faithful, therefore, although they are no longer in sin and condemnation, nevertheless acknowledge in their flesh the malice of sin, and with the Apostle they complain of it with grief; so far are they from saying that they have no sin.

units.la: IGITVR & qui obdormierunt in Christo, inquit, perierunt.] Sic incommodum ex incō- modo nascitur. Si Christus non resurrexit, ina nis est Christianorum fides. Si fides inanis est, sumus adhuc in peccatis nostris. Si adhuc in peccatis sumus, consequitur pire eos qui moriun- tur in Christo. Retinentur. n. æternæ mortis uinculis, ppter peccata in quib. sunt mortui.
units.tr: THEREFORE those also who have fallen asleep in Christ, he says, have perished. Thus one disadvantage arises from another. If Christ has not risen, the faith of Christians is empty. If the faith is empty, we are still in our sins. If we are still in our sins, it follows that those who die in Christ perish. For they are held in the chains of eternal death on account of the sins in which they died.

units.la: Cauendum uero est, ne uerbum, perierunt, idem esse sentiamus, quod in nihilû abierunt, prius anima & corpore extincti sunt, ut nihil de illis maneat reliqui. Nam animæ mortuorū tam fidelium quàm infidelium supersunt, licet impari forte, donec in die iudicij corporibus suis reddantur. Pereunt tamen infideles, dum moriuntur, propterea quod æternæ sunt mor ti & condemnationi obnoxij.
units.tr: We must take care, however, that we do not think the word "perished" means the same as "went into nothing," as if they were first destroyed in soul and body so that nothing of them remained. For the souls of the dead, both faithful and unfaithful, survive, although perhaps in a lesser state, until in the day of judgment they are restored to their bodies. Unbelievers, however, do perish when they die, because they are liable to eternal death and condemnation.

units.la: Quod fideles attinet, qui in Christo, hoc est, in fide, & si ita uisum fit Deo, propter fidē Chri sti moriuntur, non moriuntur illi, sed obdor- miunt, propter sequuturam resurrectionē non animarum, sed corporum: nec pereunt, sed spi ritu transeunt à morte in uitam, licet corpore quiescant in terra. Quare uigilâter factum est, quod loca sepulturę Christianorum uocarunt κοιμητήρια, id est, dormitoria, nō propter animas quæ non in sepultura cum corporibus condū- tur, sed in cœlestia deportâtur, sed propter cor pora in sepulchris quiescentia, indeq; uelut è cubili in die Domini proditura.
units.tr: As for the faithful, who die in Christ, that is, in faith, and if it so pleases God, die because of faith in Christ, they do not die but fall asleep, looking to the resurrection that will follow, not of souls but of bodies; nor do they perish, but in spirit they pass from death into life, although their bodies rest in the earth. Wisely, therefore, Christians called the places of burial κοιμητήρια, that is, dormitories: not because souls are buried with the bodies in the grave, but because souls are carried off to heaven, while the bodies resting in the tombs will thence come forth, as from a bed, on the day of the Lord.

units.la: Consulto itaq; non dixit: Igitur qui mortui sunt, sed qui obdormierunt in Christo. Quam- uis enim resurrectionem mortuorū nonnulli negabant, quorum dementiam præsenti argu- mentatione corrigi: nihilo tamen secius incon cussa
units.tr: Deliberately, then, he did not say "those who have died," but "those who have fallen asleep in Christ." For although some denied the resurrection of the dead, and their madness is corrected by the present argument, nevertheless the truth of Christian doctrine and faith was equally unshaken; and therefore those who had died had fallen asleep in Christ, they had not perished.

units.la: A
units.tr: A

units.la: B cussa erat Christianæ doctrinæ pariter ac fidei veritas: ideoq; qui obierant, in Christo obdormierant, non perierant.
units.tr: B the truth was unshaken. Therefore those who had died had fallen asleep in Christ; they had not perished.

units.la: Dicet hic quisquam de numero eorum qui Romano papatui adhærēt: Maiores nostri crediderūt Christum resurrexisse à mortuis, & in ea fide, in qua nos sumus, obdormierunt, ergo non perierunt. Siquidē virtute resurrectionis Christi credentes in ipsum, nō pereunt, sed servantur. Seruabimur itaq; & nos in fide hac Romanæ ecclesiæ manentes, in qua ipsi obdormierunt & salui facti sunt.
units.tr: Someone from among those who cleave to the Roman papacy may say here: Our forefathers believed that Christ rose from the dead, and they fell asleep in that faith in which we also stand; therefore they did not perish. For those who believe in him through the power of Christ's resurrection do not perish, but are kept safe. Therefore we too shall be kept safe, remaining in this faith of the Roman Church, in which they themselves fell asleep and were made safe.

units.la: Respondeo. Verum est, qui credunt in Christum pro peccatis nostris mortuum, sepultū, & tertio die à mortuis excitatum, non pereūt, sed servantur. Deinde, facile credimus fuisse in Papatu tot iam elapsis, seculis multos fideles ab initio ad vitam in Christo electos: quibus symbolū apostolicæ fidei cordi fuerit, & Christus totius fidei, spei ac salutis anchora. Tertio de illis recte credimus, quod propter fundamentum Christum, cui innixi fuere credentes, in cuius etiam fide obdormierunt, non perierint, sed saluati sint & vitæ æternæ participes. Hinc tamen nō potest recte colligi, quod propter Papisticæ religionis non fidem, sed superstitiones salui sint facti: uel quisquā ob id debeat in Papatu manere, quod maiores nostri in illo sunt mortui. Aliud est enim manere in fide mortis ac resurrectionis Christi, in qua sola est salus & vita: & aliud manere scienter ac prudenter in Papatu, per quē nemo saluatur, innumeri vero perduntur. Singulari ope Dei multi seruantur in mari, & licet in naufragium inciderint, eripiūtur tamen. Nemo tamē sic insanit, ut dicat, manebo in mari. nā multi in illo sunt hactenus seruati. Mare quoddam est Papatus, innumeris procellis, uoraginibus, syrtib. scyllis, charybdibus, & aliis errorum, falsorum cultuum, superstitionū, tenebrarum, captiuitatis conscientiarum, tyrannidis & improbi dominatus periculis refertū: in quo innumera millia falsorum Christianorū perierunt ac pereūt: qui vero servati sunt & adhuc servantur, admirabili ac singulari gratia Dei per fidem in Christum seruati sunt, perinde atq; septē illa millia fidelium, qui tempore Eliæ singulariter sic fuerūt seruati à Deo, ut genua sua nō incuruarint ante Baal, quorū metio in Ro.cap.II. facta est.
units.tr: I answer: It is true that those who believe in Christ, who was dead for our sins, buried, and raised up from the dead on the third day, do not perish but are kept safe. Next, we readily believe that in the Papacy, over the many centuries that have now passed, there were many faithful people from the beginning chosen to life in Christ, for whom the creed of the apostolic faith was dear to the heart, and for whom Christ was the anchor of all faith, hope and salvation. Thirdly, we rightly believe about those that, because of Christ the foundation, on whom the believers rested, and in whose faith they also fell asleep, they did not perish, but were saved and became partakers of eternal life. Yet from this it cannot rightly be concluded that they were made safe because of the Papist religion, not by faith but by superstitions; or that anyone ought to remain in the Papacy because our forefathers died in it. For it is one thing to remain in faith in the death and resurrection of Christ, in which alone is salvation and life; and it is another to remain knowingly and deliberately in the Papacy, through which no one is saved, while countless numbers perish. By the singular help of God many are preserved at sea, and although they have fallen into shipwreck, they are nevertheless snatched away. Yet no one is so mad as to say, "I will remain at sea," because many have hitherto been preserved in it. The Papacy is a sea full of countless storms, whirlpools, sandbanks, Scyllas and Charybdises, and the dangers of other errors, false worships, superstitions, darkness, captivity of consciences, tyranny and wicked domination; in it countless thousands of false Christians have perished and are perishing; but those who have been saved, and are still being saved, have been saved by the admirable and singular grace of God through faith in Christ, just as those seven thousand faithful, who in the time of Elijah were singularly preserved by God so that they did not bow their knees before Baal, whose number is mentioned in Romans 11.

units.la: SI in uita hac tantum spem positam habemus in Christū, inquit, miserabiliores sumus omnibus hominibus: uel, ut quidā uertūt, miserrimi sumus omnium hominum.] Postremum hoc est absurdum & incomodum. Si resurrectio mortuorum nō est, nulla nobis post hanc erit uita futura. Si nō uiuemus post hanc uitam, ergo fides nostra ac spes de Christo coepta præsenti hac uita sic terminatur, ut nihil nobis post illam inde fit emolumēti futurum, etiamsi ille à mortuis resurrexerit. Quid hinc cōsequetur aliud, quàm spem Christianorum esse temporariam ac præsentis tantū uitæ, atq;
units.tr: IF we have placed our hope in Christ in this life only, he says, we are more wretched than all men; or, as some translate it, we are the most wretched of all men. This last point is absurd and disadvantageous. If there is no resurrection of the dead, there will be no future life for us after this one. If we do not live after this life, then our faith and hope begun in Christ are so bounded by the present life that nothing of advantage from it will come to us afterwards, even if he has risen from the dead. What else would follow from this, than that the hope of Christians is temporary and belongs only to the present life, and so Christians are the most unhappy of all mortals?

units.la: ita Christianos omnium esse mortalium infelicissimos. Sic puto particulā hanc habere occupationem, ne obiiciat quisquam: Etsi nō credimus futurā esse mortuorū resurrectionē, credimus tamen Christum esse à mortuis excitatum, illiq; tanquam nostro domino spe ac fiducia adhæremus. Ergo, inquit, in hac tantum uita habemus dominū Christum: & spes nostra quæ in illum est, huius tantum uitæ bona spectat. Nam etiamsi ille à mortuis excitatus, non est moriturus amplius, sed uicturus in sempiternum: nobis tamen prodesse nō poterit, nisi uiuamus & ipsi. Itaque si totam spem nostram in Christum præsentis tantū uitæ bonis & cōmodis metimur, nemo nobis ex omnibus est mortalibus infelicior.
units.tr: Thus I think this particle has the following force, lest anyone object: Even if we do not believe that the resurrection of the dead is to come, we nevertheless believe that Christ has been raised from the dead, and we cling to him as our Lord with hope and trust. Therefore, he says, we have the Lord Christ only in this life; and our hope that is in him looks only to the goods of this life. For even if he, raised from the dead, is not going to die again but will live for ever, nevertheless he cannot benefit us unless we also live. Therefore, if we measure our whole hope in Christ by the goods and advantages of this life alone, no one is more unhappy than we are among all mortals.

units.la: MISERABILIORES sumus, inquit, omnibus hominibus.
units.tr: We are more miserable, he says, than all other men.

units.la: Quare? An ob id quod præsentis tantum uitæ bona acciperemus, si nō esset alia uita post hāc præsentem futura? At hac ratione nō essemus reliquis hominibus miserabiliores. Nam & illorum eadem est conditio. Qui extra Christum sunt, accipiunt bona temporaria in uita sua, secundum exemplū diuitis epulonis. Si Christianus quoq; propter Christum, uel per Christū nō nisi huius uitæ bonis fruitur, non uideo quare ob id cæteris sit infelicior. Inspice totum illum ordinē ecclesiasticū pontifices, Carnales, episcopos, prælatos, abbates, canonicos, sacerdotes, monachos & monachas, quorum pars maxima temporaria tātum in Christo bona, dominia, dignitates, præbendas, beneficia, &c. sectatur, atq; ita temporariū tātū Christū amplectitur, an illos cæteris mortalibus omnib. miserabiliores esse cēsebimus? Visq; adeo felices sunt, ut fortunas suas ne cum regum quidem felicitate commutet. Quid est igitur, quod Apostolus hic dicit: Si in hac tātū uita speramus in Christum, omniū sumus hominū miserrimi? Quomodo & in quibus hoc Christianis uerū esset, si nulla nobis in Christo spes esset, nisi præsentis huius uitæ? In carnalibus sanè ac falsis nihil haberet loci: sicuti patet in illis quorū memini, qui se norūt accommodare seculo, & quibus nulla prorsus est de futura uita cogitatio. Relinquitur ergo cōcernere hoc ueros Christianos, q quoniā pie uolūt uiuere in Christo Iesu: seipsi abnegāt, crucé suam tollūt, & Christum crucifixū sequētes à mūdo, cui sunt crucifixi, innumeris modis exagitantur, suntq; uelut oues occisionis, quos hāc ob causam sapientes huius mūdi pro insanis habēt ac deploratis. Tolle istis futurae uitae spē: & uide, an nō oim sint censendi miserrimi, pterea quod ne præsentis quidē uitę cōmodis utūtur cū aliis, sintq; perinde post morte perituri atq; ceteri omnes. Huc accedit, qd in carne sua propter peccati reliquias multis sunt tētationib. obnoxij, & assiduo certamine cōtra Satanam pugnando fatigantur. Præterea magna illis est afflictio spiritus cum propter irremissum desiderium, quo dissolui & cum Christo esse cupicupiunt, tum propter perditionem mortaliū, quos Satan cæcitate mentis percussos captiuos habet, & in barathrum perditionis præcipitat. Hoc genus hominū, si nulla sit expectanda futuræ uitæ felicitas, quis non duxerit omnium esse miserrimum?
units.tr: Why? Is it because we would receive only the goods of this present life, if there were no other life to come after this one? But on that reasoning we would not be more miserable than other men, for their condition is the same. Those who are outside Christ receive temporal goods in their lives, as in the example of the rich glutton. If a Christian too, on account of Christ or through Christ, enjoys only the goods of this life, I do not see why he should on that account be more unhappy than others. Look through that whole ecclesiastical order: popes, cardinals, bishops, prelates, abbots, canons, priests, monks and nuns. The greater part of them seek after temporal goods in Christ only: lordships, dignities, prebends, benefices and so on, and so they embrace a Christ who is only temporal. Shall we judge them more miserable than all other mortals? Indeed they are so happy that they would not exchange their fortunes even for the happiness of kings. What then does the Apostle mean when he says: If in this life only we hope in Christ, we are the most miserable of all men? How and in what sense would this be true of Christians, if we had no hope in Christ except for this present life? In carnal and false people it would have no place, as is evident in those I have mentioned, who know how to accommodate themselves to the age and have no thought at all of the future life. It remains, then, to apply this to true Christians. Since they wish to live piously in Christ Jesus, they deny themselves, take up their cross, and, following Christ crucified, they are harassed in countless ways by the world, to which they have been crucified. They are like sheep for the slaughter, and for this reason the wise of this world regard them as mad and desperate. Take away from them the hope of future life, and see whether they are not to be judged the most miserable of all, because they do not even enjoy the comforts of the present life along with others, and will perish after death just as all the rest do. Add to this that in their flesh, on account of the remnants of sin, they are exposed to many temptations and are worn down by constant struggle against Satan. Moreover, they suffer great distress of spirit: partly because of their unabated desire to be dissolved and be with Christ, and partly because of the perdition of mortals whom Satan holds captive, struck with blindness of mind, and hurls into the pit of destruction. If no happiness of future life were to be expected, who would not judge this kind of people the most miserable of all?

units.la: Tam igitur Christianismi gloria & felicitas non sunt præsentis huius uitæ, ut si futuræ uitæ spes tollatur, nihil sit homine Christiano in mundo magis inglorium & infelicius. Hic enim palæstra tantum est, frequens pugna, irre missus labor, indefinens tentatio, passio & afflictio spiritus, odium Vatinianum à Satana & mundo sustinendum, auiditas desiderij, fidei ac spei exercitium, probatio per patientiam & quæ alia sunt huiusmodi, in quibus est gloria nulla, miseriarum & ærumnarum multum. In futura uero uita horum omnium finis erit cū gloria & felicitate non modò magna, sed & prorsus infinita. Hic cum innumeris molestijs peregrinamur à Domino, absentes è facie gloriæ eius: illic cum gaudio exultabimus ac refocillabimur in patria. Sic diuisus est Christianismus in præsentem hanc & futuram uitā, ut præsenti deputatum sit exercitium probationis per omnis generis tentationes ac passiones: futuræ uero corona uictoriæ, cum gloria & felicitate sempiterna. Quare si quis ordine hunc peruerterit, quærens in prima Christianismi parte, quod expectandum demum est in altera, omni suo conatu frustrabitur. Sūt enim priores passiones posteriores gloriæ. Rursus si qui primæ se parti accommodant, spe alterius frustrentur, omnium necesse est sint mortaliū miserrimi: felicissimi uero, si illius fuerint facti compotes.
units.tr: So the glory and happiness of Christianity do not belong to this present life. If the hope of future life were taken away, nothing in the world would be more inglorious and unhappy for a Christian. Here there is only a wrestling-ground, frequent battle, unremitting toil, unceasing temptation, suffering and distress of spirit, the Vatinian hatred endured from Satan and the world, longing of desire, the exercise of faith and hope, proof through patience, and other things of this sort, in which there is no glory but much misery and hardship. In the future life, however, all these will end in glory and happiness not only great but utterly infinite. Here we wander as pilgrims from the Lord with countless troubles, absent from the face of his glory; there we shall exult with joy and be refreshed in our homeland. Thus Christianity is divided between this present life and the future: the exercise of testing through every kind of temptation and suffering is assigned to the present, but the crown of victory, with glory and eternal happiness, to the future. Therefore, if anyone reverses this order, seeking in the first part of Christianity what is to be expected at last in the second, he will be frustrated in all his effort, for the earlier sufferings come before the later glory. Again, if those who devote themselves to the first part are cheated of hope in the other, they must be the most miserable of all mortals; they would be the most happy only if they had become partakers of that other.

units.la: NVNC autē Christus surrexit ex mortuis, inquit.] Hactenus ex falsa propositione eorum, qui resurrectionem mortuorum inter Corinthios negabant, falsa, absurda & incommoda collegit: quæ errorem illorum consequuntur, ut de his erubescentes errorem relinquerent: uel si nollent, etiam consequentia absurda tenere, atq; ita totum Christianismum subuertere cogerentur.
units.tr: "But now Christ has risen from the dead," he says. Up to this point, from the false premise of those among the Corinthians who denied the resurrection of the dead, he has drawn false, absurd and inconvenient conclusions, which follow from their error. The aim is that, ashamed of these, they might abandon the error; or, if they were unwilling, they would be forced to hold absurd consequences and so overturn the whole of Christianity.

units.la: Nō sunt enim uera absurda, sed falsa, quę ex falsa quidem sententia, uera tamen cōnexione & argumentatione colligit dicens: Si resurrectio mortuorum non est, neq; Christus resurrexit. Si Christus non resurrexit, inanis est prædicatio nostra, inanis est fides uestra, &c. quorum nihil est uerum. Surrexit enim Christus, & neque prædicatio apostolorum, neque fides Christianorum inanis est: neque sunt apostoli falsi, sed ueracissimi testes Dei. Nam filium suum Deus uerè excitauit, neque sunt in Christum credentes adhuc in peccatis: neq; pereūt qui in illo obdormiunt, sed omnino seruantur: & Christianorum spes non præsentis tantum, sed futuræ potius est uitæ: suntque ideo omnium mortalium non miserrimi, sed felicissimi.
units.tr: For these absurdities are not true but false. He draws them from the false opinion, yet by a true connection and argument, saying: If there is no resurrection of the dead, neither has Christ risen. If Christ has not risen, our preaching is vain, your faith is vain, and so on. None of these is true. For Christ has risen, and neither the preaching of the apostles nor the faith of Christians is vain. Nor are the apostles false, but the most truthful witnesses of God. For God truly raised up his Son, nor are those who believe in Christ still in their sins; nor do those who have fallen asleep in him perish, but they are altogether preserved. The hope of Christians is not of the present life only, but rather of the future; and therefore they are not the most miserable of all mortals, but the most happy.

units.la: Et tamen absurda hæc quæ obiecit Apostolus, præcedentem propositionem, qua resurrectionem mortuorum non esse dicebat, necessario sequuntur. Itaque cum illa fuit falsa, consequitur & propositionem illam, quam ea uer aci argumentatione sequuntur, necessario esse falsam.
units.tr: And yet these absurdities, which the Apostle has set out, necessarily follow from the preceding proposition, by which he said that there is no resurrection of the dead. Therefore, since that proposition was false, it follows that the proposition from which these consequences follow by a true argument is necessarily false.

units.la: Etenim ubi consequentia falsa sunt & absurda, quo magis firmiore ratiocinatione consequuntur, hoc magis præcedentem propositionem, unde colliguntur falsam esse conuincunt: quare relinquitur falsum esse, quod resurrectionem mortuorum nō esse dicebat, ideoq; omnino futurum, ut mortui resurgant. Cum igitur Apostolus euidentissima id ratiocinatione collegisset, mox subiungit, dicens: Nunc autem Christus surrexit à mortuis. Vbi uocula, nunc non temporis habet connotationem, sed præmissæ argumentationis conclusionē. Neque enim Christum tum resurrexisse dicit, sed sic ex præmissa argumentatione concludit. Quasi dicat: Iam uero nihil ueri habent hæc omnia. Surrexit enim Christus ex mortuis: quare sequitur, mortuorum esse resurrectionem.
units.tr: For where consequences are false and absurd, the more firmly they follow from a premise, the more they prove that premise, from which they are drawn, to be false. Hence it follows that what he said, that there is no resurrection of the dead, is false, and so it must be that the dead altogether rise. When the Apostle had drawn this by the clearest reasoning, he immediately adds: But now Christ has risen from the dead. Here the little word "now" (nunc) carries not a temporal sense but the force of the conclusion of the preceding argument. For he does not say that Christ then rose; he concludes thus from the preceding argument, as if to say: Now indeed none of these things holds true. For Christ has risen from the dead; therefore it follows that there is a resurrection of the dead.

units.la: Non dicit: Nunc autem mortui resurgunt: sed, Nūc autem Christus surrexit ex mortuis, quia in quæstione erat, an mortui resurgerent: de eo uero, quod Christus ex mortuis resurrexisse prædicatur, nulla erat in ecclesia controuersia. Id ergo conclusionis uice ponit: unde quod illi negabant, uerum & præmissa absurda falsa esse comprobantur.
units.tr: He does not say: "Now the dead rise," but "Now Christ has risen from the dead," because the question was whether the dead rise. Concerning the claim that Christ rose from the dead, however, there was no controversy in the Church. He therefore puts this in place of a conclusion, by which what they denied is proved true and the absurd premises are shown to be false.

units.la: Primitiæ eorum qui dormierāt, fuit. Postquā enim per hominem mors, etiā per hominem resurrectio mortuorum. Quēadmodū enim in Adam oēs moriuntur, ita & in Christo omnes uiuificabuntur: unusquisq; autē in proprio ordine, primitiæ Christus, deinde ij qui sunt Christi, in aduentu ipsius.
units.tr: He was the firstfruits of those who had fallen asleep. For since death came through a man, the resurrection of the dead also comes through a man.
