That lying spirit was an angel who was sent to entice the impious king Ahab, so that he would be a lying spirit in the mouths of all the prophets he had. This mission made him an angel, but not an angel of light; he was an angel of darkness and error. An angel of light is a minister of truth and a messenger of the grace of God. Such was Gabriel, sent to the blessed Virgin; such were the angels whom we read announced good news to the shepherds; such were those who announced the resurrection of Christ to the women; and there were no others who appeared to the patriarchs, prophets, Christ, and the apostles. Satan cannot be changed into an angel of that kind, but he can be transfigured. Thus that spirit of seduction, in order to deceive Ahab, whom God wished to punish, transfigured himself into an angel of light, as if he were the spirit of truth. This transfiguration of Satan brought into the churches every kind of error, impiety, superstition, false worship, and idolatry, because the bishops, having neglected the holy Scriptures, were unwilling to recognise Satan except as black and plainly visible, and embraced him, transfigured and whitewashed in appearance, as an angel of light.

units.la: NON magnum est igitur, si & ministri illius inquit, tranfigurentur, quasi sint ministri iusticię.) Chrys. particulā hāc aliter legit. In priore fiquidē ad Cor. cap. 6. homil. 16. super illud: An nescitis quod angelos iudicabimus? sic dicit: Dicūt nonulli significari hoc loco sacerdotes. Sed absit. Nā de dęmonibus loquitur. Etenim si de corruptis sacerdotib. dixisset, significasset eos supra, dicēs, nā in uobis iudicatur mūdus. Solet enim scriptura malos homines uocare mundū. Neq; secūdò idē dixisset, nec si maius aliquid dixisset, postremo illud loco posuisset. Verū de angelis illis loquitur, de quibus dicit
units.tr: "It is therefore no great thing if his ministers also," he says, "are transfigured as if they were ministers of righteousness." Chrysostom reads this part differently. In his first homily on 1 Corinthians, chapter 6, homily 16, on the words "Do you not know that we shall judge angels?", he says: "Some say that priests are meant here. But far be it. For he speaks of demons. For if he had spoken of corrupt priests, he would have signified them above, saying, 'for the world is judged by you.' For Scripture is accustomed to call wicked men the world. Nor would he have said the same thing a second time, nor, if he had meant something greater, would he have put it last. Rather, he speaks of those angels of whom he says"

units.la: Christus: Ite in ignem æternū, qui paratus est diabolo & angelis eius. Et Paulus: Quoniā angeli eius, inquit, transfigurantur uelut ministri iusticiæ. Hæc ille. Manifestum est, nō esse antiquariorū negligētiam, ὅτι ἄγγελοι αὐτῆς. i. qđ angeli eius, scriptum pro eo quod est εἰ ἡ διάκονοι αὐτῆς. i. si & ministri eius, sed ab ipso sic Chrys. tanquam ab Apostolo scriptū, ad hoc citatum, ut coprobaret & Satanam habere angelos. Et tamen in hoc ipso loco reperitur idē Chrysost. legere non ὅτι ἄγγελοι, sed, εἰ ἡ διάκονοι αὐτῆς, ut appareat sciolum quendam lectionem illius mutasse, ne à recepta discreparet.
units.tr: Christ says: "Depart into everlasting fire, prepared for the devil and his angels." And Paul: "For his angels," he says, "are transfigured as ministers of righteousness." So far Chrysostom. It is clear that this is not an oversight of the ancient copyists, ὅτι ἄγγελοι αὐτῆς [hoti angeloi autēs], "that his angels," written in place of εἰ ἡ διάκονοι αὐτῆς [ei kai hai diakonoi autēs], "if also his ministers." Rather, Chrysostom himself wrote it thus, as if it were written by the Apostle, and cited it to prove that Satan also has angels. Yet in this very passage the same Chrysostom is found reading not "that his angels" but "if also his ministers," so it appears that some half-learned person changed his reading so that it would not differ from the received text.

units.la: NON est magnum igitur, inquit.) In se quidem satis magnū est, si ministri Satanæ in ministros iusticiæ transfiguretur, nec magnū modo, sed & admodū noxiū, uerū respectu maioris nequitiæ, qua Satā ipse in angelū lucis transformatur, magnū esse negat, id qđ ob id facit ut cautiores reddat Corinthios. Etenim quo facilior est ista transfiguratio, hoc maiore attentione ac uigilantia obseruanda uenit, quo uitetur. Magnum enim nō esse, pro, mirum nō esse dixit. Sunt autem factu difficilia quæ mira, rursus faciliora, quæ mira non sunt, & mala quæ facile conflantur, quo expeditiora sunt ad nocendum, hoc sunt diligentius cauenda. Cum itaq; dicit, Nō magnū est, nō extenuat periculū, quod est à transfiguratis ministris Satanæ, sed magis monet diligentius esse uitandum.
units.tr: "It is therefore no great thing," he says. In itself it is indeed a great thing if the ministers of Satan are transfigured into ministers of righteousness, and not only great but very harmful. Yet with respect to the greater wickedness by which Satan himself is transformed into an angel of light, he denies that it is great, and he does this so as to make the Corinthians more cautious. For the easier such a transfiguration is, the more attention and vigilance must be used to avoid it. For he said "it is no great thing" in place of "it is no wonder." Things that are marvellous are difficult to do, and things that are not marvellous are easier; and evils that are easily brought about, the more readily they can do harm, the more carefully they must be guarded against. Therefore, when he says "it is no great thing," he does not diminish the danger that comes from the transfigured ministers of Satan, but rather warns that they must be avoided with greater care.

units.la: SI & ministri illius, inquit.) Vide quomodo pseudapostolos magis ac magis detestabiles reddat. Primò: Nam si is, inquit, qui uenit aliū Iesum prædicat. Deinde, ut āmputē occasione, inquit, ijs qui cupiūt occasione. Tertiò, Siquidē istiusmodi pseudapostoli, inqt. Quartò, quo eos prorsus auersandos esse moneat, pro eo quod dicēdū uidebatur: nō est magnū si & pseudapostoli, non est magnū, inquit, si & ministri illius, Satanæ uidelicet, transfigurarentur, quasi sint ministri iusticiæ. Nos admonemur quo loco habēdi sint pseudapostoli in apostolos Christi transfigurati. Pro ipsissimis scilicet Satanæ ministris & apostolis. Quemadmodum enim Christus totus est in saluādo, ita Satan ecōtra totus est in perdendo genere humano. Et ut Christus apostolos habet salutis huius ministros, ita Satan quoq; apostolos habet, quorum ministerio ad seducendum ac perdendum mortales utitur.
units.tr: "If also his ministers," he says. See how he makes the false apostles more and more detestable. First: "For if he who comes preaches another Jesus," he says. Second: "that I may cut off the occasion from those who desire an occasion." Third: "For such false apostles," he says. Fourth, he warns that they must be utterly shunned, instead of what might seem to be the expected statement. He does not say, "It is no great thing if false apostles are also transformed," but "it is no great thing if also his ministers, namely Satan's, are transformed as if they were ministers of righteousness." We are warned in what light the false apostles should be regarded, since they have been transformed into the apostles of Christ, though they are in fact the very ministers and apostles of Satan. For just as Christ is wholly given to saving, so Satan on the contrary is wholly given to destroying mankind. And as Christ has apostles as ministers of this salvation, so Satan too has apostles, whose service he uses to seduce and destroy mortals.

units.la: TRANSFIGVRANTVR, inquit, quasi sint ministri iusticiæ.) Non dicit, ut sint, sed, quasi sint ministri iusticiæ. Ministri iusticiæ aliter atqs aliter dicuntur.
units.tr: "They are transformed," he says, "as if they were ministers of righteousness." He does not say "that they may be," but "as if they were ministers of righteousness." Ministers of righteousness are spoken of in different ways.

units.la: Primò, de illis qui iudiciariæ iusticiæ ad defensionem bonorum & oppressionem malorum quocunque modo ministrant, qui omnes ad ordinem magistratus pertinent.
units.tr: First, of those who serve the righteousness of judgment, in whatever way, for the defence of good people and the oppression of wicked ones; all of these belong to the order of the magistracy.

units.la: Deinde, de apostolis Christi, qui iusticiæ Dei quæ per fidem est in Christum, euangelizando subseruiunt.
units.tr: Second, of the apostles of Christ, who by preaching the gospel serve the righteousness of God which is through faith in Christ.

units.la: Tertiò, de omnis gēris doctorib. qui docen do, hortādo, & corripiēdo quosuis ad iusticiā
units.tr: Third, of teachers of every kind, who by teaching, exhorting and rebuking instruct any people to righteousness

units.la: & innocentiam uitæ instituunt. Quarto, per Ebraismum, in genere de ministris, iuste ac recte ministrantibus, ut sicut operarij iniqui, operarij iniquitatis, ita ministri iusti, ministri iustitiæ uocentur.
units.tr: and innocence of life. Fourth, by a Hebraism, in general of ministers who serve justly and rightly, so that, just as unjust workers are called workers of iniquity, so righteous ministers are called ministers of righteousness.

units.la: Præsenti uero loco Chrysostomus exponit ad hunc modum: Quid autem est ministerium iusticiæ? Id scilicet quod nos sumus, euangelion prædicates uobis, quod iusticiam habet. Nam uel hoc dicit, uel quod iustorum uirorum sibi opinionem assumunt. Existimo conuenire ut intelligamus de iustitia, quâ pseudapostoli Iudaico more magis quàm Christiano prædicabant: non quod iusticiam amaret, aut ueraciter prædicarent, sed quod illam contra doctrinam gratiæ prætexerent, quam Paulus ubiq; prædicabat. Paulus absq; ulla dissimulatione ministerium gratiæ Christi obibat: illi uero doctrinam iustitiæ, qua iusti redderentur homines, iactabant, quo sibijpsis quoq; opinionem iustitiæ conciliarét, & cunctis sese approbarent. Nam id genus doctrinæ plausibilior est Iudæis & Gentibus, quàm sit doctrina gratiæ, ac fidei iustificantis.
units.tr: In this passage, Chrysostom explains it in this way: "What, then, is the ministry of righteousness? It is that which we are, preaching the gospel to you, which has righteousness. For he says either this, or that they assume for themselves the reputation of righteous men." I think we should understand it of the righteousness with which the false apostles, in the Jewish manner rather than the Christian, were preaching: not that they loved righteousness, or preached it truthfully, but that they put it forward against the doctrine of grace, which Paul preached everywhere. Paul carried out the ministry of the grace of Christ without any pretence; but they boasted of a doctrine of righteousness, by which men are made righteous, so that they might win for themselves too a reputation for righteousness and commend themselves to everyone. For this kind of doctrine is more pleasing to Jews and Gentiles than the doctrine of grace and of justifying faith.

units.la: QVORVM finis erit iuxta opera eorum, inquit.) Habet hæc particula comminationem meriti interitus. Interitum significat perfine. Neq; enim simpliciter utitur hac uoce de morte corporea, qua uerorum quoq; apostolorum cursus finitus est, sed de interitu, quo pereunt pseudapostoli, qui quasi fructus est operum malorum. Sic Rom.6. eorum finem qui peccato serviunt morte, aliorum uero qui Deo obediût, uitam æterna esse dicit. Sic geminus est mortalium finis, bonorum alius, alius malorum. Bonorum uita æterna, malorum interitus sempiternus, de quo & Phil.3. sic dicit: Nam complures ambulant, de quibus sepe dixi uobis, nunc autem & flens dico, inimici crucis Christi, quorum finis perditio est. Consolationis quidem materiam habet, quod finis paratus est omnib. ministris Satanæ, hypocritis ac seductoribus, ut sciam nequitiâ illorum haud duraturâ in sempiternum: uerum iuxta comiseradi ueniût, si qualitatem finis illorum cõsideremus. Erit enim ille non secûdum gratiam, sed secundum iustû Dei iudicium, quod Apostolus innuens, non simpliciter dicit, quorum erit finis, sed addit, iuxta eorum opera. Significat interitum illorum responsurû meritis ipsorum. Etenim quo magis ingeniû Satanæ operibus suis exprimunt, hoc grauius merentur exitium. Sic nos facile diuinare poterimus, quàm sit graue futurû eorum iudiciû & exitiû, qui hodie & ueritate Dei oppugnando, & ouiculas Christi atrocissime mactando, tam Satanæ se, quàm uentris & gloriæ suæ ministros esse declarât. Erit.n.eorû quoq; finis secundû opera ipsorum, nisi in tempore resipiscant, quo per gratiam Christi seruetur.
units.tr: "Their end will be according to their works," he says. This phrase carries a threat of deserved destruction. By "end" he means perdition. For he does not use this word simply of bodily death, by which even the course of the true apostles was ended, but of the ruin by which the false apostles perish, which is, as it were, the fruit of their evil works. So in Rom. 6 he says that the end of those who serve sin is death, but that of others who obey God is eternal life. Thus mortals have a twofold end: one for the good, another for the wicked. The end of the good is eternal life, that of the wicked is everlasting ruin, of which he speaks in Phil. 3 as follows: "For many walk, of whom I have often told you, and now I tell you even weeping, that they are enemies of the cross of Christ, whose end is destruction." There is indeed matter for comfort in the fact that an end is prepared for all the ministers of Satan, hypocrites and seducers, so that we may know that their wickedness will not last for ever; yet they are rightly to be pitied if we consider the nature of their end. For it will be not according to grace but according to the just judgment of God. The Apostle hints at this, and does not simply say "their end will be," but adds "according to their works." He signifies that their ruin will correspond to their deserts. Indeed, the more they express the cunning of Satan in their works, the more gravely they deserve destruction. So we can easily guess how grievous their judgment and destruction will be, who today, by attacking the truth of God and most cruelly slaughtering Christ's little sheep, declare themselves ministers of Satan no less than of their own belly and glory. Their end too will be according to their works, unless in time they repent, by which they are preserved through the grace of Christ.

units.la: Irerû dico, ne quis me putet insipientè esse, alioqui & iam ut insipientè accipite me, ut paululû quiddâ & ego glo-
units.tr: Again I say, lest anyone think me foolish; otherwise, receive me even as foolish, so that I too may boast a little.

units.la: rier. Quod dico, non dico secundû dominum, sed uelut per insipientiâ, in hoc argumento gloriationis. Quandoquidem multi gloriantur secundum carnè, & ego gloriabor. Libenter enim sufferatis insipientes, cum sitis sapientes. Sufertis enim, si quis uos in seruitutè adigit, si quis exedit, si quis accipit, si quis attollit sese, si quis uos in faciem cædit, iuxta contumeliâ loquor, perinde quasi nos infirmi fuerimus.
units.tr: What I say, I do not say according to the Lord, but as it were in folly, in this matter of boasting. Since many boast according to the flesh, I too will boast. For you gladly bear with fools, since you yourselves are wise. For you bear it if anyone brings you into bondage, if anyone devours you, if anyone takes from you, if anyone exalts himself, if anyone strikes you on the face. I speak as to reproach, as though we had been weak.

units.la: ITERVM dico, inquit.) Rediturus ad materiam gloriationis suæ, quam supra ingressus est, ut pseudapostolorum iactatiam retundat, dicit: Iterû dico, quasi dicat, quod supra dixi, dico denuo, uel, qd' dicere cœpi repeto.
units.tr: I say again, he says.) Returning to the subject of his boasting, which he had begun above, in order to check the boasting of the false apostles, he says: "I say again," as if to say, "I repeat what I said above, or I return to what I began to say."

units.la: Quare? Ne quis me putet esse insipiente, quasi obli tus sim eorum, quæ dicere cœpi, ac temerè scribedo, uelut æstu gloriationis inebriatus ferat. Potest & sic exponi. Iterum dico. Quid' Id uidelicet, Ne me quisquam reputet esse insipien tem, propter gloriationes meas, quas sum contra pseudapostolos prolaturus, sed cogitet, quàm graui causa, ut eas proferâ sim adactus.
units.tr: Why? So that no one thinks me a fool, as though I had forgotten what I began to say and, drunk with the heat of boasting, wrote carelessly and rashly. This can also be explained thus: "I say again," that is, that no one should think me foolish because of the boasts I am about to set out against the false apostles, but should consider how serious a cause compelled me to bring them forward.

units.la: ALIOQVI, inquit, & iam ut insipientem accipite me.) Græcè est, εἰ δὲ μήγε καὶ ὡς ἀφρονα δέξασθέ με, id est, Si uero minus, saltè ut insipiente accipite me. Nö loquebatur ex insipientia, sed ex Apostolica prudetia, cura & solicitudine, ideoq; poscit ab illis, ne se insipiente esse putent. Iam addit ex abundâti, dicés, Sed esto, reputetis me insipiente, an non sic quoq; par est, ut me uelut insipiente accipiatis? Sic contendit ab illis quouis modo, ut se accipiant & audiant. Si non ut insipiens loquor, inquit, sed ut sapiés, accipite me tanquâ uera ac necessaria loquente. Si uero iudicatis me desipere, date mihi uel eam tolerantiam, qua insipientes quoq; subinde patienter audiûtur, propterea quod illi quoq; sæpenumero uera loquuntur.
units.tr: "Otherwise," he says, "and now receive me as a fool.") The Greek is: "But if not, at least receive me as a fool" [εἰ δὲ μήγε καὶ ὡς ἀφρονα δέξασθέ με]. He did not speak out of folly, but out of apostolic prudence, care and concern; therefore he asks them not to think him a fool. He then adds, as it were in surplus, saying: "But grant that you think me foolish; would it not still be fitting that you receive me as though I were foolish?" In this way he urges them, in whatever manner, to receive and hear him. "If I do not speak as a fool," he says, "but as a wise man, receive me as one speaking true and necessary things. But if you judge that I am out of my mind, then at least grant me that tolerance by which fools too are from time to time patiently heard, since they too often speak true things."

units.la: VT paululum quiddam, inquit, & ego glorier. Verbo accipiendi, pro uerbo ferendi, ac tolerandi usus est, petens ut se patienter, uel quasi insipiente audiant. Iam ad quid se audire debeant, subiungit, Vt paululum quiddam, & ego glorier, inquit. Non simpliciter, ut glorier, sed, ut & ego glorier. Quasi dicat: Quàdoquidem pseudapostoli inter uos tâtopere gloriantur, & uos illos patienter auditis, cocedite ut & ego glorier: quod in illis toleratis, tolerate & in me, si insipientiam illorum ferre nostis, ferte & meam.
units.tr: "That I may boast a little, I too," he says. He has used the verb "receive" in the sense of "bear" and "tolerate," asking that they hear him patiently, or as though he were a fool. Now he adds what they ought to hear from him: "That I may boast a little, I too," he says. Not simply "that I may boast," but "that I too may boast." As if to say: Since the false apostles boast so much among you, and you listen to them patiently, grant that I too may boast. What you bear in them, bear in me too, if you know how to endure their folly, bear mine as well.

units.la: Significat se non fuisse gloriaturum, nisi ad id per iactantiam pseudapostolorum cogeretur, nec iniquum se petere ab illis, cum id ultro pseudapostolis concedant. Nec otiosum est, quod non simpliciter dicit, ut & ego, sed ut paululum quiddam & ego glorier. Significat haud multa sibi & operosa gloriatione opus ad hoc esse, ut iactantiam pseudapostolorum reijciat, sed satis fore, si uel modicam attingat eorum partem, de quibus ipse uera- citer, si ita res poscerêt, gloriari posset. Et reua ra sic habebat uirtutum ipsius excellentia, ut uel minima illarum portio pluris esset facien- da, quàm omnis pseudapostolorum iactantia. Quare opus illi non erat, ut multum & impen- se gloriaretur, præsertim cum in propatulo ef- set Apostolatus ipsius excellentia & efficacia.
units.tr: He signifies that he would not have boasted unless he were compelled to do so by the boasting of the false apostles, and that it is not unfair for him to ask this of them, since they readily grant it to the false apostles. It is also not idle that he does not simply say "as I too," but "that I too may boast a little." He signifies that no lengthy and laborious boasting is needed for him to repudiate the boasting of the false apostles, but that it will be enough if he touches even a small part of those things in which he could truly boast, if the situation required it. Indeed the excellence of his gifts was so great that even the smallest portion of them was to be valued more highly than all the boasting of the false apostles. So there was no need for him to boast much and at length, especially since the excellence and efficacy of his apostleship was openly evident.

units.la: QVOD dico, inquit, non dico secundū do- minum (uulgata habet secundum Deum) sed uelut per insipientiam, in hoc argumento glo- riationis.) Ne uideatur Apostolicū esse, & ad mādatum à domino acceptū pertinere, si quis de factis suis glorietur, cauet diligēter, dicens: Quę dicturus sum, non sum dicturus secundū dominum, hoc est, tanquam Apostolus domi- ni, secundum illius mandatum, sed perinde ac si sim insipiens, ut desipiam cum magnis illis uestris magistris, in præsenti causa gloriatio- nis. Lyranus exponit hæc uerba cum adiecta conditione ad hunc modum: Si facio hoc sine causa rationabili uel necessaria, sicut faciebát pseudapostoli, non loquor secundum Deum, sed quasi in insipientia. Chrysostomus tamen simpliciter absq; conditione accipit, sic expo- nens: Vides quod gloriatio iam non sit secun- dum dominum. Dicit enim: Quando omnia feceritis, dicite qd' serui inutiles sumus. Hoc genus ergo gloriationis, quo gloriabantur pseudapostoli, & ad quod adigebatur Paulus per improbam illorum iactantiam, non est se- cundum dominum, secūdum quem magis est humilitas, ac modestia inutiles se seruos esse dicentium. Significat uel ex iactantia pseud- apostolorum manifestum esse, quod non sint ueri Christi apostoli, quandoquidem gloria- tio illorum secundū dominum esse nequeat.
units.tr: "What I say," he says, "I do not say according to the Lord" (the Vulgate has "according to God"), "but as in folly, in this matter of boasting.") Lest it seem to be apostolic, and to belong to a command received from the Lord, if anyone boasts of his own deeds, he carefully guards against this, saying: "What I am about to say, I am not going to say according to the Lord," that is, as an apostle of the Lord, according to his command, but just as if I were a fool, so that I may play the fool with your great teachers in the present matter of boasting. Lyra explains these words with an added condition, in this way: "If I do this without a reasonable or necessary cause, as the false apostles did, I do not speak according to God, but as in folly." Chrysostom, however, takes it simply, without condition, explaining thus: "You see that the boasting is no longer according to the Lord. For he says: When you have done all things, say that we are unprofitable servants." Therefore this kind of boasting, by which the false apostles boasted and to which Paul was driven by their shameless boasting, is not according to the Lord, according to whom humility and modesty are rather found in those who say that they are unprofitable servants. He signifies that from the boasting of the false apostles it is clear that they are not true apostles of Christ, since their boasting cannot be according to the Lord.

units.la: Rursus autem non simpliciter dicit, sed per insipientiam, uerum, sed uelut per insipientiā, ne sibijpse insipientiæ notam inurat. Deinde addit, in hoc argumento gloriationis, quibus uerbis per limitationem cauet, ne quod dicit de tota sua doctrina intelligatur. Ideo restrin- git illud ad præsentem gloriationis causam. Sic & supra cap. 9. eadem est limitatione, ijs- demq; uerbis usus.
units.tr: Again, he does not say simply, but "as in folly," "but as it were in folly," so that he does not brand himself with the mark of folly. Then he adds, "in this matter of boasting," by which words he guards, through a limitation, against his statement being understood of his whole teaching. Therefore he restricts it to the present cause of boasting. So also above, in chapter 9, he used the same limitation and the same words.

units.la: QVANDOQVIDEM multi gloriantur se- cundum carnem, inquit, gloriabor & ego.) Quod supra dixit, ut paululū quiddam & ego glorier. Quasi dicat: Quemadmodum pseud- apostoli, id iam magis exprimit, dicens: Quan doquidem multi gloriantur secundū carnem, gloriabor & ego. Quasi dicat: Nisi secundū car nem gloriarētur tam multi, nollem ego gloria ri: uerum quoniam tam multi sunt qui hoc fa- ciant, cogor & ego gloriari parumper secun- dum carnem. Notanter dicit: secundum car- nem, ut intelligas illud: Quod dico, non dico secundū dominū, dictum esse de gloriatione secundum carnem. Quid autem sit gloriari se- cundum carnem, dictum est alibi. Chrysosto- mus dicit esse gloriari: [illegible, ~12 letters]
units.tr: "Since many boast according to the flesh," he says, "I too will boast.") He had said above, "that I may boast a little, I too." As if to say: Just as the false apostles do. He expresses this more clearly, saying: "Since many boast according to the flesh, I too will boast." As if to say: If so many did not boast according to the flesh, I would not wish to boast; but since there are so many who do this, I too am compelled to boast for a little while according to the flesh. He says pointedly, "according to the flesh," so that you understand that what he said, "What I say, I do not say according to the Lord," was said about boasting according to the flesh. What it is to boast according to the flesh has been said elsewhere. Chrysostom says that to boast is [illegible, about 12 letters].

units.la: [illegible, ~20 letters] Greek line of the Chrysostom quotation, below the text column.
units.tr: [illegible, about 20 letters] Greek line of the Chrysostom quotation, below the text column.

units.la: A vrs Greek note: [illegible, ~10 letters], ἀπὸ τῆς τ... Mox tamen in fra glorias pseudapostolorum, quibus secun- dum carnem gloriabantur, expressurus est.
units.tr: A verse Greek note: [illegible, about 10 letters], from the ... [ἀπὸ τῆς τ...] Soon, however, he is going to set out, in what follows, the boasts of the false apostles by which they boasted according to the flesh.

units.la: Non dicit autem simpliciter, quandoquidē nonnulli, sed, quandoquidem multi glorian- tur secundū carnē, gloriabor & ego. Admone- mur non esse mox faciedum Apostolo, ac mi- nistro Christi, quod in se non sit decorum, & secundum dominum, si unus & alter ineptiat: sed conniuendum magis, ne præter graues ra- tiones cum insipientibus desipere uideatur, nisi multitudo ineptientium extorqueat, ut faciat quod facturus aliàs non erat.
units.tr: He does not, however, say simply, "since some," but "since many boast according to the flesh, I too will boast." We are reminded that the apostle and minister of Christ should not immediately do what is not becoming in himself, and what is not according to the Lord, if one or two act foolishly; rather he should overlook it, lest he seem, apart from weighty reasons, to play the fool with fools, unless the multitude of those acting foolishly compels him to do what otherwise he would not have been going to do.

units.la: LIBENTER enim suffertis insipientes, in- quit, cum sitis sapientes.) Dixit: Si uero mi- nus, saltem ut insipiente accipite me. Huc ac- commodat quod dicit: Libenter enim suffer- tis insipientes, cum sitis sapietes. Quasi dicat: Quod alias facitis, haud illibenter insipietiam pseudapostolorum sufferentes, facite & mihi. Hęc autē dicęs, notat & carpit in illis per obli- quum, quod tam erant faciles ad ferendum pseudapostolos arroganter sese iactates. Non simpliciter dicit: Suffertis enim, sed, Libenter enim suffertis insipietes, significans eos nimis esse propensos erga pseudapostolos, ac insipi- entia illorum tam non offendi, ut illa delecten tur etiam. Morsum habet & illud, quod dicit, cum sitis sapientes.
units.tr: "For you gladly bear with fools," he says, "since you yourselves are wise.") He had said: "But if not, at least receive me as a fool." To this he applies what he says: "For you gladly bear with fools, since you are wise." As if to say: What you otherwise do, bearing with the folly of the false apostles not unwillingly, do also for me. In saying this, he also notes and censures, indirectly, that they were too ready to tolerate the false apostles who boasted arrogantly. He does not simply say, "For you bear," but "For you gladly bear with fools," signifying that they were too inclined towards the false apostles, and that the folly of these men did not offend them so much that they even took pleasure in it. There is also a sting in what he says, "since you are wise."

units.la: Tales haberi uolebant, non autem erat, nisi secundum sæculum forsan. Id uicij notat di- cens: cum sitis sapientes, subintellige, uestro iudicio. Sanè sapientum est insipientiam pa- tienter ferre stultorum. Illi autem non ferebāt simpliciter, sed ἰδίως, id est, cum delectatione, quod fieri non poterat, nisi insipientia pseud- apostolorum uoluptatem ipsis attulisset, uel singularis cuiusdam sapientiæ loco habita suis- set. Etenim non reputabant eos esse insipien- tes. Alioqui locum in illis non habuissent quæ mox subiicit, dicens:
units.tr: They wished to be regarded as such, but perhaps they were not, except in the sense of worldly wisdom. He notes this fault in saying, "since you are wise," understand: in your own judgment. Certainly it belongs to the wise to bear patiently the folly of fools. But they did not bear it simply, but "in a special way" [ἰδίως], that is, with delight, which could not have happened unless the folly of the false apostles had brought them pleasure, or had been regarded as a kind of singular wisdom. For they did not consider them to be fools. Otherwise what he goes on to add would have had no place among them, saying:

units.la: SVFFERTIS enim si quis uos in seruitu- tem adigit, si quis exedit, si quis accipit, si quis attollit sese, si quis in faciem uos cædit.) Hæc utiq; à pseudapostolis, omnium minimè tulis- sent Corinthij, si cognouissent eos esse insipi- entes. Vide autē quales illi fuerint insipiētes. Tribuit eis dominatum tyrannicum, uoracita- tem, auaritiam, arrogantiam & contumeliam. Hęc exercere nō potuissent in Corinthios, nisi admodum fuissent uersuti ac dolosi, unde eos supra operarios dolosos uocauit. Hoc genus insipiētes nos Germani uocamus <bl>böse Narren.</bl>
units.tr: "For you suffer it if anyone brings you into bondage, if anyone devours you, if anyone takes from you, if anyone exalts himself, if anyone strikes you on the face." These things the Corinthians would least of all have endured from the false apostles, had they recognised them as fools. Consider what sort of fools they were. He attributes to them tyrannical lordship, greed, avarice, arrogance and insolence. They could not have exercised these against the Corinthians unless they had been very crafty and deceitful, which is why he called them deceitful workers above. We Germans call this kind of fool <bl>böse Narren</bl>, that is, wicked fools.

units.la: SVFFERTIS enim,inquit.) Exprobrat il- lis præposteram tolerantiam. Non debebant ferre ne in ueris quidem apostolis, quæ ferē- bant in falsis. Qualis sit, & multis iam sæculis fuerit in ecclesijs pseudepiscoporum toleran- tia, qui nihil tam iniquè præsumere potuerūt, quod nō omnium turpissimè pertulerint ma- iores nostri, & pars maxima hodie quoq; per- ferat, non est ut moneamus, cum omnium sit manifestissimum. Quæ Corinthij pertulerũt à pseudapostolis, A principia quædam fuerunt, quorũ auxefis immensa in Romana sese ecclesia exeruit, & totum Christianum orbem occupare sategit.
units.tr: "For you suffer it," he says. He reproaches them for a perverse tolerance. They ought not to have borne even from the true apostles what they bore from the false ones. What sort of tolerance has existed for many centuries in the churches of the false bishops, who could devise no injustice so iniquitous that our forefathers did not endure it in the most shameful way, and that the greater part of people today still endure, is not something we need to point out, since it is perfectly plain to all. What the Corinthians endured from the false apostles was a kind of beginning, whose immense growth has shown itself in the Roman church and has laboured to occupy the whole Christian world.

units.la: SI quis uos, inquit, in seruitutem adigit.) Adigere in seruitutem, est non simpliciter docere, admonere, corrigere & cosolari, sed more dominorum quiduis imperare, & omnimodam qualis seruorum est, obedientiam exigere. Si illa præstetur, seruitus est, siue sit coacta, siue uoluntaria. Si præstetur Christo domino non coacte, sed sponte, debita obseruatia est, & grata Deo, tamq; non indigna Christianis, ut pro summo sit honore censenda. Et in hanc ducũt nos ueri apostoli. Si uero præstetur hominibus in religione, noxia est, illicita, & dedecorosa Christianis, quibus Apostolus Christi dicit: Empti estis precio magno, nolite fieri serui hominum. Item: State in libertate ad quã uos Christus uocauit. In hac ducunt pseudapostoli, ministri Satanæ. Non debebant illa præstare Corinthij, præstasse uero ex eo patet, quod Apostolus hic illis exprobrat, dicens: Suffertis enim si quis uos in seruitutem adigit. Pótifex Romanus quo seruitutem hanc à toto Christiano orbe extorqueret, finxit se supremum esse in terris Christi uicarium, & hoc titulo inflatus Persica prorsus superbia, pedem suum regibus & principibus osculandum præbet, imo ceruicibus regum imponit.
units.tr: "If anyone brings you into bondage," he says. To bring into bondage is not simply to teach, admonish, correct and comfort, but to command anything at all in the manner of masters and to demand that complete obedience which is the due of slaves. If that obedience is rendered, it is servitude, whether it is extracted by force or given willingly. If it is rendered to Christ the Lord, not under compulsion but freely, it is a proper observance, pleasing to God, and not unworthy of Christians, so that it may be counted the highest honour. It is into this that true apostles lead us. But if it is rendered to men in matters of religion, it is harmful, unlawful and disgraceful to Christians, to whom the apostle of Christ says: "You were bought with a great price; do not become slaves of men." Likewise: "Stand fast in the liberty to which Christ has called you." Into this the false apostles, the ministers of Satan, lead. The Corinthians ought not to have rendered that obedience; that they did render it is clear from what the apostle reproaches them with here, saying: "For you suffer it if anyone brings you into bondage." The Roman Pontiff, in order to wrest this servitude from the whole Christian world, feigned himself to be the supreme vicar of Christ on earth, and, puffed up by this title with truly Persian arrogance, offers his foot to kings and princes to be kissed, or rather places it upon the necks of kings.

units.la: Nosta est historia quæ in chronica Germanorum, lib.18. de Alexandro tertio legitur. Hic Venetijs Imperatori Fridericho, ad ianuá diui Marci imperauit, ut se humi prosterneret, ac veniá clara uoce rogaret. Imperator procidit ad pedes Papæ. Papa Cæsaris collum pede in terram premit, dicens: Scriptum est: Super aspidem & basiliscum ambulabis, & conculcabis leonem & draconem. Respondit Friderichus: Non tibi Alexander, sed beato Petro, cui te discis succedere, pareo. Ad hæc Pontifex ait: Et mihi & Petro. Idem Alexander cum Romę omnem sibi potestate subijcere satageret, cœpit cogitare de abrogandis consulibus, & mox id effecit, ut consules Pontifici iurarent, se sedi Pontificiæ fore fideles, & audietes per omnia, nihilq; contra sententiã Pontificis facturos. In seruitutem subactis Imperatoribus & principibus, consulibusq; Romanis, quæ potuit libertas manere reliquis? Quis non uidet successores pseudapostolorum Romanam ecclesiam occupasse, inq; illa dominatum suum sub nomine Petri confirmasse?
units.tr: There is a well-known story, read in the Chronicle of the Germans, book 18, concerning Alexander III. At Venice he commanded the Emperor Frederick, at the doors of St Mark, to prostrate himself on the ground and ask pardon in a clear voice. The Emperor fell at the Pope's feet. The Pope pressed the Emperor's neck to the ground with his foot, saying: "It is written: You shall walk upon the asp and the basilisk, and you shall trample the lion and the dragon." Frederick replied: "I obey not you, Alexander, but blessed Peter, whose successor you confess yourself to be." To this the Pontiff said: "Both me and Peter." The same Alexander, when he strove to subject all power at Rome to himself, began to plan the abolition of the consuls, and soon accomplished it, so that the consuls swore to the Pontifical see that they would be faithful to it, would obey in all things, and would do nothing against the judgement of the Pontiff. When the emperors, princes and Roman consuls had been brought into servitude, what liberty could remain for the rest? Who does not see that the successors of the false apostles have seized the Roman church and in it confirmed their dominion under the name of Peter?

units.la: SI quis exedit, inquit.) Vbi pseudapostoli Corinthios in seruitutem adegerunt, mox omnibus illorũ & fortunis & honoribus frenum iniecerunt, uorates, rapietes, & per superbiam contumelijs eos afficiētes. Cum ergo dicit: Si quis exedit, notat pseudapostolorũ ingluuiē insatiabilē, qualis & pseudoprophetis, Esa.56. tribuitur, qui canes impudentissimi saturitatē nescientes eo loco uocantur. Rō. Carnaliū gulā totus uix orbis exaturare queat, ut tacea nu-
units.tr: "If anyone devours you," he says. Where the false apostles have brought the Corinthians into servitude, they soon put a bridle on all their fortunes and honours, devouring, plundering, and afflicting them with insults through pride. When he says, "If anyone devours you," he notes the insatiable gluttony of the false apostles, such as is ascribed to the false prophets in Isaiah 56, where they are called shameless dogs that know no satiety. For the belly of carnal men could scarcely be satisfied by the whole world, not to mention

units.la: merosum illū porcorū Epicureorum gregem.
units.tr: that numerous herd of Epicurean swine.

units.la: SI quis accipit, inquit.) Existimo uerbum accipiendi positū hic esse non simpliciter, sed de auiditate accipiendi, qualis esse solet homi num auarorum, ac φιλαργυροι. Talesapostoli omnes eorũ fortunas, quos sibi seruiliter subiectos habent, non minus ad se, quàm ad illos pertinere iudicant: ideoq; impudenter ab illis extorquent quicquid ipsis libuerit, sic tamē ut id fictis uerbis, secundum dictum Petri, negociando faciant. Inspicè ecclesias Papisticas, & monasteria ociosorum aqualiculorum, & unde, an non omnia sacra quęstui sint devota, sic ut nisi detur perpetuo, nihil impetretur.
units.tr: "If anyone takes from you," he says. I think the word "takes" is used here not in a simple sense but of a greedy taking, such as is characteristic of avaricious and [φιλάργυροι] lovers of money men. All such apostles judge the fortunes of those whom they hold in servile subjection to belong no less to themselves than to those people; therefore they shamelessly extort from them whatever pleases them, doing so under feigned words, and by trafficking, according to the saying of Peter. Look at the Papist churches and the monasteries of idle bellies: is not everything sacred devoted to gain, so that unless something is given continually, nothing is obtained?

units.la: SI quis, inquit, attollit se(se.) Dominio coniunctus est fastus. Existiinat se infinitis modis excellere eos, quibus dominantur. Pseudapostoli efferebant se sub nominibus magnorum apostolorum Petri, Iacobi & Ioannis, & inflabatur ex præroga tiua carnis, qd' essent Ebręi, semen Abrahæ, Israelitæ, circumcisi, &c. ita ut omnes fideles & gentibus præ se superbissimė fastidirent. In ecclesijs nostris, quàm elatos fidelium patientia dominos ferat, non modo inflati tituli, sed & pomposa uita mostrat, quam uix sæculi principes adæquât. De Antichristo futurum prædixit Apostolus 2.Thess. 2. ut se extollat supra omne quod dicitur Deus, aut quod colitur, ita ut in templo Dei sedeat ostēdens se quasi sit Deus. 1 Ad hanc superbiam prorsus diabolicam pertinet, qd' se Pontifex Romanus dominū facit cœlestis ac terreni im perij. 22.dist.Can.Omnes. 2 Et quod suam sententiam omnium episcoporum sententijs præponit, uide in glossa dist.4. Can.In istis.
units.tr: "If anyone," he says, "exalts himself." Arrogance is joined with domination. A man thinks he surpasses in countless ways those over whom he rules. The false apostles lifted themselves up under the names of the great apostles Peter, James and John, and they were puffed up by the prerogative of the flesh, because they were Hebrews, the seed of Abraham, Israelites, circumcised, and so on, so that they scorned all the faithful and the Gentiles with the utmost arrogance. In our churches, the patience of the faithful bears how proudly lords exalt themselves, as not only their inflated titles but also their pompous way of life show, which scarcely the princes of the world can equal. The apostle foretold in 2 Thessalonians 2 that Antichrist would exalt himself above everything that is called God or that is worshipped, so that he sits in the temple of God, showing himself as if he were God. To this utterly diabolical pride belongs the fact that the Roman Pontiff makes himself lord of the heavenly and earthly empire (22 dist., canon "Omnes"). And that he places his own opinion before the opinions of all bishops, see the gloss on dist. 4, canon "In istis."

units.la: 3 Quodq; à nemine se iudicare debere cōtendit, etiamsi innumerá ahimarum millia secum trahat in gehennam, dist.40.Si Papa. 4 Et quod sibi soli omnē potestatis plenitudinem uindicat; 2.quæst.6. Can. Qui se scit. 5 Item quod sit lex animata in terris. Sexti, de officio delegati. Can. Ab arbitris, glos.in uerbo, Iuris. 6 Et quod solus queat absque concilio deponere Imperatorem, & omnes subditos liberare ab illius fide, gloss.in Ca. Ad apostolicæ. De sent.& re iudicata, in titulo. 7 Quodq; ius habeat condēdi leges, ipse uero nullus sit subiectus. 25.quæst.1. Can. Ideo. 8 Et Nicolaus Papa, dist.96. Can. Satis euidenter, ad asserendum pontificium fastigium citat Constantinum Imperatorem, qui Pontificem Romanum Deum appellarit. Hæc & multa consimilia alia satis opinor monstrant, quoufq; pseud. apostolorum superbia in ecclesia Romana ascenderit.
units.tr: (3) And that he contends he ought to be judged by no one, even if he drags innumerable thousands of souls with him into hell (dist. 40, "Si Papa"). (4) And that he claims for himself alone the fullness of all power (2 q. 6, canon "Qui se scit"). (5) Likewise that he is a living law on earth (Sext, On delegated office, canon "Ab arbitris," gloss on the word "Iuris"). (6) And that he alone can depose the Emperor without a council, and free all subjects from their allegiance to him (gloss on the canon "Ad apostolicae," On sentence and res judicata, in the title). (7) And that he has the right to make laws, while he himself is subject to none (25 q. 1, canon "Ideo"). (8) And Pope Nicholas, in dist. 96, canon "Satis evidenter," to assert the pontifical eminence, cites the Emperor Constantine, who called the Roman Pontiff God. These and many similar things, I think, sufficiently show how far the pride of the false apostles has risen in the Roman church.

units.la: SI quis uos in faciem cędit, inquit.) In faciē cædere est præsentem pudore suffundere. Non loquitur de uerberibus manuum colaphis, uel alapis. Sed de contumeliosæ uerbere linguæ, quod perinde est, ac si colaphum, uel alapam incutias, unde & nos Germani ubi pudore suffundimur, dicimus: mir wuas als hette er mir eins ins angsicht geben.
units.tr: "If anyone strikes you on the face," he says. To strike on the face is to suffuse someone with shame in their presence. He is not speaking of blows with the hands, such as cuffs or slaps, but of the striking of the tongue with insult, which is just the same as if you were to inflict a cuff or a slap; hence we Germans also say, when we are put to shame: mir wuas als hette er mir eins ins angsicht geben, that is, "it was as if he had given me a slap in the face."

units.la: Illud: iuxta contumeliam, uel, iuxta ignominiam loquor, alij referunt ad praecedente particulam, alij ad sequentem. Si referas ad praecedentem expositio illius erit, ac legendum, de ignominia, uel de contumelia loquor, qua uidelicet, uos afficiunt, dum uos in facie uocant עָרְלִים כלבים גוים & טמאים, id est, gentes, canes, incircuncisos, & immundos. Quid sancti patres Romae uocet nos Germanos abunde notum est. Si referas ad sequentem, sensus erit. Loquor ista ad exprimendam ignominiam, qua nos afficiunt, dum nos plane hac in parte infirmos fuisse monstrant, propterea quod nec in seruitutem uos adegimus, nec exedimus, nec accepimus, nec elati inter uos, sed humiles fuimus, nec in faciem uos cecidimus. Siue ad praecedentem, siue ad sequentem particulam referas, nihil est incommodi.
units.tr: The phrase "according to the insult" (or "I speak according to the reproach") some refer to the preceding particle, others to the following one. If you refer it to the preceding one, its explanation will be this, and it should be read: "I speak of the reproach or insult by which they assail you, when they call you in the face [עֲרֵלִים, כְּלָבִים, גּוֹיִם, וּטְמֵאִים], that is, uncircumcised, dogs, Gentiles and unclean." How the holy fathers at Rome call us Germans is abundantly well known. If you refer it to the following one, the sense will be: I say these things to express the reproach by which they assail us, when they show that we were plainly weak in this respect, because we neither brought you into servitude, nor devoured you, nor took from you, nor exalted ourselves among you, but were humble, nor struck you on the face. Whether you refer it to the preceding or the following particle, there is no difficulty.

units.la: Illud, perinde quasi nos infirmi fuerimus, in Graeco est, ὡς ὅτι ἠμεῖς ἠσθενήσαμεν, i. qd nos infirmi fuimus. ὡς ὅτι, nanq; idem est quod ὅτι simpliciter. Reddi ergo potest, propterea qd nos infirmi fuimus. Et hoc sensu connectendum est, cum praecedenti particula, ad hunc modum. Dico ista ad ignominiam nostri, propterea quod nos magnis illis dominis uestris comparati admodum fuimus inter uos infirmi.
units.tr: That "as if we had been weak" stands in the Greek as ὡς ὅτι ἠμεῖς ἠσθενήσαμεν [as that we were weak], that is, "that we were weak." ὡς ὅτι is simply the same as ὅτι alone. It can therefore be rendered "because we were weak." It must be read in this sense together with the preceding clause, like this: I say these things to shame you, because in comparison with those great lords of yours we were very weak among you.

units.la: Obserua uero, quod haec incommoda non exprobrat pseudapostolis, qui intulerunt, sed Corinthijs, quod illa sint passi, aperitque illorum oculos, ut uideant quantum sit discrimi-nis inter Apostolatum suum, quantumuis in speciem infirmum & humilem, & sublimium B illorum dominorum factum & dominatum, quamq; sint ipsi dementes, qui tam superbos, rapaces, uoraces, ac contumeliosos dominos ferre malint, quam amare eum, qui ad hoc se humiliarit inter ipsos, ut ipsi exaltarentur, seruire ipsis, quam imperare, dare quam accipere, cohonestare ipsos, quam ignominia affice re maluerit. Verum nos admonemur, quid competat illis, qui humilem Christi ministrum fastidiunt. Seruitus uidelicet, qua subsint magnis dominis, illorumq; sint fastui, uoracitati, rapacitati, & contumeliosae libidini expositi. Digni nanque sunt, ut Saulem tyrannum ferant, qui Samuelem prophetam contemnunt ac reijciunt, digni sunt inquam, ut pseudapostolorum iugo subdantur, qui uerum Christi ministrum humilitatis gratia respuunt.
units.tr: Notice, however, that he does not reproach the false apostles, who brought these hardships upon them, but the Corinthians, for suffering them. He opens their eyes so that they may see how great the difference is between his apostleship, however weak and lowly it appears, and the rule and domination of those lofty lords. He also shows how foolish they are, for they would rather bear such proud, grasping, greedy and insulting lords than love the one who humbled himself among them so that they might be exalted: who chose to serve them rather than rule over them, to give rather than receive, to honour them rather than to shame them. Yet we are reminded what befits those who despise the humble minister of Christ. Namely, servitude under great lords, exposed to their pride, greed, rapacity and insolent lust. For they deserve to bear a tyrant like Saul, who despise and reject the prophet Samuel. They deserve, I say, to be placed under the yoke of false apostles, who for the sake of humility refuse the true minister of Christ.

units.la: Seruiant Satanae, qui nolunt seruire Christo: uorentur à ministris Satanae, qui ministro Christi modico pascere grauantur, spolientur à magistris errorum, qui ueritatis ministros egere sinunt: mancipia sint superborum, qui humilitatem ministrorum Christi fastidiunt: cedantur in faciem omnis generis contumelijs audiantque bestiae, bardi, laici, &c. qui cohonestari à fidelibus ministris, inque precio haberi nolunt.
units.tr: Let them serve Satan, who are unwilling to serve Christ. Let them be devoured by the ministers of Satan, who grudge feeding on the modest minister of Christ. Let them be stripped by the masters of error, who allow the ministers of truth to starve. Let them be the slaves of the proud, who scorn the humility of Christ's ministers. Let them be struck in the face with every kind of insult, and let them be called beasts, boors, laymen, and so on, who refuse to be honoured by faithful ministers and to be valued by them.

units.la: Imo, in quocunq; audet aliquis per insipientiam loquor, audeo & ego. Hebrei
units.tr: Indeed, in whatever respect anyone dares to speak foolishly, I dare too. Are they Hebrews?

units.la: sunt? sum & ego. Israelitae sunt? sum & ego. Semen Abrahae sunt? sum & ego, ministri Christi sunt? desipiens loquor, excellentius sum ego, in laboribus copiosius, in uerberibus supra modum, in carceribus abundantius, in mortibus frequenter. A Iudaeis quinquies quadraginta plagas una minus accepi. Ter uirgis caesus fui, semel fui lapidatus, ter naufragium feci, noctem ac diem in profundo egi, in itinerib. saepe, in periculis fluminum, periculis latronum, periculis ex genere, periculis ex gentibus, periculis in ciuitate, periculis in deserto, periculis in mari, periculis inter falsos fratres, in labore & molestia, in uigiliis saepe, in fame & siti, in ieiunijs saepe, in frigore & nuditate, praeterea quae extrinsecus accidunt, incumbens mihi quotidiana cura omnium ecclesiarum. Quis infirmatur, & ego non infirmor? Quis offenditur & ego non uror? Si gloriari oporteat, dehis quae infirmitatis meae sunt gloriabor.
units.tr: I am too. Are they Israelites? I am too. Are they the seed of Abraham? I am too. Are they ministers of Christ? I speak as one beside himself: I am more so. I have laboured more abundantly, been beaten beyond measure, imprisoned more often, and faced death frequently. Five times I received from the Jews forty lashes less one. Three times I was beaten with rods, once I was stoned, three times I suffered shipwreck, and I spent a night and a day in the deep. I have often been on journeys, in perils of rivers, perils of robbers, perils from my own people, perils from the Gentiles, perils in the city, perils in the wilderness, perils at sea, perils among false brothers; in toil and hardship, often in watchings, in hunger and thirst, often in fastings, in cold and nakedness. Besides those things which come from outside, there is the daily pressure on me of care for all the churches. Who is weak, and I am not weak? Who is offended, and I do not burn? If I must boast, I will boast of the things that concern my weakness.

units.la: Dixit supra: Quandoquidem multi gloriantur secundum carne, gloriabor & ego. Ia gloriaturus dicit se quoq; audere in quocunq; quisquá alius audeat. In Graeco est, ἐν ῳ ἂν τις τολμᾷ, i. Sed in quo quis audet, per insipientia dico, audeo & ego. Q. d. uidetur pseudapostoli esse inter uos magni ac praestantes, quod in seruitutem uos adigunt, quod exedunt, quod accipiunt, quod attollunt se, & quod in faciem uos caedunt, ita ut illis comparatus admodum uideat esse infirmus, qui nihil horum inter uos fecerim. Sane sunt uiri audentes, dum haec faciunt. Verum in his situ est argumentum magnorum Apostolorum, in quo quis illorum audet, quanquam insipienter hoc dico, audeo & ego. Non enim minus sum q ipsi ad audendum instructus. Illud: p insipientia loquor, ad hoc inseruit, ut significet se eiusmodi audaciam non probare, sed magis insipientiae damnare, nec se fuisse quicquam tale dicturum, nisi praeter animi sententiam adactus insipientiae pseudapostolorum occurrere statuisset.
units.tr: He said above: "Since many glory after the flesh, I too will glory" (2 Cor. 11:18). Now, about to boast, he says that he too dares in whatever matter anyone else dares. The Greek is ἐν ῳ ἂν τις τολμᾷ [in whatever anyone dares], that is: "But in whatever anyone dares, I speak foolishly, I dare too." As if to say: the false apostles seem to be great and outstanding among you because they enslave you, devour you, take from you, exalt themselves, and strike you in the face. So compared with them I seem very weak, since I have done none of these things among you. Certainly they are bold men when they do these things. But the true mark of great apostles lies in these things, and in whatever of these any of them dares, I (though I say this foolishly) dare too. For I am no less equipped for daring than they are. The phrase "I speak as one beside himself" is inserted to show that he does not approve such boldness, but rather condemns it as folly. He would never have said anything of this kind, had he not, against his own inclination, resolved to meet the folly of the false apostles.

units.la: HEBRAEI sunt? sum & ego, inquit.) Singularis praerogatiua solet homines reddere audentiores & elatiores. Pseudapost. autem habebant carnis suae nobilitatem, quod essent Ebraei, Israelitae, & semen Abrahae, pro singulari praerogatiua, & huius nomine admodum inflati, sic audebant inter Graecos, ut quosuis fideles in seruitutem adigerent, & contumeliosius tractarent. Eam illis audaciam & gloriam deprecaturus, dicit: An ob id tantopere insolescunt, qd sunt Ebraei? At Ebraeus sum & ego. Quod sunt Israelitae? Israelita sum & ego. Quod sunt semen Abrahae? Et ego sum semen Abrahae. Nihil ergo hoc nomine habent, quo me excellant, neq; inferior illis sum, quo minus & ipse gloriari posim in carne, si in carne gloriādum & audendum esset Apostolo Christi. Confimi li modo occurrit illis, & Phil.3. dicens: Cauete canes, cauete malos operarios, cauete concisionem. Nos enim sumus circumcisio, qui spiritu Deum colimus, & gloriamur in Christo Iesu, ac non confidimus in carne, quamuis & ego in carne quoq; cōfidere posim. Si quis quam alius uidetur cōfidere in carne, ego magis, circumcisus octauo die, Israel ex genere, tribus Beniamin, Ebraeus ex Ebraeis, iuxta legem Pharisaeus, iuxta studium persequens ecclesiam, iuxta iusticiam quae est ex lege, factus irreprehensibilis, &c.
units.tr: "Are they Hebrews? I am too," he says. A singular privilege tends to make men bolder and more arrogant. The false apostles, however, boasted in the nobility of their flesh, that they were Hebrews, Israelites and the seed of Abraham. Puffed up by this as a singular privilege, they dared among the Greeks to enslave any of the faithful and to treat them more insolently. Wishing to curb this boldness and boasting, he says: Do they grow so proud because they are Hebrews? I am a Hebrew too. Because they are Israelites? I am an Israelite too. Because they are the seed of Abraham? I too am the seed of Abraham. So they have nothing in this name by which they excel me, nor am I inferior to them, so that I could not also boast in the flesh, if an apostle of Christ ought to glory and dare in the flesh. He meets them in a similar way in Philippians 3: "Beware of dogs, beware of evil workers, beware of the concision. For we are the circumcision, who worship God in the Spirit and glory in Christ Jesus, and do not trust in the flesh; although I too might trust in the flesh. If anyone seems to trust in the flesh more than others, I more: circumcised on the eighth day, of the stock of Israel, of the tribe of Benjamin, a Hebrew of Hebrews; as touching the law a Pharisee; as touching zeal persecuting the church; as touching the righteousness which is in the law, blameless," and so on.

units.la: HEBRÆI sunt, inquit, sum & ego.) De Heber, unde dicti sunt Ebraei, uide in Commentarijs nostris super Genesim, cap. 10. Israelitae sunt? sum & ego.) A Iacobo nepote Abrahae, qui ab angelo Israelis nomen accepit, uocati sunt Israelitae, qui ab illo prodierunt.
units.tr: "They are Hebrews," he says, "I am too." On Heber, from whom the Hebrews are named, see our commentaries on Genesis, chapter 10. "Are they Israelites? I am too." Those who descended from Jacob, the grandson of Abraham, who received the name Israel from the angel, were called Israelites.

units.la: SEMEN Abrahae sunt? sum & ego.) Quasi non sufficeret ad carnis gloriam, Ebreum dici & Israelitam, propter eximiam Abrahae praerogatiuam, & benedictione feminis illi promissam, gloriabantur esse se semē Abrahae. Semen Abrahae Christus est, in quo benedicūtur omnes gentes. Ad semen Abrahae pertinent nō omnes qui ex carne illius, sed qui ex Isaaco electionis filio per Iacob descenderunt. Ideo impēsius se Israelitas, & sic Abrahae semen esse iactabāt, unde prodijt Christus. Speciosa erat illorum gloriatio propter carnem Christi, uerum in cognatione carnis Christi innumeri erāt alieni a spiritu Christi. Et Christus ipse cognatione carnis suę nō agnoscere se, Matth.12. satis disertè testatur, dicēs: Quis est mater mea? Et qui sunt fratres mei? Qui facit uoluntatem patris mei, mater mihi est, frater & soror.
units.tr: "Are they the seed of Abraham? I am too." As if being called Hebrew and Israelite were not enough for the glory of the flesh, they boasted that they were the seed of Abraham, because of Abraham's outstanding privilege and the blessing promised to his seed. Christ is the seed of Abraham, in whom all nations are blessed. Not all who are of his flesh belong to the seed of Abraham, but those who descended through Jacob from Isaac, the son of promise. So they boasted all the more that they were Israelites, and thus the seed of Abraham, from whom Christ came. Their boast was splendid because of the flesh of Christ, but in kinship of the flesh to Christ countless people were strangers to the Spirit of Christ. Christ himself clearly testifies that he does not acknowledge them by fleshly kinship, in Matthew 12, saying: "Who is my mother? And who are my brothers? Whoever does the will of my Father is my mother, brother and sister to me."

units.la: Peculiare hoc est Iudaeis omnibus, ut se glorientur esse filios Abrahae, inquit ea carnis praerogatiua, qua de & Ismaelitae, & Idumaei, perinde atque ipsi gloriari possunt, admodum elati, reliquas nationes omnes contemnunt, & nimis securi impiè ac pessimè uiuunt. Eam gloriationem reprehendit in illis & Ioannes Baptista Matth.3. & Christus, Ioan.8. Apostolus hic cum negare posset esse eos uerum Abrahę semen, & ueros Israelitas: per concessionem tamē sic gloriā hanc extenuat, ut nihil illis relinquat, in quo se excellat. Sic objcit illud, & ego, non ut in carne, perinde atque ipsi glorietur, sed ut typhum eorum, & insolentiam nihil habere rationis admoneat, quod aduersum se iactare posint.
units.tr: This is peculiar to all Jews: they glory that they are the sons of Abraham. By this fleshly privilege, the Ishmaelites and Idumaeans could likewise boast, and being very proud, despise all other nations and live impiously and most wickedly, too secure. John the Baptist reproved this boasting in them (Matt. 3), and Christ too (John 8). The Apostle here, though he could deny that they are the true seed of Abraham and true Israelites, nevertheless by granting it diminishes this boast so that nothing remains for them in which they can excel. So he adds "I am too," not as if he were glorying in the flesh in the same way as they, but to warn that their arrogance and insolence have no reasonable ground for boasting against him.

units.la: MINISTRI Christi sunt? desipiens loquor excellentius sum ego.) Quia non solū de carnali praerogatiua, sed & de ministerio Christi gloriabantur, iactantes se ministros esse Christi, quo sub illius quoq; nomine dominarētur in ecclesijs, quemadmodū & Romanū Pontificem facere uidemus, qui ut sub nomine Christi dominium exerceat in fideles, uicarium se Christi constitutum esse contendit, etiā hane illis iactantiam infringit Apostolus, dicēs: Ministri Christi sunt? desipiens loquor, plus ego. Non dicit eos esse ministros Christi, quemadmodū nec Israelitas, & semen Abrahae, sed per interrogationis figurā, Ministri Christi sunt? inquit. Quasi dicat: Quemadmodum gloriantur. Esto sint ministri Christi. Ideo ne cōtra me insurgunt, & uobis dominātur, quasi minister Christi nō sim & ego? Cū sim excellentius minister Christi, quàm ipsi, mihiq;, si hinc gloriari liceret, gloriādum magis sit, quàm ipsis. Poterat negare ministros eos esse Christi. Verum ne contentiosius agere uideretur, concesit quidem eos esse Christi ministros, uerū simul excellentiam sibi ministerij huius uindicauit, quo causam illis insolescendi adimeret.
units.tr: Are they ministers of Christ? I speak as a fool: I am more excellent. Because they boasted not only of their carnal privilege but also of the ministry of Christ, calling themselves ministers of Christ so that under that name they might lord it over the churches, just as we see the Roman Pontiff do, who claims to have been appointed Christ's vicar so that he may exercise dominion over the faithful under the name of Christ, the Apostle also breaks this boast, saying: "Are they ministers of Christ? I speak as a fool: I am more." He does not say that they are ministers of Christ, any more than that they are Israelites and the seed of Abraham. Rather, by the figure of a question he says, "Are they ministers of Christ?" As if to say: "Let them boast as they do. Suppose they are ministers of Christ. Do they therefore rise up against me and lord it over you, as if I were not also a minister of Christ? Since I am a more excellent minister of Christ than they are, if it were permitted to boast in this, I ought to boast more than they do." He could have denied that they were ministers of Christ. But lest he seem to be contending too contentiously, he granted that they were ministers of Christ, yet at the same time claimed for himself the excellence of this ministry, so as to take away from them the occasion of their arrogance.

units.la: IN laboribus copiosius, inquit.) Quod dixit, excellentius se ministrū esse Christi, ne temere dixisse uideatur, probat illud per argumentum euidens ac manifestū, per omnis uidelicet generis, labores & pericula, quae propter Christū multa ac grauia ferebat, quorum nonnulla recensēt: utpote, labores, uerbera, carceres, mortes, lapidationes, naufragia, & uaria pericula. Dicet quisquā. Ergo ne quo quis plu ribus molestijs ac periculis inuoluitur, hoc est excellētius Christi minister? Si pericula Christi ministrum arguūt, pro ministris Christi habendi erunt quām plurimi haeretici, qui & ipsi haud modicis sese periculis propter sua dogmata obnoxios reddiderunt.
units.tr: "In labours more abundantly," he says. Because he said that he was a more excellent minister of Christ, lest he seem to have said it rashly, he proves it by a clear and manifest argument: namely, by labours and dangers of every kind, which he bore for Christ, many and grievous, some of which he lists: labours, stripes, imprisonments, deaths, stonings, shipwrecks, and various perils. Someone will say: "So does anyone who is involved in more troubles and dangers for this reason become a more excellent minister of Christ? If dangers prove someone to be a minister of Christ, then very many heretics must be regarded as ministers of Christ, for they too have exposed themselves to no small dangers on account of their doctrines."

units.la: Respondeo. Vt martyrem Christi facit, non passio, sed causa passionis, ita & Christi ministrū, non simpliciter pericula, sed pericula propter Euangelium Christi fideliter, ac iusto zelo praedicatum illata arguūt, & commendant. Excellentiam non dignitatis, ac praelaturę, sed ministerij uindicat sibi Apostolus, illiusq; argumētum proponit in multitudine laborum, ac periculorū. Est enim hęc sors Euāgelij serio & fideliter praedicati in hoc mundo, ut obnoxium reddat Christi ministrum, omnis generis laboribus, afflictionib. & periculis, ut quo quis maiore zelo Christum ubique praedicat, hoc pluribus & grauioribus periculis inuoluatur, & hoc argumento excellens in ministerio Christi comprobetur. Tribuit & Pontifex Romanus sibijpse illud ὑπερεχω.i. excellentius ego, caeteris uidelicet omnibus, uerum quod sequitur, in laboribus copiosius, &c. tribuere sibi non poterit. Otiosus, delicatus, ac propudiosissimus, uindicat sibi priuatum in ecclesijs omnibus, ex praerogatiua Petri, ex Principum Romanorum constitutionibus, ex primis sessionibus in concilijs, & consimilibus alijs nugis: quia non quaerit ministerij, sed dignitatis & honorum supereminentiam.
units.tr: I answer: just as it is not the suffering but the cause of the suffering that makes a martyr of Christ, so too it is not dangers simply, but dangers incurred for the sake of the Gospel of Christ, faithfully and with due zeal preached, that prove and commend a minister of Christ. The Apostle claims for himself excellence not of dignity and preeminence, but of ministry, and he sets out the proof of it in the multitude of labours and dangers. For this is the lot of the Gospel, when it is preached seriously and faithfully in this world: it makes the minister of Christ liable to every kind of labour, affliction and danger, so that the more zealously someone preaches Christ everywhere, the more he is involved in many and grievous dangers, and by this argument he is proved to be excellent in the ministry of Christ. The Roman Pontiff also claims for himself the word hyperecho [ὑπερέχω], that is, "I excel", above all others, of course; but what follows, "in labours more abundantly," etc., he will not be able to claim for himself. Idle, delicate and most shameless, he claims for himself a primacy over all the churches, from the privilege of Peter, from the constitutions of the Roman princes, from the first seats in councils, and from other similar trifles, because he seeks not the excellence of the ministry but the preeminence of dignity and honours.

units.la: IN laboribus copiosius, inquit.) In Graeco est ἐν κόποις, qd' idem est atq; in molestijs. Potest tamen intelligi, tam de laboribus praedicandi, in quibus multum molestiarum pertulit, quā de afflictionibus. De laborib. Euāgelizandi exposuimus, supra cap.6. ubi dicit, in laboribus, borib.in vigilijs,in ieiunijs,&c.quèadmodum & cap.10.vbi non in immensum gloriantes su per alienis laborib.De molestijs loquitur cum Gal.6.dicit, Τλοιπὸς κόπως μὴ μηδεὶς παρεχέτω.i. De cætero labores mihi nemo facessat.
units.tr: "In labours more abundantly," he says. In the Greek it is en kopois [ἐν κόποις], which is the same as "in troubles". It can, however, be understood both of the labours of preaching, in which he endured much trouble, and of afflictions. We have explained the labours of evangelising above, in chapter 6, where he says "in labours, in watchings, in fastings," etc., and likewise in chapter 10, where he speaks of not boasting beyond measure in the labours of others. He speaks of troubles in Galatians 6, where he says: To loipon kopous moi mēdeis parechetō [Τὸ λοιπὸν κόπους μοι μηδεὶς παρεχέτω], that is, "Let no one cause me trouble from now on."

units.la: IN verberibus supra modū,inquit.) Quod hic in genere dicit,dicturus est paulo post per speciem.
units.tr: "In stripes above measure," he says. What he says here in general, he will say shortly afterwards in particular.

units.la: IN carcerib.abundatius.) Meminit verbe-rum & carcerū suprà quoq; ca. 6. Obserua hic insigne metamorphosim. Qui priusquá cóuerteretur ad Christū,viros ac mulieres in Chri-stū credentes carceribus incluserat, post con-uersione & ipse carcerib.propter Christum in cluditur,perferens afflictiones quas alijs intu-lerat.Nemo igitur de persequutoribus Euan-gelij Christi desperet,sed ,p cóuersione potius illorum ad dominum orent omnes.
units.tr: "In imprisonments more abundantly." He mentioned stripes and imprisonments above also, in chapter 6. Observe here a remarkable metamorphosis. He who, before he was converted to Christ, had shut up men and women believing in Christ in prisons, after his conversion was himself shut up in prisons for Christ's sake, suffering the afflictions he had inflicted on others. Therefore let no one despair of the persecutors of the Gospel of Christ, but let all pray rather for their conversion to the Lord.

units.la: IN mortib.frequéter,inquit.) Supra ca.4.di xit:Sæper enim nos qui viuimus,in morte tra-dimur propter Iesum.Quoniā discrimina qui-b9 vita ipsius frequenter obijciebatur non e-iusdē erát, sed uarij generis,non dixit in singu-lari,in morte,sed pluraliter,in mortib. Vide au tē quomodo paucis verbis quasi ordinem ea-rum est affiictionum complexus,quas propter Christū patiebatur.Primaerat molestia laborū deinde plagæ quas inferebant ipsi hostes Chri-sti,tertiò carceres quib.tanquā occidendus in cludebatur,& post carceres expectatio mor-tis.Et tamè ex his omnib.semper ereptusest à dno,donec tempus adesset,quo dominum san-guine suo sanctificaret.
units.tr: "In deaths frequently," he says. Above, in chapter 4, he said: "For we who live are always delivered to death for Jesus' sake." Since the dangers to which his life was frequently exposed were not of the same kind but of various kinds, he did not say in the singular "in death", but in the plural, "in deaths." Notice also how, in a few words, he has as it were embraced in order the afflictions which he suffered for Christ: first was the trouble of labours; then the blows which his enemies, the enemies of Christ, inflicted; thirdly, the prisons in which he was shut up as one to be killed; and after the prisons, the expectation of death. And yet from all these he was always rescued by the Lord, until the time came when he would sanctify the Lord with his own blood.

units.la: A' Iudæis,inquit,quinquies quadragenas plagas vna minus accepi.) Species eorū subij cit,quę paucis in genere dixit:Orditur autem à verberib.quibus cæsus fuit à Iudæis hostib9 infensissimis.Non est aūt præter rationem qd' Iudæorum mox initio ac nominatim memi-nit.Per obliquuum nanq; Iudaicam pseudapo-stolorum iactantiam ac gloriam perstrinxit, dum narrat quid ab ea sit gente perpessus.Qd' verò quadragenarium plagarum numerum at tinet,legimus Deut.25.ad hunc modum: Sin autem eum qui peccauit dignum viderint pla gis,prosternent eum,& coram se verberari fa-cient.Pro mensura peccati erit & plagarū mo-dus,sic tamen vt quadragenarium numerū nó excedant,ne fœde laceratus in oculis tuis obe at frater tuus.Itaq; cumApostolum Christi ver berarent Iudæi authoritatem legis huius præ-texebant,quasi secundum illâ dignus ,esset pla gis.Atqui nihil admittebat, quo lex ista in ipsū quadraret,quæ plagas decernit ידשי, id est, impio ,idq; secundum modum impietatis ipsi us. Deinde non decernit numerum quadra genarium hac conditione, vt minus quadra-ginta inferre non liceat,sed ne plures inferan-tur.Erat enim non ignota Deo populi huius immisericordia & nimia ad sanguinis effusio-nem propensio.Illi verò,quamuis nullam iu-stam verberandi illum causamhaberent,verbe-rarunt tamen eum pleno 40. plagarum numę-
units.tr: "Of the Jews," he says, "five times I received forty stripes less one." He sets out a species of those things which he mentioned in a few words in general. He begins with the stripes by which he was beaten by the Jews, his most hostile enemies. Nor is it beside the point that he mentions the Jews first and by name. For by indirection he struck at the Jewish boasting and glory of the false apostles, while he tells what he suffered from that nation. As for the number of forty stripes, we read in Deuteronomy 25 as follows: "But if they see that the one who has sinned is worthy of stripes, they shall cast him down and cause him to be beaten before them. The manner of the stripes shall be according to the measure of the sin, yet so that they do not exceed the number forty, lest your brother be shamefully torn in your sight." Therefore, when the Jews were beating the Apostle of Christ, they pretended the authority of this law, as if he were worthy of stripes according to it. Yet nothing in it applied to him, since this law decrees stripes for the rasha [רשע], that is, the impious, and that according to the measure of his own impiety. Then, it does not decree the number forty on the condition that it is not lawful to inflict fewer than forty, but that not more be inflicted. For the mercilessness of this people and their excessive proneness to shedding blood were not unknown to God. But they, although they had no just cause for beating him, nevertheless beat him with the full number of forty stripes, one only being taken away,

units.la: ro, vna tantum dempta, quod plures interre partim lege partim maiorum constitutione p hiberentur,qua in re satis declarabát, quosq; verberando progressuri essent, nisi cancellis numeri huius cohiberentur. Scio quid adfe-rat hic Burgensis, uerùm illius sententia cū di cta lege non concordat.
units.tr: because the law, partly by its own terms and partly by the constitution of their ancestors, forbade more to be inflicted. In this matter it sufficiently showed how far they would have gone in beating him, had they not been restrained within the bounds of this number. I know what the Burgensis brings forward here, but his opinion does not agree with the said law.

units.la: Vbi autem & quibus circumstantijs plagas istas quinquies illatas perpessus sit, nusquam, quod ego sciam,certò traditur. Et tamen non est vt de illis dubitemus,quandoquidem acce pisse se,id est, perpessum esse illas tam diserte testatur.
units.tr: Where and in what circumstances he suffered these stripes, inflicted five times, is nowhere, so far as I know, certainly recorded. Yet there is no reason for us to doubt them, since he testifies so clearly that he received them, that is, suffered them.

units.la: TER virgis cæsus fui,inquit.) Semel tantū virgis cæsum illū fuisse legimus Act.16. Secun do ac tertio factum hoc esse, non constat nisi ex hisce ipsius verbis.Poterit aūt quęri,quales fuerint quadragenarię illæ plagæ quas à Iudæ is se quinquies accepisse dixit, an non & ipsæ virgis fuerint illatæ?Si virgis,quorsum hic se-orsum ter se virgis cæsum fuisse dicat.Verùm si rectè distinguantur hæ plagæ, hactenus aliæ fuerunt atq; aliæ,qd' illas à Iudæis,istas à Gen tib.inflictas pertulit,quam distinctionem po-nit & Ambrosius.
units.tr: "Three times I was beaten with rods," he says. We read that he was beaten with rods only once, in Acts 16. That it happened a second and a third time is not known except from these very words of his. But it may be asked what kind of forty stripes those were which he said he had received five times from the Jews. Were they not also inflicted with rods? If with rods, why does he here say separately that he was beaten with rods three times? Yet if these stripes are rightly distinguished, the one set was different from the other, in that he suffered the former at the hands of Jews and the latter at the hands of Gentiles. Ambrose also makes this distinction.

units.la: Obseruet hic lector,quæ fuerit moderatio apud Iudæos & Gètes,in castigadis illis quos ipsi pro hereticis habebant.A'Iudeis Aposto-lus quinquies quadragenas plagas vna minus accepit, & ab ethnicis ter virgis cæsus fuit , & post verbera dimissus. Sic dimissum fuisse,vt recantaret, nec legimus, nec factum esse vllo modo credimus.Dimissus ergo fuit absq; recá tatione.Si hodie in viuis existens in manus Pa pistarum incideret,nisi reuocaret ea quæ do-cuit,ne virgis quidem cæsus dimitteretur, sed prorsus neci daretur.
units.tr: Let the reader observe here what moderation there was among the Jews and the Gentiles in chastising those whom they regarded as heretics. From the Jews the Apostle received five times forty stripes less one, and from the heathen he was beaten three times with rods, and afterwards released after the blows. That he was released on condition that he recant, we neither read nor believe in any way to have happened. He was therefore released without any recantation. If he were alive today and fell into the hands of the Papists, unless he recanted what he had taught, he would not even be released after being beaten with rods, but would be given over entirely to death.

units.la: SEMEL fui lapidatus,inquit.) Factum hoc fuerat Lystris,quo de Act.14.legimus ad hunc modū.Superuenerūt aūt quidà ab Antiochia & Iconio Iudæi,qui cum persuasissent turbis, ac Paulū lapidassent,extraxerūt eū è ciuitate, mortuum esse existimantes. Circundantib.au tem eū discipulis,surrexit & intrauit ciuitaté, ac postero die profectus est cū Barnaba Der-ben. Videmus hic quoq; moderatiores fuisse in lapidatione Pauli tam Iudæos quàm Gen-tes,in eo qd' non sequierunt in mortuū, sicuti putabant,sed vbi mortuum esse existimabant, reliquerunt eū,ac discesserunt.At hodie tanta est in pseudochristianis crudelitas, vt non sint occidisse contenti,nisi crudelissimis cruciatib. quos è medio sublatos volūt sic occidāt, vt de cies occisi videri possint.
units.tr: "Once I was stoned," he says. This happened at Lystra, of which we read in Acts 14 in this way: "And there came thither certain Jews from Antioch and Iconium, who persuaded the people, and, having stoned Paul, drew him out of the city, supposing he had been dead. Howbeit, as the disciples stood round about him, he rose up and came into the city, and the next day he departed with Barnabas to Derbe." Here we see that both Jews and Gentiles were more moderate in stoning Paul, in that they did not pursue him once he was dead, as they supposed, but when they thought he was dead they left him and went away. Today, however, there is such cruelty among the pseudo-Christians that they are not content to kill, unless with the most cruel torments, and those whom they remove from the midst they kill in such a way that they might seem to have been killed ten times over.

units.la: TER naufragiū feci,inquit.) Semel naufra-giū perpessum legimus Act.27.quâ historiâ le-ctor ipse suo loco inspiciat. Vbi preterea nau-fragium fecerit non legimus.
